duplicates.note: Constructs the automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite étale covers with its equivalence to finite continuous sets, recovering the absolute Galois group for Spec K: the general form of 0D's equivalence.

targets.target: Effective faithfully flat descent, with cocycle and uniqueness, for affine schemes
targets.note: Mathlib proves that extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic, the Amitsur equalizer A = eq(B ⇉ B ⊗_A B), and the general IsStack formalism. Its own docstring leaves effective descent for modules as a TODO, and no stack instance for affine schemes or algebras exists.

targets.target: Descent of sections and morphisms along fpqc and fppf covers
targets.note: Mathlib proves that the fpqc and fppf topologies are subcanonical, and that quasi-compact flat surjections and fppf surjections are effective epimorphisms. So morphisms and sections that agree on overlaps descend uniquely. The four instances are unnamed in the source; their generated names were confirmed with Lean.

targets.target: Effective descent for finite locally free schemes, closed subschemes, finite locally free subgroup schemes and Cartier-divisor equalities
targets.note: Mathlib descends properties of morphisms (isomorphism, open immersion, universally closed and open), not objects. No effective descent of schemes or subschemes exists.

targets.target: Effective descent of projective relative curves equipped with a compatibly descended relatively ample line bundle
targets.note: Neither library defines relative ampleness or polarised descent.

targets.target: Descent of group objects, homomorphisms, the group law and its axioms, level structures, finite group actions and torsors
targets.note: Once the scheme has descended, the group law descends by descent of morphisms (above) and its axioms by faithfulness of pullback along fpqc covers, which Mathlib proves. Tau Ceti describes the points of an affine group by faithfully flat descent. Level structures, actions and torsors have no descent statement.

targets.target: Spreading out: finite-presentation models for a polarised curve with section, group law, subgroup and level data; morphisms and equalities descend to a common finite stage
targets.note: For a cofiltered limit of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps, Mathlib shows that morphisms to a locally finitely presented target factor through a finite stage, and that two morphisms agreeing on the limit agree at a finite stage. Missing: descending the objects themselves (curve, polarisation, group law, subgroup, level data) to a finite stage.

targets.target: The agreement locus of two finitely presented morphisms is representable and contains the original base after enlargement
targets.note: Equalizers of scheme morphisms exist, and into a separated target the equalizer is a closed immersion; agreement on the limit propagates to a finite stage. The combined statement is not formulated.

targets.target: The universal quotient's relative spectrum is a finite locally free rank-N subgroup scheme of G, compatible with base change; the parameter scheme is projective and finitely presented, and need not be finite
targets.note: No parameter space for subgroup schemes exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Constructs Grassmannians with their quotient universal properties and base change, and proves that invariant-subbundle equations are closed. That covers 0G's Grassmannian and closed-loci steps.

targets.target: The projective cubic of W : WeierstrassCurve R as a closed subscheme of ℙ²_R, with structure morphism and zero section [0:1:0]
targets.note: Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Projective is the equation in homogeneous coordinates, with point classes over a field. Neither library builds a scheme from a Weierstrass equation (the roadmap cites mathlib4#25983 for the affine model) or has ℙ²_R as a named scheme.

targets.target: Properness of the projective model
targets.note: Mathlib proves Proj 𝒜 ⟶ Spec 𝒜₀ proper when 𝒜 is of finite type over 𝒜₀ (an instance, name confirmed with Lean). Applied to R[X,Y,Z]/(F) this would give properness, but the model is not constructed.

targets.target: Smoothness of relative dimension one when W.IsElliptic
targets.note: Only algebraic stand-ins exist: on an elliptic curve over a nontrivial ring every solution is nonsingular (Mathlib), and over a field the affine coordinate ring is integrally closed (Tau Ceti). No smoothness statement for a scheme exists.

targets.target: Compatibility of the model with base change and with VariableChange
targets.note: Equation level only: variable changes act on Weierstrass curves over any commutative ring, compatibly with ring maps. The scheme-level compatibilities are missing along with the model.

targets.target: EllipticCurveGeom S: smooth proper π : E ⟶ S of relative dimension one with a section, Zariski-locally pointed-isomorphic to a projective Weierstrass model; base change and its functoriality
targets.note: No elliptic curve over a base scheme exists in either library. The closest carrier is Tau Ceti's AbelianVariety K, a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field, with no Weierstrass atlas and no non-field base.

duplicates.note: Constructs, over a field, the smooth projective scheme of an elliptic Weierstrass equation with its section at infinity, and proves smoothness and properness: the field case of 1A.
Identifies one-dimensional abelian schemes with this roadmap's elliptic curves via the Weierstrass-presentation theorem, so it shares the EllipticCurveGeom S carrier.
Its proper flat families with smooth elliptic or polygonal fibres restrict on the smooth locus to 1A's EllipticCurveGeom S, and it names that compatibility as a milestone.

targets.target: Over a field with W elliptic, sections of projModel W ⟶ Spec K correspond to W.toAffine.Point, the zero section to infinity
targets.note: The affine-chart half is in Tau Ceti: for any R-algebra A, solutions of the base-changed equation give R-algebra maps from the coordinate ring (evalAlgHom), and conversely. Mathlib identifies projective and affine point classes over a field, and Tau Ceti identifies points with degree-one places. The projective model and the section at infinity are missing.

targets.target: Over a local ring, points as unimodular homogeneous triples; over a ring with trivial Picard group, the same after trivialising the line bundle
targets.note: Mathlib's projective point classes are defined only over fields, and there is no functor-of-points description of projective space over a ring.

targets.target: Over an arbitrary base T, T-points as a line bundle with three generating sections satisfying the cubic, up to isomorphism, proved by Zariski descent
targets.note: Mathlib has no functor of points of ℙⁿ, contrary to the layer's stated dependency. It has maps to Proj from generating global sections and the functor of points of affine space.

duplicates.note: Compares scheme-valued F-points of the elliptic Weierstrass scheme and their group law with the existing Weierstrass point group: item 1 of 1B.

targets.target: The Weierstrass variable-change group x = u²x′ + r, y = u³y′ + su²x′ + t: multiplication, inverse, action on the five coefficients, and the transformation law of the equation
targets.note: Mathlib has the group, its action on Weierstrass curves over any commutative ring and the coefficient formulas. Tau Ceti proves the transformation law of the equation over any ring, and over a field the induced isomorphism of point groups.

targets.target: Action of a variable change on x, y and on the invariant differential
targets.note: Tau Ceti's invariant differential lives in the Kähler differentials of the function field, and no variable-change transformation law for it is stated.

targets.target: The relative effective Cartier divisor [0], its multiples, and the line bundles ℒ_n = 𝒪_E(n[0])
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs 𝒪_X(D) for a Weil divisor on a noetherian integral scheme of dimension at most one (an absolute curve), not for a divisor on a relative curve.

targets.target: For n > 0: R¹π_*ℒ_n = 0, π_*ℒ_n locally free of rank n, formation commuting with arbitrary base change
targets.note: The fibrewise count exists in function-field language: Riemann–Roch, and ℓ(nP) = n at a rational place of a genus-one function field. Tau Ceti also has absolute sheaf cohomology Hⁱ(X, M). Missing: the comparison with sheaf cohomology on a curve, higher direct images, local freeness of pushforwards, and cohomology and base change.

targets.target: Positive-degree theorem: for M invertible of constant positive fibre degree d, R¹π_*M = 0 and π_*M is locally free of rank d with base change; for d = 1 the evaluation section cuts out a unique section, compatibly with base change and fppf descent
targets.note: Only the function-field shadow exists: in genus one ℓ(D) = deg D for deg D > 0, and a degree-one divisor is linearly equivalent to exactly one place of degree one. The relative statements need the cohomology package of the Jacobian Challenge, which neither library has.

targets.target: Pole-filtration construction of a pointed Weierstrass equation Zariski-locally on the base, with unit discriminant; identification of the bases 1, x, y, x², xy, x³ and of the pole-order-six relation with the Weierstrass equation
targets.note: Not even the field case exists: Tau Ceti's own docstring names ℓ(nP) = n as the input for constructing Weierstrass coordinates, but no construction derives a Weierstrass equation from a genus-one function field.

targets.target: Classification: every pointed isomorphism of projective Weierstrass models over the same base is induced by a unique variable change, over an arbitrary base by descent
targets.note: Not proved even over a field. Tau Ceti's Aut.lean takes variable changes as the definition of isomorphism of Weierstrass curves, and its degree-one isogenies are not related to variable changes.

targets.target: Weierstrass-presentation theorem: a smooth proper relative genus-one curve with a section is Zariski-locally pointed-isomorphic to a projective Weierstrass model
targets.note: No relative curve theory exists in either library.

targets.target: Independence of the spreading-out model and of the finite exceptional set for G(A)
targets.note: Changing the finite exceptional set is available abstractly for restricted products, but there is no smooth affine model of an algebraic group over O_S and hence no statement that G(A) is independent of the model.

targets.target: The adelic points functor G ↦ G(A) with the diagonal G(F) → G(A) and local projections
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor` sends every commutative R-algebra A to the convolution group of A-points of the affine group scheme of a Hopf algebra, functorially in A. Evaluated on the adele ring it gives the abstract group G(𝔸), and `mapPoints` along K → 𝔸[K] gives the diagonal; the local projections still need 𝔸[K] → K_v packaged as algebra maps (only ring homomorphisms such as `evalRingHom` exist). For GL_n and G_m Tau Ceti identifies the points with GL_n(A) and Aˣ. Missing: any topology on G(𝔸), its identification with the restricted product of the G(F_v) with respect to G(O_v) for a model over O_S, and hence the adelic group itself. For G_a and G_m the adelic objects do exist concretely: the adele ring with its diagonal, and IdeleGroup = 𝔸ˣ, which `unitsEquiv` identifies with the restricted product of the local unit groups (as groups only).

targets.target: Base change and restriction-of-scalars equivalences on adelic points
targets.note: Base change on points is algebraically available: `baseChangePointsMulEquiv` identifies (A →ₐ[k] R) with (K ⊗ A →ₐ[K] R) as convolution groups for any K-algebra R. But there is no Weil restriction in either tree (`grep -rn -i 'weil restriction'` finds only prose), no map 𝔸_F → 𝔸_E or identification 𝔸_E ≅ E ⊗_F 𝔸_F, and no topology on adelic points, so neither Res_{E/F} G(𝔸_F) ≅ G(𝔸_E) nor the adelic base-change equivalence can be stated.

targets.target: Compatibility of adelic points with closed subgroups, centres and products
targets.note: On points all three compatibilities hold for every commutative value algebra, so for 𝔸 as abstract groups: points of a product are the product of the points (`pointsMulEquiv`, natural in the algebra), points of the closed subgroup cut out by a Hopf ideal are the points vanishing on it (`quotientPointsSubgroup`), and over a field the points of the centre (`centerDefiningIdeal`) are the universally central points (`centerPointsSubgroup_eq_center`). Missing: everything topological — that H(𝔸) → G(𝔸) is a closed embedding, that the product decomposition is a homeomorphism — since G(𝔸) carries no topology in either library.

targets.target: G(F) is a discrete subgroup of G(A) (and not of the finite adeles alone)
targets.note: Proved without sorry for the additive group: K is discrete and closed in 𝔸[K], and 𝔸[K]/K is T3. The layer's caveat is not a theorem anywhere: density of K in the finite adele ring appears only in the docstring of Tau Ceti's Discrete.lean (it is planned as `denseRange_algebraMap_finiteAdeleRing` in the GlobalNumberFields roadmap), and the cited `InfiniteAdeleRing.denseRange_algebraMap` is density in the infinite adele ring K∞, i.e. weak approximation at the archimedean places. Nothing for a general G.

targets.target: G(A) is unimodular for reductive G
targets.note: Mathlib defines the modular character of a locally compact group, so unimodularity is expressible (∆ ≡ 1), but there is no Haar measure on any adelic group and no such theorem.

targets.target: Vanishing of H_G on G(F) (product formula)

targets.target: Invariant quotient measures and Weil's integral formula, independent of the fundamental domain
targets.note: Two pieces are in Mathlib. For a countable subgroup acting with a fundamental domain: independence of the fundamental domain (`IsFundamentalDomain.measure_eq`), uniqueness of the quotient measure, Haar-ness of the quotient measure for a normal discrete subgroup, and the unfolding formula. For a closed normal subgroup (via `TopologicalGroup.IsSES.ofClosedSubgroup`), Haar/Extension.lean builds a Haar measure on the group from Haar measures on the subgroup and on the quotient and proves ∫_B f = ∫_C (∫_A f(b·a) da) dc for compactly supported continuous f — Weil's formula in the normal case. Missing: the invariant measure on H\G for a non-normal, non-discrete closed subgroup under the condition Δ_G|_H = Δ_H (needed for quotients such as Z(𝔸)G(F)\G(𝔸) or N(𝔸)\G(𝔸)), and the extension from compactly supported continuous functions to integrable ones.

States rapid decay on Siegel sets, which presupposes and partly restates the Siegel-set construction and height estimates of AA.3.
Proves compactness of the norm-one idele class group and recovers class-group finiteness from it: the GL₁ case of AA.3's finite volume of G(F)\G(A)¹ and finiteness of G(F)\G(A_f)/K.

targets.target: Weak approximation for algebraic groups, in the justified cases, with visible failure for tori
targets.note: Only field-level statements are proved: K is dense in every finite product of its completions (G_a), and a single element of Kˣ approximates targets at finitely many finite places while taking prescribed signs at the real places (the G_m form). Nothing for a general algebraic group, and no discussion of the failure of weak approximation for tori.

targets.target: Strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple G outside S with a noncompact local factor
targets.note: The one algebraic-group case is SL₂ over ℚ with S = {∞}, in congruence form: Tau Ceti proves SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/dℤ) surjective for every d, jointly at two coprime moduli, which is equivalent to density of SL₂(ℤ) in SL₂(ℤ̂). It is not stated adelically, and nothing covers other simply connected groups or other number fields; even additive strong approximation for a number field (density of K in the finite adeles) is unproved. Tau Ceti also proves strong approximation for the field of a function field. It has simply connected algebraic groups (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SimplyConnected), but no approximation theorem uses them.

targets.target: Finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels, and degrees via stabilizer indices
targets.note: The abstract ingredients exist: for H ≤ G acting on E with E → E/G a quotient covering map, E/H → E/G is a covering map (`isCoveringMap_of_comp`), and the degree of a double coset H₁gH₂ is the index [H₁ : H₁ ∩ gH₂g⁻¹] (`degree_eq_relIndex`). No neatness predicate exists in either library — the word occurs only in three informal comments — and there are no adelic level quotients G(F)\G(𝔸)/K whose covering degrees could be computed.

targets.target: Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences on adelic quotients
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a classical Hecke ring for GL_2 and GL_n double cosets (TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/), but no adelic double-coset correspondence with Cartesian squares of level covers.

targets.target: Quotient groupoids and stabilizers in the non-neat case
targets.note: No algebraic-stack quotient of an adelic double-coset space exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Proves existence of neat congruence subgroups and uses strong approximation in the same restricted form, so the neatness and approximation targets overlap.
Owns additive strong approximation and the idele group; AA.4's approximation targets are the algebraic-group generalization of that layer.

targets.target: Identification of the GL_1 adelic quotient with the idele class group, and the split-centre normalization with the norm-one subgroup
targets.note: The idele class group 𝔸ˣ/Kˣ is defined in Mathlib (as an abbrev, with no structure theory), and the product formula shows the principal ideles have norm one; but the norm-one idele subgroup 𝔸^1, its compactness modulo Kˣ, and the comparison with the GL_1 case of a general adelic quotient are all missing.

targets.target: Identification of the GL_2/Q component with the upper half-plane
targets.note: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have the upper half-plane with its SL(2,R) action and modular curves at level Γ(N), but no adelic GL_2(A) description and hence no comparison.

targets.target: Compactness of the quotient for a definite quaternion inner form
targets.note: Quaternion algebras exist in Mathlib (Mathlib/Algebra/Quaternion.lean) but there is no adelic group of a quaternion algebra and no compactness statement.

targets.target: Comparison of volumes under finite-index level changes
targets.note: Mathlib has both shapes of the wanted statement: [G:H]·μ(H) = μ(G) for a measurable finite-index subgroup and a left-invariant measure (`Subgroup.index_mul_measure`, the local identity vol(K) = [K:K']·vol(K')), and the covolume/index relation for ℤ-lattices in a real vector space. There is no measure on an adelic group and hence no volume of an adelic quotient to compare.

duplicates.note: Owns level structures and the quotient identification that AA.5 imports for the GL_2/Q comparison.
Its connected-component decomposition is the same identification of an adelic double-coset quotient with a classical arithmetic quotient.

Defines the idele norm, the closed norm-one subgroup IdeleClassGroup.normOne and proves its compactness, recording that the full idele class group is not compact: the GL_1 split-centre normalization AA.5 identifies.

targets.target: The Hodge bundle omega on a modular curve
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'hodge bundle'` over both trees returns nothing, and no modular curve exists as a scheme or stack in either library.

targets.target: Cusp ideal / cusp divisor on the compactified curve
targets.note: Only the analytic cusp is present (the cusp function of a periodic form, and `Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean` for the set of cusps); there is no cusp divisor on an algebraic curve.

targets.target: Geometric modular forms as sections of omega^k, and their base change along a ring map
targets.note: Mathlib's `ModularForm Γ k` is a complex-analytic function on the upper half-plane; there is no space of forms over a general base ring and hence nothing to base change.

targets.target: Agreement of geometric and analytic forms over C (GAGA comparison)
targets.note: `grep -rn -i gaga` over both trees returns nothing: there is no analytification functor or GAGA theorem in either library.

targets.target: Coefficient-field and integral q-expansion comparison via the moduli family
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the universal Weierstrass curve over Z[a_1,...,a_6] and its specialization property, which is the closest thing to a universal family, but it is not a family over a modular curve and carries no level structure.

targets.target: Descent for small levels from a rigidified cover or the moduli stack, with stabilisers visible
targets.note: No algebraic stack of elliptic curves and no level structures on a family exist in either library.

duplicates.note: Owns the Hodge bundle and the identification of weight-two cusp forms with regular differentials, which is the case k=2 of R15.1's construction and comparison.
Identifies the characteristic-zero Hodge bundle after extension to a splitting field and proves descent, the Hilbert analogue of R15.1.
Constructs the determinant of invariant differentials (the Hodge bundle) of an abelian scheme, the general case of the same bundle.
Owns projective coherent GAGA, the equivalence of coherent algebraic and analytic sheaves on a projective complex scheme, which is the GAGA step of R15.1's comparison of geometric and analytic forms.

targets.target: q-expansion principle: a form is detected by its q-expansions at the needed cusps
targets.note: Mathlib proves the analytic statement at the cusp at infinity: for Γ ≤ GL(2,R) with a strict period h > 0, f ↦ qExpansion h f is injective on ModularForm Γ k. This is one cusp, over C, for connected-type Γ; the geometric statement (a section of omega^k over a base ring vanishing iff its q-expansion vanishes) is absent.

targets.target: Integral version of the q-expansion principle
targets.note: No forms over a ring exist, so there is no integral q-expansion principle and no bounded-denominator statement.

targets.target: Finite generation and base change of spaces of forms
targets.note: Over ℂ only: Tau Ceti proves M_k(Γ) and S_k(Γ) finite-dimensional for any finite-index Γ ≤ SL(2,ℤ) (via the Sturm bound) and that E₄ and E₆ freely generate the graded ring of level-one forms (`mvPolynomialEquivModularForms`); Mathlib has the level-one dimension formula. Finite generation of modules of forms over a coefficient ring, and its compatibility with base change, do not exist.

targets.target: Hecke actions and the coefficient formulas for their q-expansions
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the full analytic Hecke theory for Γ_0(N) with nebentypus: T_n on q-expansions, the eigenvalue/coefficient identity a_n(f) = λ_n a_1(f), the old/new decomposition and multiplicity one. The layer wants the Hecke action defined from the algebraic correspondences of R14 and *compared* with this; the algebraic side does not exist.

targets.target: Algebraic integrality of Hecke eigenvalues and their reduction
targets.note: No statement that the eigenvalues of a normalised eigenform are algebraic integers, and no reduction of a q-expansion modulo a prime, appears in either library (`grep -i` for IsIntegral/𝓞 in the Tau Ceti ModularForms tree finds only unrelated uses).

targets.target: Separation of reduction of characteristic-zero forms from lifting a characteristic-p eigenform
targets.note: There are no characteristic-p modular forms at all, so neither direction is stated.

duplicates.note: Proves the formal comparison at the Tate curve 'used in the q-expansion principle', i.e. the geometric input to R15.2's first target.
Also asks for the q-expansion principle together with integral level structures and diamond operators, for the ordinary tower.
Owns the integral Hecke algebra, coefficient fields and the integral q-expansions-at-all-cusps lattice argument, which is exactly R15.2's integral Hecke theory.
Builds an integral q-expansion principle for Hilbert Eisenstein series; the same principle in a wider setting.

targets.target: The Hasse invariant with its q-expansion
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'hasse invariant'` and `hasseInvariant` over both trees return nothing: Mathlib's Hasse names are the Hasse derivative and the Hasse diagram, and the quadratic-form Hasse invariant exists only as a Tau Ceti roadmap target. There is also no supersingular/ordinary theory or [p]-series height; the inputs to E_{p−1} ≡ 1 (mod p) — the Eisenstein q-expansion coefficients and von Staudt–Clausen — are in Mathlib but the congruence is not stated.

targets.target: Frobenius and Verschiebung on forms in characteristic p
targets.note: Frobenius and Verschiebung exist for Witt vectors and (in Tau Ceti) Frobenius isogenies of elliptic curves in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Frobenius, but not as operators on mod-p modular forms.

targets.target: The theta operator with its q-expansion formula and Hecke compatibility
targets.note: Mathlib has the normalized derivative D = (2πi)⁻¹ d/dz of a complex modular form and the Serre derivative D − (k/12)E₂ as a map M_k(Γ) → M_{k+2}(Γ) for Γ ≤ SL(2,ℤ) (`serreDerivativeMF`), but no q-expansion formula a_n(Df) = n·a_n(f), no Hecke compatibility and nothing in characteristic p, where θ = q d/dq preserves mod-p forms.

targets.target: Filtration and weight-change results with exact hypotheses on p and level, including p = 2, 3
targets.note: No mod-p filtration of a modular form exists.

targets.target: The Igusa-curve interpretation
targets.note: `grep -rn -i igusa` over both trees returns nothing.

duplicates.note: Proves the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem 'with its characteristic-p operations', so it restates the theta/filtration package of R15.3.
Uses Hasse sections and the ample Hasse invariant on strata, the higher-dimensional version of R15.3's Hasse invariant.

targets.target: Serre's piecewise weight recipe k(rho-bar) as an exhaustive local case table
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'serre weight'` returns nothing in either tree; there is no residual Galois representation to feed the recipe.

targets.target: Tame inertia characters and the irreducible local-inertia case
targets.note: Mathlib has decomposition/inertia subgroups in Hilbert ramification theory and the p-adic cyclotomic character of a field with enough roots of unity, but no fundamental tame characters of level 1 and 2 and no local Galois representation theory.

targets.target: Reducible local representations: scalar and extension-sensitive cases, with the extension class stored
targets.note: Tau Ceti has continuous H¹ of the absolute Galois group of any field in low degree, and the Kummer map Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ ↪ H¹(G_K, μₙ) (`kummerClassMap_injective`; surjectivity via Hilbert 90 is not yet there), which for K = ℚ_p contains the classes Serre's peu/très ramifié condition is phrased in. Missing: the identification of H¹ with extensions of characters, two-dimensional local Galois representations, the peu ramifié notion and any storage of an extension class with the recipe.

targets.target: Twisting and determinant parity of the recipe
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Invariance of the weight under coefficient extension and isomorphism
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: For p = 2: weight 2 exactly in the finite-flat case, weight 4 otherwise
targets.note: The finite-flat condition on a local representation (ρ̄|G_{ℚ₂} prolongs to a finite flat group scheme over ℤ₂) cannot be stated: neither library attaches group schemes to Galois modules or has Raynaud or Fontaine–Laffaille theory. Tau Ceti does have finite locally free commutative affine group schemes over any commutative ring, with Cartier duality (`FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDuality`) and its base change — the carrier such a condition would use.

targets.target: The Deligne–Serre eigenvalue-lifting lemma for a finite Hecke algebra
targets.note: The commutative-algebra ingredients (minimal primes, going-down for flat algebras, DVR lifting) are in Mathlib, but the lemma itself — a mod-p eigensystem of a finite torsion-free O-algebra lifts to a characteristic-zero eigensystem after extending O — is nowhere stated, in either library.

targets.target: Application to the relevant modular-form modules
targets.note: Tau Ceti's Hecke algebra acts on complex spaces of cusp forms with multiplicity one, but there is no integral Hecke algebra acting on a lattice of forms and no mod-p eigensystem to lift.

targets.target: Passage from a mod-p eigensystem at controlled weight and level to a characteristic-zero normalised eigenform, with the possible weight change
targets.note: Absent; there are no characteristic-p eigenforms.

targets.target: Special low weights, including Katz weight one
targets.note: Absent.

Organizes Deligne–Serre Artin representations and weight-one modularity, overlapping the same lifting statement.

targets.target: Residual modularity: coefficient field, prime over p, eigenform and isomorphism with the residual semisimplification
targets.note: There is no Galois representation attached to an eigenform in either library, and no semisimplification of a representation over a finite field; `grep -i semisimplification` in the declaration index returns nothing.

targets.target: The classical weight-and-level target stated with N(rho-bar) and k(rho-bar)
targets.note: Neither invariant is defined.

targets.target: Elementary character/determinant congruence consequences of the local recipe
targets.note: The mod-p cyclotomic character is available as the reduction of Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter, but the congruence det rho-bar = chi^{k-1} eps is not stated.

targets.target: Finite-flat weight-two consequence
targets.note: Absent, as is finite-flat local theory.

duplicates.note: States exactly this package — a normalised characteristic-zero newform of level N(rho-bar) and weight k(rho-bar), a coefficient prime and an isomorphism with the residual representation, plus determinant compatibility and coefficient-field invariance.
Owns the actual optimisation of weight and level, for which R15.6 supplies the statement vocabulary; the two overlap in the definition of the classical target.

Defines reduction followed by semisimplification and proves its independence of the lattice by Brauer–Nesbitt: the residual semisimplification that R15.6's definition of residual modularity compares with.

targets.target: Cartan involutions of a real reductive group
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'cartan involution'` over both trees returns nothing; Mathlib's Cartan names are Cartan subalgebras and Cartan matrices of Lie algebras.

targets.target: Maximal compact subgroups K_infty
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'maximal compact'` returns nothing in either tree.

targets.target: The contractible symmetric space X = G(F_infty)/K_infty with its G(F_infty)-action
targets.note: Only the rank-one example is present: the upper half-plane with its SL(2,R)-action and its contractibility as a convex-like subset of C. There is no general symmetric space.

targets.target: Finite decomposition of X_K into arithmetic Gamma-components with explicit stabilizers and component maps
targets.note: This needs AA.3's adelic double-coset finiteness, which is also absent; no adelic locally symmetric space is defined.

targets.target: Proper discontinuity of the arithmetic action, and freeness at neat level
targets.note: Mathlib defines proper discontinuity, proves finiteness of stabilizers from it, passes it along finite relative index, and proves that every discrete subgroup of SL(2,ℝ) and every arithmetic subgroup of GL(2,ℝ) acts properly discontinuously on ℍ; Tau Ceti shows the free locus of such an action is open with a covering-map quotient. Absent: the statement for an arithmetic subgroup of a general G(F_∞) acting on its symmetric space, and freeness at neat level (there is no neatness predicate in either library; the word occurs only in informal comments).

targets.target: Orientation local system, covering the nonorientable case
targets.note: Tau Ceti has local coefficient systems — functors from the fundamental groupoid to modules, with constant systems, pullback, transport and monodromy (`TauCeti.LocalCoefficientSystem`) — but no orientation local system: Mathlib orients modules, not manifolds, and neither library has local orientation classes.

targets.target: The reductive-centre correction in the definition of the quotient
targets.note: Absent, as is the adelic quotient it corrects.

duplicates.note: Supplies the finiteness of G(F)\G(A_f)/K 'needed for locally symmetric components', i.e. the component-decomposition target of ALS.0.
Proves arithmeticity and commensurability of G(Q)_+ ∩ gKg^{-1}, neatness and proper discontinuity, and the connected-component decomposition — the same statements in the Hermitian case.
Owns the real reductive group interface including the maximal compact subgroup and Cartan decomposition that ALS.0 constructs the symmetric space from.

For a real reductive G with maximal compact K and Cartan involution θ, proves the Cartan decomposition K × 𝔭 ≅ G as a diffeomorphism (so G/K ≅ 𝔭 is contractible) and the Iwasawa and KAK decompositions: ALS.0's Cartan involutions, maximal compact subgroups and contractible symmetric space.

Defines a Cartan involution through the compact real form and builds the Hermitian symmetric domain structure on each component: the Cartan-involution and symmetric-space targets in the Hermitian case.
Constructs local orientation classes and the orientation local system of a manifold, the object ALS.0 retains to cover the nonorientable case.

targets.target: Local systems from discrete integral coefficient modules and from algebraic representations with stable lattices
targets.note: The carrier exists in Tau Ceti: `LocalCoefficientSystem R X` is a functor from the fundamental groupoid of X to R-modules, with constant systems, pullback, path transport and the monodromy functor to representations of π₁(X, x); covering spaces are classified by fundamental-groupoid actions (`CoveringSpace.monodromyEquivalence`). Missing: the inverse construction of a module-valued local system from a π₁-representation, local systems on X_K attached to Γ-modules or to lattices in algebraic representations, and any cohomology with local coefficients.

targets.target: Singular, cellular, compact-support and relative cochain complexes
targets.note: Mathlib has the singular chain complex as a functor with homotopy invariance and H_0, and relative CW complexes; Tau Ceti has relative singular homology of pairs and triples with their connecting maps. All of this is homology with constant coefficients: there is no cochain complex, no compact-support variant and no cellular chain complex.

targets.target: Comparison of singular/cellular cohomology with sheaf cohomology
targets.note: Sheaf cohomology on a site exists in Mathlib, but no comparison with singular or cellular theory is stated and singular *cohomology* is not defined.

targets.target: Bounded finite projective chain models over the coefficient ring at neat level, with base change
targets.note: Absent: neither neatness nor a finite CW model of an arithmetic quotient exists.

targets.target: Perfect coefficient complexes with a uniform amplitude
targets.note: Mathlib has derived categories of abelian categories but no notion of a perfect complex over a ring: the declaration index contains no name matching `perfectComplex`, and `IsPerfect` names are graph matchings and perfect groups.

targets.target: The universal-coefficient spectral sequence with its Tor terms
targets.note: Mathlib has Tor and the spectral-object machinery for building spectral sequences, but `grep -rn -i 'universal coefficient'` over both trees hits only unrelated 'universal coefficient matrix'/'universal coefficients' phrases in Tau Ceti's unipotent-group and division-polynomial files, and there is no Künneth theorem either.

duplicates.note: Builds cellular complexes on finite CW or Borel–Serre models and compares them with singular/étale cochains, restating ALS.1's finite chain models and comparison.
Constructs étale and Betti cohomology with algebraic local systems, the same coefficient construction for Hilbert modular varieties.
Imports finite-complex models and torsion-stabilizer descent from this roadmap, restating the finite-projective-model target.

Defines absolute and relative singular cochains with local coefficient systems, proves the universal-coefficient short exact sequence and the Ext spectral sequence over a general ring, and constructs cup and cap products: ALS.1's cochain complexes and universal-coefficient target for arbitrary spaces.
Defines cellular chains of a CW complex from Mathlib's skeleta and proves the natural cellular-to-singular comparison and finite-CW finiteness: ALS.1's cellular complexes and finite chain models.

targets.target: Rational parabolic boundary components from unipotent radicals, Levi symmetric spaces and split-torus corners
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the algebraic Levi decomposition of a dynamic parabolic, but no rational parabolic of an arithmetic group and no boundary component.

targets.target: Gluing by the parabolic incidence relation; manifold-with-corners structure at neat level
targets.note: Mathlib has manifolds with corners as a general framework (and Tau Ceti adds boundary/interior lemmas in TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Boundary), but the Borel–Serre corner construction is absent; `grep -rn -i 'borel.serre'` over both trees finds nothing.

targets.target: Compactness of the Borel–Serre quotient and the homotopy equivalence from the interior
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Boundary strata as nilmanifold fibrations over Levi arithmetic quotients, with monodromy
targets.note: Absent; there is no nilmanifold in either library.

targets.target: Finite stratification filtration and its spectral sequence with explicit differentials
targets.note: The abstract machinery for a filtration spectral sequence is in Mathlib; the stratification it would be applied to does not exist.

duplicates.note: Imports Borel–Serre compactification and finite-complex models from this layer, restating its outputs.
Imports 'Borel–Serre finiteness' from this roadmap for GL_2/F.
Builds toroidal compactifications and their refinements, the algebraic analogue of the corner construction, with the same Hecke-compatibility problem.

targets.target: The two finite-level maps through K ∩ gKg^{-1}, with pullback and trace on cochains
targets.note: The index set Γ₁/(Γ₁ ∩ gΓ₂g^{-1}) of the correspondence is in Tau Ceti's double-coset API, but there is no space X_K, hence no covering maps and no pullback/trace on cochains.

targets.target: Independence of the induced chain maps from the choice of coset representatives
targets.note: Representative-independence is proved at the level of double cosets in the Hecke ring, not for chain maps on a quotient space.

targets.target: Composition of correspondences via the double-coset algebra
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Hecke triple and the double-coset module; Tau Ceti proves that the convolution product is associative and unital, giving a Semiring/Ring instance on 𝕋 Δ H R, with structure constants and an anti-involution commutativity criterion, all sorry-free. This is exactly the abstract double-coset algebra ALS.3 composes in, but no action on a cohomology complex is constructed.

targets.target: Compatibility with cup products, compact support and boundary restriction
targets.note: There is no cup product on singular cohomology in either library and no compact-support or boundary theory.

targets.target: Lifting the relations to the derived category with coherence data
targets.note: The derived category exists abstractly; nothing about Hecke operators in it.

targets.target: Change-of-level and groupoid versions with stabilizer factors
targets.note: The combinatorics exists: degrees of double cosets (`LeftCosetModule.deg`), and for 𝒢 ≤ ℋ acting on a set the stabilizer-weighted count of coset translates landing in a 𝒢-orbit, which equals the ℋ-stabilizer (`card_fiber_orbitOfCosetTranslate_mul_cardStabilizerOnOrbit`). Absent: change-of-level maps on cochain complexes of arithmetic quotients and their groupoid version with these stabilizer factors.

Constructs the algebraic Hecke correspondences, degeneracy maps and diamond operators for modular curves — the GL_2 case of the same correspondences.
Proves naturality of cohomology for Hecke correspondences and changes of coefficient, overlapping ALS.3's coefficient-change statements.
Constructs transfer on chains for finite coverings with p_* ∘ transfer = d and the regular-cover formula: the trace half of ALS.3's pullback-and-trace correspondences.

targets.target: The triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_boundary → RΓ_c[1], functorial in level and coefficients
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the long exact sequence of a pair in singular homology, which is the shadow of this triangle for a compact pair, but there is no compact-support cohomology and no boundary of a Borel–Serre compactification.

The Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (a stated TODO in Mathlib's GroupCohomology/Basic.lean), transgression, and any application to a unipotent/Levi stratum are absent.

targets.target: Comparison of the Hecke action on the boundary with parabolic induction and Satake transforms, with modulus and Tate shifts
targets.note: `grep -rn -i satake` over both trees returns nothing, and there is no parabolic induction of smooth representations.

targets.target: Gluing across intersections, filtration convergence, compatibility with localization at a Hecke ideal
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Conditions for vanishing or a useful summand of the boundary after localization, by an eigenvalue argument

Missing: the Harish-Chandra isomorphism describing Z(U(g)) and when χ_λ = χ_μ, the complexified algebra for a real reductive group, and the decomposition of a (g,K)-module into generalized infinitesimal-character subspaces.

targets.target: The GL_2/Q dictionary with classical modular forms: slash actions, central character and normalized Hecke operators
targets.note: The classical side of the dictionary is fully present: Mathlib's slash action and ModularForm/CuspForm, Tau Ceti's Hecke operators with nebentypus (the central character), normalized eigenforms and coefficient formulas. The adelic side, and hence the dictionary itself, is absent.

targets.target: Algebraic modular forms on compact-at-infinity groups as functions on finite adelic double cosets valued in an algebraic representation
targets.note: Abstract double cosets and their Hecke algebra exist, but there is no finite adelic double-coset set for an algebraic group and no Gross-style algebraic modular form.

targets.target: Compatibility with restriction of scalars, products, central characters and inner forms
targets.note: Absent: there is no Weil restriction in either library (`grep -rn -i 'weil restriction'` finds nothing) and no inner form of a reductive group.

duplicates.note: Owns Hecke characters with their infinity types (HeckeCharacter.infinityType), which is AF.5's GL_1 dictionary input.
Identifies the GL_1 adelic quotient with the idele class construction and the GL_2/Q component with the upper half-plane — the same two validation comparisons.
Uses n=1 algebraic Hecke characters and n=2 classical modular forms as its acceptance examples, the same dictionaries.

Defines HeckeCharacter K as continuous characters of the idele class group, its local components and finite conductor, the real shift and unitary part, and the dictionary with ray class and Dirichlet characters: the conductor and unitary-twist half of AF.5's GL_1 dictionary.

targets.target: local Schwartz–Bruhat spaces: locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places, Schwartz functions at real and complex places
targets.note: `SchwartzMap` (𝓢(E,F) on a real normed space) covers the archimedean places ℝ and ℂ ≅ ℝ². Neither library packages locally constant compactly supported functions on a nonarchimedean local field as a space; searches for Schwartz–Bruhat/Bruhat–Schwartz and for `LocallyConstant` with `HasCompactSupport` found nothing.

targets.target: Fourier transform on local fields with respect to a nontrivial additive character; self-duality of the local additive groups
targets.note: `Fourier.fourierIntegral e μ f` is defined for any commutative ring with a unitary character `AddChar 𝕜 Circle` and a measure, so a local-field transform can be written, but only the real inner-product-space case has theorems. No standard character x ↦ exp(2πi{Tr x}_p) of ℚ_p or its extensions, no self-dual Haar measure and no isomorphism F_v ≅ F_v^ exist. `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/AddChar.lean` classifies p-adic-valued characters of ℤ_p (Amice), a different object. Tau Ceti classifies continuous characters of the circle only.

targets.target: restricted tensor-product adelic Schwartz–Bruhat space S(𝔸_F) = ⊗'_v S(F_v)
targets.note: The restricted product and 𝔸_K exist as topological rings. There is no restricted tensor product of local function spaces and no space of factorizable adelic test functions; searches for restricted tensor products found nothing in either library.

targets.target: Fourier inversion (local and adelic, including the reflected argument)
targets.note: Inversion is proved on finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with the 2π convention, for integrable f with integrable 𝓕f (continuous or at continuity points). This covers the real and complex places; nothing covers nonarchimedean fields or 𝔸_F.

targets.target: change-of-character and change-of-measure formulas for local and adelic Fourier transforms
targets.note: Proved covariances are translation and linear isometries on real spaces, and Tau Ceti converts between the 2π Fourier convention and Mathlib's characteristic-function convention on real inner-product spaces. There is no formula relating the transforms for ψ and ψ(a·), and no rescaling of self-dual measures.

targets.target: adelic Poisson summation for the diagonal lattice F ⊂ 𝔸_F, with the volume of 𝔸_F/F
targets.note: Poisson summation is proved only for ℤ ⊂ ℝ: for continuous f with locally uniform summability of translates, and for Schwartz f. Tau Ceti proves K discrete and closed in 𝔸_K. Compactness of 𝔸_K/K (only mentioned in that file's docstring), its covolume, and any lattice or adelic Poisson formula are absent.

targets.target: holomorphic parameter integrals, Mellin transforms and the domination estimates that justify differentiating under the integral
targets.note: Differentiation of parametric integrals over any `RCLike` field (so holomorphic dependence), the Mellin transform on (0,∞) with convergence and holomorphy in s from rpow bounds, and Mellin inversion are all proved. They are real-line tools: no Mellin transform over F_v^× for finite v or over the idele class group is defined.

duplicates.note: Also builds adelic test functions as restricted tensor products of locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places (with C_c^∞ rather than Schwartz functions at infinity), so there should be a single restricted-tensor-product construction.

Defines the adelic Weil representation on the restricted tensor product of local Schwartz spaces and proves compatibility with changes of additive character, the same space and change-of-character formulas as AL.0.
The global-function-field counterpart: self-dual local characters and Haar measures from a differential, the residue pairing, discreteness and cocompactness of K ⊂ 𝔸_K, and adelic Poisson summation.
Also plans Mellin transforms and convergence proofs for interchanging limits, differentiation and Euler products, the analytic tools of AL.0's last sentence.

Declared supplier rather than overlap: it states discreteness of K in 𝔸_K and compactness of 𝔸_K/K, the lattice and covolume that AL.0's Poisson summation takes from GlobalNumberFields. Discreteness is already proved in Tau Ceti.

Builds Schwartz–Bruhat function spaces as the Schrödinger models of the Heisenberg extension, with polarizations and their change maps, local compactness, Haar normalization and the translation/modulation relations for a chosen Fourier convention: AL.0's local test-function spaces and change-of-character formulas, one layer below MP.4's adelic Weil representation.

targets.target: local Tate zeta integral Z(f,χ,s) = ∫ f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d×x for a quasi-character χ of F_v^× and a Schwartz–Bruhat f, convergent for Re s > 0
targets.note: At a real place and on ℝ_{>0}, the integral is Mathlib's Mellin transform, and ∫_0^∞ t^{a−1}e^{−rt} dt = r^{−a}Γ(a) is proved. There are no quasi-characters of F_v^× as objects, no multiplicative Haar measure d×x on a local field, and no nonarchimedean zeta integral.

targets.target: rationality of the nonarchimedean zeta integrals in q_v^{−s}
targets.note: No nonarchimedean zeta integral exists to be rational. Mathlib's `ofPowerSeries q f` only turns a formal power series in T = q^{−s} into a formal Dirichlet series.

targets.target: meromorphic continuation of the archimedean zeta integrals
targets.note: Continuation is available for Γ (hence for the Gaussian integral Γ_ℝ) and, abstractly, for Mellin transforms of Mathlib's weak FE-pairs (constant plus rapid decay, with f(1/x) = εx^k g(x)). There is no continuation of ∫_{ℝ^×} f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d×x for a general Schwartz f by Taylor expansion at 0, and no ℂ^× version.

targets.target: L-, ε- and γ-factors with exact normalizations and the local functional equation
targets.note: No local ε- or γ-factor and no local functional equation exist. `rootNumber` is the global root number of a Dirichlet character (Gauss sum over ZMod N divided by i^a√N), `gammaFactor` its archimedean factor, and the Γ_ℝ reflection identities are archimedean γ-factor ratios. None is obtained from a local integral.

targets.target: real and complex gamma factors Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)
targets.note: Deligne's archimedean factors are in Mathlib with their doubling and reflection formulas, poles and residues. They are identified with the Mellin transform of a Gaussian theta sum (`hasSum_mellin_pi_mul_sq`), but not as the local zeta integral of the Gaussian against a character of ℝ^×.

targets.target: unramified and ramified characters of F_v^×, conductor exponents, Gauss sums and character twists
targets.note: Mathlib has Gauss sums over finite rings, with g(χ)g(χ⁻¹) = χ(−1)#R for nontrivial χ on a finite field, and conductors and primitive characters of Dirichlet characters. There is no unramified/ramified decomposition of characters of ℚ_p^× or K_v^×, no conductor exponent a(χ_v), and no local Gauss sum of a ramified character against ψ_v. Tau Ceti has only ring conductors (e.g. the conductor exponent of an order), not character conductors.

targets.target: global zeta integral: Euler factorization, meromorphic continuation and functional equation of Hecke L-functions via Poisson summation, keeping the trivial-character poles
targets.note: For F = ℚ and finite-order characters, Mathlib proves continuation, the functional equation with conductor, Gauss-sum root number and parity, the Euler product and the residue of the trivial character. It uses the classical Hurwitz/theta–Mellin route (with `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` for ζ), not idelic integrals. Over a general number field there is only the Dedekind zeta series with its residue as a one-sided real limit (Mathlib) and its Euler product for Re s > 1 (Tau Ceti). No continuation or functional equation of Dedekind zeta or Hecke L-functions exists, and no idelic zeta integral.

evidence.target: real and complex gamma factors Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)
evidence.name: Complex.Gammaℝ

evidence.target: real and complex gamma factors Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)
evidence.name: Complex.Gammaℂ

evidence.target: real and complex gamma factors Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)
evidence.name: Complex.Gammaℝ_div_Gammaℝ_one_sub

duplicates.note: Continuation, functional equations with conductor, Gauss sum and parity, gamma factors and the principal-character pole for ζ and Dirichlet L-functions: the F = ℚ finite-order case of AL.1's global statements, which Mathlib largely has.
Completed Hecke and Dedekind L-functions over number fields with real/complex gamma factors, residues and ramified Euler factors, the same global targets as AL.1.

Defines Hecke characters as continuous characters of the idele class group, with local components, finite conductor and unitary part: the character carriers and conductors that AL.1 computes local factors for.
Classifies the continuous characters of ℝ^× and ℂ^× as |x|^s sgn(x)^ε and (z/|z|)^k|z|^s, the archimedean quasi-characters whose zeta integrals produce AL.1's real and complex gamma factors.

Proves Mellin-transform continuation, primitive-character Gauss sums, conductor change and imprimitive Euler-factor deletion, and the Dedekind-zeta pole, which it attributes to AL.1's trivial-character Tate theorem. These overlap AL.1's Dirichlet-character and trivial-character targets.
Proves the GL₁ dictionary with Hecke characters, including infinity type, conductor and unitary twist: the same character bookkeeping AL.1 does locally.

Builds prehomogeneous-vector-space zeta integrals and local densities with orbit decomposition, Poisson summation and functional equations, and lists AL.0 among its inputs: the same zeta-integral-to-functional-equation route as AL.1 for a different family, so the convergence and local-factor conventions must be shared.

targets.target: local Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals from Schwartz(–Bruhat) functions on M_n(E) and matrix coefficients of irreducible admissible representations of GL_n(E)
targets.note: Neither library has smooth or admissible representations of GL_n over a local field or their matrix coefficients; searches for admissible/smooth representation, matrix coefficient, Godement and Jacquet found nothing relevant. Only abstract Haar measure on locally compact groups and Schwartz functions on real vector spaces are available.

targets.target: nonarchimedean rationality in q^{−s}, the fractional-ideal characterization of L(s,π) and the local functional equation with γ(s,π,ψ)
targets.note: Nothing: no local zeta integrals, no fractional ideal of ℂ[q^{±s}] and no ε-factors for GL_n.

targets.target: archimedean gamma factors via Casselman–Wallach globalizations, Schwartz estimates and meromorphic parameter integrals; their functional equation
targets.note: No (g,K)-modules, Harish-Chandra modules or smooth Fréchet globalizations exist in either library (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 owns them).

targets.target: unramified spherical computation L(s,π) = det(1 − q^{−s}A_π)^{−1} and comparison with the Satake parameter
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Shimura's Theorem 3.20 for n = 2 (and n = 1): the p-local Hecke ring of GL_n over ℚ relative to GL_n(ℤ) is a polynomial ring on the diagonal double cosets. It also proves the GL₂ recurrence T(p^{k+1}) = T(p)T(p^k) − p·T(p,p)T(p^{k−1}), the formal identity behind the degree-two Euler factor. There is no spherical function, Satake transform, unramified principal series or local zeta integral.

targets.target: global integral for cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n: Euler factorization, analytic continuation and functional equation, with the n = 1 pole separated
targets.note: Only classical special cases exist, proved by Hecke's Mellin argument rather than adelic integrals. For n = 2 over ℚ and holomorphic modular forms on an arithmetic subgroup, Mathlib packages f(it) and its S-translate as a weak FE-pair (continuation and a functional equation relating f to f|S) and proves cusp-form L-functions entire; Tau Ceti identifies the coefficient L-series with them (`CuspForm.hasEntireExtension_qExpansion_coeff`). For a newform, Tau Ceti proves the formal Euler factorization at primes not dividing the level: a_{mn} = a_m a_n for coprime good m, n, and a_{p^{r+2}} = a_p a_{p^{r+1}} − χ(p)p^{k−1}a_{p^r}. The analytic Euler product is not stated. For n = 1 over ℚ there are Dirichlet L-functions. Nothing exists for n ≥ 3, for Maass forms or over other number fields.

targets.target: bounds and normalization conversions for use in interpolation formulas
targets.note: No GL_n local-factor normalizations exist to convert between.

duplicates.note: Relates the GL_n Hecke polynomial P_v(X) to the normalized Satake transform, determinant character and Tate twist: the unramified comparison AL.2 derives from the spherical zeta integral, so the two normalization dictionaries must coincide.

Hecke's completed L-function and functional equation for newforms of level N with the Atkin–Lehner sign, and their Euler product: the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ case of AL.2's global Euler factorization and functional equation.

Constructs local constants for GL_m on the analytic side and proves their dictionary with Weil–Deligne constants. Its text assigns the integral constructions to AL, so its analytic L/ε-factors must be AL.2's rather than a second construction.

targets.target: comparison of the nonarchimedean Whittaker/derivative constructions of SR.5 with the classical complex Whittaker model
targets.note: No Whittaker functional, Kirillov model or Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivative exists in either library; the word Whittaker occurs only in bibliography entries for Whittaker–Watson.

targets.target: GL_n × GL_m local Rankin–Selberg integrals: convergence, nonarchimedean rationality and gcd-normalized L-factors
targets.note: Nothing. Searches for Rankin–Selberg, Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika and gcd L-factors found nothing; Tau Ceti's only 'Rankin' is Rankin's trick in an ideal-counting bound.

targets.target: archimedean Whittaker functionals with uniqueness and continuity on Casselman–Wallach globalizations, completed tensor products, and Jacquet's estimates (§§2–16)
targets.note: Mathlib has the injective seminorm on finite tensor products of normed spaces, but no completed projective tensor product of Fréchet spaces, no globalization and no Whittaker functional.

targets.target: archimedean holomorphic multiples, boundedness in vertical strips, gamma factors and functional equation without a gcd argument
targets.note: Only the general Phragmén–Lindelöf principle in a vertical strip is available as a tool; no Rankin–Selberg integral exists to apply it to.

targets.target: unramified computations, global unfolding for cuspidal data, poles in the contragredient/twist case and nonvanishing in the proved regions
targets.note: Mathlib defines only the Petersson integrand y^k f(τ)·conj f'(τ); there is no unfolding of an Eisenstein series against cusp forms and no Rankin–Selberg L-function.

targets.target: comparison of integral rational structures, Gauss sums and complex periods with the cohomological normalization; periods up to their scalar ambiguity
targets.note: Finite-ring Gauss sums exist, but there is no period of an automorphic representation, no cohomological normalization and no rational structure to compare.

duplicates.note: Defines period lines and scalar periods Ω_f^± of a newform up to basis choice, with Gauss sums and critical values of twists: the GL₂ × GL₁ case of AL.3's period comparison and scalar-ambiguity requirement.
Proves a Rankin–Selberg/Hecke evaluation of the regulator integral for modular units at a stated level and character, a specific GL₂ × GL₂ unfolding that should consume AL.3 rather than reprove it.

Declared supplier: builds the Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives and Whittaker functionals AL.3 imports. The comparison with the classical complex Whittaker model sits on the boundary and should have one owner.

targets.target: Euler polynomial det(1 − r(t_v)X) attached to the Satake semisimple conjugacy class t_v and an algebraic representation r of the L-group
targets.note: `Matrix.charpolyRev M = det(1 − X·M)` supplies the polynomial once a matrix is given. No L-group, no Satake class and no representation of a dual group exist in either library; searches for Satake, L-group, Langlands dual and dual group found nothing.

targets.target: invariance of the Euler polynomial under conjugacy, direct sum, tensor product, duality and scalar extension
targets.note: The linear algebra for conjugacy, direct sums and base change is in Mathlib for characteristic polynomials (hence for their reverses). There is no formula for the characteristic polynomial of a tensor product or of the contragredient in terms of the factors, and nothing ties these to Satake parameters.

targets.target: partial Euler product L^S(s,π,r) and its convergence under a supplied bound on the Satake eigenvalues
targets.note: Mathlib builds formal L-functions from local power series in q^{−s} (`ofPowerSeries`, `eulerProduct`) and proves ∏_p Σ_e f(p^e) = Σ f(n) for multiplicative f with absolutely summable values. Tau Ceti has the ideal-indexed Euler product of a multiplicative weight over a number field, and the degree-two good-prime recurrence of newform coefficients (the standard L-function of GL₂/ℚ in formal form). The step from an eigenvalue bound |α_{v,i}| ≤ q_v^θ to absolute convergence of a degree-n Euler product for Re s > 1 + θ is not proved, and no L^S(s,π,r) is defined.

targets.target: comparison with the AL.1–AL.3 factors and with Weil–Deligne L-factors under an actual local-compatibility theorem
targets.note: No Weil group, Weil–Deligne representation or local L-factor of a Galois representation exists in either library, and no AL.1–AL.3 factors exist to compare.

duplicates.note: For GL_n and its standard representation, constructs the Hecke polynomial Σ(−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2}T_{v,i}X^{n−i} and relates it to normalized Satake: the same unramified Euler polynomial as AL.4 in that case.
Builds the normalization dictionary among normalized Satake, the integral Hecke polynomial, Frobenius conventions and Tate twists, the conventions AL.4's Euler polynomials must follow.
Defines completed L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data, the Galois-side factors AL.4 is to compare with.

targets.target: removal and reinsertion of Euler factors at a finite set, and imprimitive/primitive comparisons
targets.note: For Dirichlet characters Mathlib proves L(χ at level N, s) = L(χ, s)·∏_{p∣N}(1 − χ(p)p^{−s}) as entire or meromorphic functions, and identifies a character with the change of level of its primitive character. Tau Ceti restricts ideal weights away from a finite set of primes and proves finite Euler products for the supported part. Nothing exists for GL₂ or Rankin–Selberg L-functions.

targets.target: critical-value normalization, functional-equation sign and algebraicity inputs for the GL₂ and Rankin families of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions
targets.note: Only GL₁/ℚ analogues exist: rationality of ζ(−k) via Bernoulli numbers and the root number of a Dirichlet character. No critical values, periods or signs of GL₂ or Rankin–Selberg L-functions are formalized.

targets.target: compatibility of conductor exponents, local test vectors and character twists
targets.note: No local conductor exponent of a representation, no newvector or test vector, and no twisting of local representations exists.

targets.target: explicit limiting or derivative results for vanishing Euler factors (exceptional zeros), without cancellation
targets.note: Nothing on exceptional zeros or L-invariants in either library.

targets.target: export of the formulas both as formal local polynomials and as complex evaluations
targets.note: Mathlib's route from local polynomials, through `PowerSeries.invOfUnit` and `ofPowerSeries`/`eulerProduct`, to `LSeries` provides the formal-versus-complex carriers. The GL₂ and Rankin formulas to export do not exist.

duplicates.note: Proves conductor change, imprimitive Euler-factor deletion and algebraicity of the complex values for Dirichlet characters: AL.5's removal/reinsertion and algebraicity interfaces for GL₁.
Primitive/imprimitive comparisons, conductor change and the interpolation formula with its removed Euler factor (1 − (χη)(p)p^{k−1}), the GL₁ instance of AL.5's contracts.
Proves changes of periods, coefficients and primitive/imprimitive conventions across the p-adic constructions, the consumer-side twin of AL.5's normalization interfaces.
States the GL₂ interpolation formula with its Euler factor (1 − χ(p)p^j/α), Gauss sum, (2πi)^{j+1} and period normalization, the critical-value normalization AL.5 is to supply.
Formulates normalized critical values with signs and powers of 2πi and retains ramified and imprimitive corrections: the same normalization targets from the periods side.

targets.target: measurable fields of separable Hilbert spaces, direct integrals, decomposable operators and isometric integration maps
targets.note: Only the two extreme cases exist. One is Hilbert direct sums (`IsHilbertSum`: an orthogonal family with E ≅ ℓ²(G)), the counting-measure case. The other is L²(α,μ;E) for a single fixed Hilbert space E, the constant-field case. Tau Ceti builds Hilbert bases of L² of product measures. There is no measurable field of Hilbert spaces, no direct integral, and no decomposable operator; searches for direct integral, measurable field and Hilbert bundle found nothing.

targets.target: the spectral theorem needed for the spectrum (bounded normal and unbounded self-adjoint operators, in projection-valued or multiplication-operator form), reusing compact-operator spectral theory
targets.note: The compact self-adjoint spectral theorem is complete: eigenspaces are dense in Mathlib, and Tau Ceti builds a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors. There is also the continuous functional calculus for normal elements of C*-algebras. For unbounded operators, Tau Ceti has partial linear maps with adjoints, self-adjointness, nonreal points in the resolvent set, and Stone's theorem (self-adjoint A ↔ unitary C₀-group generated by iA). No projection-valued measure, spectral measure or multiplication-operator form of the spectral theorem exists, bounded or unbounded.

targets.target: trace-class and Hilbert–Schmidt integral operators (kernels, traces as diagonal integrals)
targets.note: Neither library defines trace-class, Hilbert–Schmidt, nuclear or Schatten operators; Mathlib mentions trace-class only in a TODO of the multivariate Gaussian file. Tau Ceti proves convolution by a continuous kernel is compact on L²(G) for compact G, and tr π(f) = ∫ f·χ_π for finite-dimensional π.

targets.target: nuclear Fréchet test-function spaces
targets.note: Mathlib has C^n test functions 𝓓^n(Ω,F) with the LF topology, the spaces 𝓓_K and the Schwartz space as locally convex (Schwartz also first countable) spaces on real normed spaces. It proves neither completeness (Fréchet) nor nuclearity, and has no test functions on a Lie group or on G(𝔸).

targets.target: weakly and strongly meromorphic operator-valued families and their finite-rank residues
targets.note: `MeromorphicAt` and holomorphy apply to functions into any normed space, including E →L[ℂ] F, so norm-meromorphic operator families are covered. Tau Ceti proves the resolvent of a partial linear map analytic, and Mathlib has the Fredholm alternative for a single compact operator. There is no weak or strong meromorphy, no analytic Fredholm theorem in a parameter, and no residue theory for operator families (Tau Ceti's residues are scalar).

targets.target: Fubini and interchange lemmas (sums, integrals, derivatives) under integrability hypotheses
targets.note: Fubini for s-finite measures, sum–integral interchange for countable families with summable L¹ norms, and differentiation under the integral (over any `RCLike` parameter, so holomorphic dependence is included) are all in Mathlib, with explicit integrability hypotheses.

targets.target: distributional convergence
targets.note: Tempered distributions carry the pointwise-convergence topology, with convergence tested on each Schwartz function, and distributions 𝓓' on open subsets of real normed spaces carry the compact-convergence topology. There are no distributions on C_c^∞ of a locally compact group or of G(𝔸), which is what the trace-formula distributions need.
