duplicates.note: Builds compact self-adjoint convolution (integral) operators on L²(G) with finite-dimensional eigenspaces and a spectral decomposition. This is the compact-group instance of AS.0's integral-operator and compact spectral-theory toolkit, already completed in Tau Ceti.

targets.target: sections of normalized parabolic induction from cuspidal data on a rational Levi M, depending holomorphically on λ ∈ a*_{M,ℂ}
targets.note: Only ingredients exist. Mathlib has algebraic (unnormalized) coinduction and the modular character of a locally compact group, from which δ_P could be built (its continuity is a TODO). Tau Ceti has the dynamic parabolic P(λ) of a cocharacter of an affine group scheme with Levi decomposition U(λ) ⋊ Z(λ) on points, and unnormalized principal series of GL₂(𝔽_q). There is no smooth induced representation of G(𝔸), no a*_M, and no holomorphic family of sections.

targets.target: absolute and locally uniform convergence of the Eisenstein series Σ_{P(F)\G(F)} φ_λ(γg) in a positive chamber, with differentiated growth estimates and automorphy
targets.note: Only the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ case at an integral point: Mathlib's Eisenstein series of weight k ≥ 3 for Γ(N) (a sum over coprime pairs in a congruence class) converges locally uniformly, is Γ(N)-invariant, bounded at every cusp, and a modular form. There is no complex parameter s or λ, no non-holomorphic or Maass Eisenstein series (searches for these, Epstein zeta and Godement's criterion found nothing), and nothing for a parabolic of a general reductive group.

targets.target: constant term of the Eisenstein series along a parabolic as a finite Weyl-group sum of intertwining operators in the convergence region
targets.note: Mathlib computes q-coefficients (including the constant term) as integrals over a period and shows the normalized E_k has constant term 1. There is no constant term along a unipotent radical of G(𝔸), no intertwining operator, and no Weyl-sum formula.

duplicates.note: Proves convergence in the initial chamber and constant terms of genuine Eisenstein series on a double cover of GSp(4). Its text requires adapting AS's linear-group estimates rather than importing them, so this is a parallel development for covers.

Plans the translation between Mathlib's level-Γ(N) holomorphic Eisenstein series and Eisenstein series with character. That is the classical GL₂/ℚ holomorphic special case of AS.1's convergence and automorphy statements.

targets.target: global and local standard intertwining operators M(w,λ) by convergent unipotent integrals; factorization for factorizable sections; cocycle and adjoint identities
targets.note: Only algebraic intertwiners and the finite-group Mackey theory exist: the double-coset decomposition of Res∘Ind and the Mackey formula for dim Hom between induced representations, the finite analogue of the Bruhat-cell analysis of intertwiners. There are no unipotent integrals, no Gindikin–Karpelevich formula and no cocycle relation.

targets.target: meromorphic continuation of intertwining operators and Eisenstein series, functional equations, and regularity/unitarity on the unitary axis, tracking singular hyperplanes and residues
targets.note: The only continuation machinery is the one-variable Mellin/theta argument for L-functions (weak FE-pairs, completed ζ and Dirichlet L-functions), which gives the scalar ξ(s) that appears in the SL₂(ℤ) scattering coefficient. Nothing continues an Eisenstein series or an operator family in λ.

targets.target: normalizing factors and normalized intertwining operators
targets.note: No normalizing factors or local coefficients (Langlands–Shahidi) exist in either library.

duplicates.note: Proves meromorphic continuation of cover-specific Eisenstein series through prescribed intertwining operators, with their functional equations and residues: AS.2's targets on a nonlinear cover.

targets.target: Arthur's truncation operator Λ^T from parabolic constant terms and chamber indicators τ̂_P; local finiteness and the alternating-sum identities on root cones (Langlands' combinatorial lemma)
targets.note: Only neighbouring objects exist: the height-truncated SL₂(ℤ) fundamental domain (a set, not an operator), the dominant chamber of a root system in Tau Ceti, and the lemma that pairwise obtuse vectors in a half-space are linearly independent (a root-cone input). There is no τ_P or τ̂_P and no truncation operator.

targets.target: integrability (rapid decay) of truncated automorphic forms for sufficiently regular T
targets.note: For classical forms there are measure-theoretic fundamental domains for PSL₂(ℤ), moderate growth of modular forms on arithmetic subgroups, and exponential decay of cusp forms at i∞. There are no Siegel sets for general G (reduction theory is AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3) and no truncated automorphic forms.

targets.target: polynomial-exponential dependence of truncated integrals on T and the behaviour of the coefficients
targets.note: No exponential polynomials in T or extraction of their coefficients exist.

targets.target: Maass–Selberg inner-product formula for truncated Eisenstein series, with limits at singular parameters, and the orthogonality and norm identities for wave packets
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Petersson products of cusp forms on finite-index subgroups, independent of the fundamental domain. Mathlib has the unfolding trick ∫_G g(πx) f(x) = ∫_{G/Γ} g·automorphize f. Nothing concerns Eisenstein series or wave packets.

targets.target: discrete cuspidal and residual subspaces of L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)) and Eisenstein wave packets
targets.note: Only holomorphic cusp forms as a submodule of M_k(Γ), and Petersson-orthogonal complements inside S_k(Γ), exist. There is no L² space on an adelic quotient, no residual spectrum and no wave packet.

targets.target: unitary isomorphism from the sum/direct integral over associate cuspidal data onto L², with surjectivity, Weyl multiplicity factors and separation of residual and continuous terms
targets.note: Nothing; this needs AS.0's direct integrals and AS.1–AS.3, none of which exist.

targets.target: finite multiplicities in the discrete spectrum
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves classical multiplicity one (good-Hecke eigenspaces in S_k(N,χ)^new have dimension ≤ 1) and finite-dimensionality of nonzero eigenspaces of convolution operators on compact groups. Finite multiplicity of automorphic representations in L²_disc is not stated.

targets.target: compatibility of the decomposition with finite Hecke operators and central characters
targets.note: Classically, Tau Ceti decomposes S_k(Γ₁(N)) into Petersson-orthogonal nebentypus spaces (the central-character decomposition for holomorphic forms) and proves Shimura's commutativity criterion for Hecke rings. No Hecke or central-character action on L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)) is defined.

targets.target: compact quotients: specialization to a discrete Hilbert sum with finite multiplicities
targets.note: For a compact group G and trivial Γ, Tau Ceti proves Peter–Weyl: the normalized matrix coefficients of a set of unitary irreducible representatives form a Hilbert basis of L²(G), so the right regular representation is a discrete Hilbert sum with multiplicity dim V. The Gelfand–Graev–Piatetski-Shapiro theorem for compact Γ\G with noncompact G (e.g. anisotropic groups) is absent.

targets.target: GL₂ over ℚ: recovery of the continuous Eisenstein contribution
targets.note: No non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, Maass forms or Laplacian spectrum on SL₂(ℤ)\ℍ exist in either library.

duplicates.note: Deduces square integrability of cusp forms with unitary central character and finite multiplicity of cuspidal constituents, the cuspidal part of AS.4's finite-multiplicity statement.
The Peter–Weyl Hilbert basis of L²(G) for compact G is the trivial-Γ case of AS.4's compact-quotient specialization. It is already completed in Tau Ceti and should be reused.
Builds the Petersson inner product with Hecke adjoints and a simultaneous orthonormal eigenbasis of S_k(Γ₁(N)): the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ piece of the discrete spectrum with Hecke compatibility.

targets.target: weighted L² complexes and regularization
targets.note: Searches for weighted cohomology, weighted L² complexes and regularization found nothing.

targets.target: finite-infinitesimal-character functors (Z(g)-finite parts)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the algebraic inputs: the Casimir element is central in U(L) for a nondegenerate Killing form, central characters χ_λ : Z(U(L)) → K come from Verma modules, and the Casimir acts on a highest-weight module by ⟨λ+ρ,λ+ρ⟩ − ⟨ρ,ρ⟩. The Harish-Chandra isomorphism, generalized Z(g)-eigenspace functors and Z(g)-finite function spaces are absent.

targets.target: filtration and acyclicity theorems comparing relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of smooth functions of uniform moderate growth (Franke)
targets.note: Mathlib has Lie algebra cochains only in degrees ≤ 3 (with the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex listed as TODO) and group cohomology. There are no (g,K)-modules, no relative Lie algebra cohomology and no Franke filtration.

targets.target: automorphic comparison with algebraic coefficient systems and Hecke equivariance, keeping ordinary rather than cuspidal or L² cohomology
targets.note: Only local coefficient systems on the fundamental groupoid (Tau Ceti) and the abstract Hecke ring of double cosets (Mathlib) exist. No cohomology of locally symmetric spaces carries a Hecke action.

duplicates.note: Constructs U(g_C), its centre, generalized infinitesimal-character subspaces and relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k),V), the objects on which AS.5's finite-infinitesimal-character functors and comparison are built.

Its full (late) form compares Betti, de Rham and relative Lie algebra cohomology and uses AS.5 for the automorphic step. The boundary between the de Rham comparison there and Franke's comparison here must be kept exact.

targets.target: automorphic kernel K_f(x,y) = Σ_{γ∈G(F)} f(x⁻¹γy) of R(f) for compactly supported smooth f, and its truncation
targets.note: Tau Ceti has convolution kernels (k∗f)(x) = ∫ k(xy⁻¹)f(y)dy and integrated operators π(f) for compact groups, and Mathlib has folding ∫_G f = ∫_{G/Γ} Σ_γ f(γx). No kernel of R(f) on L²(Γ\G) or G(F)\G(𝔸) exists, truncated or not.

targets.target: integrability and equality of the coarse geometric and spectral expansions
targets.note: Only the finite-group Frobenius formula for induced characters exists, the trace formula for a finite group. Searches for trace formula, Selberg and orbital integral found only unrelated uses (trace formulas in linear algebra and topology). The compact-quotient Selberg trace formula is also absent.

targets.target: weighted orbital integrals, weighted characters, (G,M)-families, their convergence and the fine expansions
targets.note: Nothing: no orbital integral of any kind is defined in either library.

targets.target: invariant distributions by the invariantization recursion and the invariant trace formula with its summation and convergence conditions
targets.note: For compact groups Tau Ceti proves tr π(f) = ∫ f·χ_π and that irreducible characters form a Hilbert basis of class functions, the compact analogue of characters as invariant distributions. There are no invariant distributions on G(𝔸) or on p-adic or real reductive groups.

duplicates.note: Builds the twisted invariant trace identity 'from the same kernel/truncation machinery' as AS.6 and says the untwisted formula is only a template, so the kernel, truncation and invariantization steps should be shared.
Constructs quotient measures on centralizer quotients and proves convergence of regular semisimple orbital integrals, the local harmonic analysis AS.6 asks to make reusable.
The Eichler–Selberg trace formula for Hecke operators at level one, with Hurwitz class numbers: a classical special case of the trace identity, planned by a separate elementary route.
Plans Selberg trace-formula comparisons and spectral zeta functions on compact or finite-volume quotients, overlapping AS.6's compact-quotient worked example.

targets.target: indexing categories of levels: compact open subgroups K_p with inclusions and conjugation, and cofinal normal or pro-p sequences
targets.note: Mathlib has the lattice of open (normal) subgroups and, in compact totally disconnected groups, open normal subgroups inside every neighbourhood of 1. Tau Ceti gives a cofinal antitone sequence of open normal subgroups in a topologically finitely generated compact group, a pro-p predicate, and the unit filtration 1+𝔪^i of a local field as a basis of neighbourhoods (the GL₁ congruence tower). There are no compact open subgroups of G(ℚ_p) for reductive G (GL_n(ℤ_p), principal congruence K(pⁿ)), no proof that these are pro-p, and no category of levels with conjugation maps.

targets.target: finite covering correspondences Y(K′) → Y(K) between arithmetic quotients, with composition identities and conjugation maps; neat cofinal towers that keep stabilizers at descended levels
targets.note: The topology of quotient coverings is available. A free, properly discontinuous action on a locally compact Hausdorff space gives a quotient covering (Mathlib). The intermediate map E/H → E/G for H ≤ G is a covering and deck transformations of E/H → X are N(H)/H (Tau Ceti). Arithmetic subgroups of GL₂(ℝ) act properly discontinuously on ℍ. There are no locally symmetric spaces Y(K) = G(ℚ)\G(𝔸)/K, no neat subgroups (Minkowski/Selberg lemmas are absent) and no orbifold or stack model at non-neat levels.

targets.target: derived group-cohomology model at levels with stabilizers, retaining torsion, with change of level
targets.note: Mathlib's group cohomology of an arbitrary group G with coefficients in a k-linear representation is Extⁿ_{Rep k G}(k, A), so it is the derived model and keeps all torsion of groups with torsion. Shapiro's lemma Hⁿ(G, Coind_S^G A) ≅ Hⁿ(S, A) holds for every subgroup, and Ind ≅ Coind for finite index, giving the level-change isomorphisms. Tau Ceti has the profinite Shapiro lemma in degree 1. The model is present for any group; what is missing is its input: the arithmetic groups Γ_K of a reductive group at each level (only congruence subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) exist), and the identification with the cohomology of the orbifold Γ_K\X (see the comparison target).

targets.target: compact support via compatible compactifications (Borel–Serre) or the functorial j_! model, with trace maps
targets.note: Group-side traces exist in low degree: corestriction on continuous H¹ for open finite-index subgroups (Tau Ceti), corestriction on group homology in all degrees (Mathlib), and the trace of modular forms between levels. There is no compactly supported cohomology, no Borel–Serre compactification, no extension by zero j_! and no transfer for finite covering spaces.

targets.target: comparison of singular, cellular and étale finite-coefficient models under finite-type/characteristic hypotheses
targets.note: Each model exists separately in some form: singular homology (Mathlib) and relative singular homology (Tau Ceti), sheaf cohomology on a site, and pro-étale Hⁿ(X, ℤ_ℓ). There is no singular cohomology with coefficients as a cochain theory, no cellular homology, no small étale cohomology with finite coefficients, and no comparison theorem between any two of them.

duplicates.note: Constructs the finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat level, computes their degrees from stabilizer indices, proves Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences and keeps quotient groupoids at non-neat level: the same covering-correspondence and stabilizer targets as CC.0.
Defines singular, cellular and compact-support cochains on the arithmetic quotients and proves their comparison with sheaf cohomology, which is CC.0's model comparison at finite level.

Constructs the p-level inverse systems, proves cofinality of the principal congruence systems and the group actions with level changes for Shimura towers: CC.0's indexing and conjugation data in the Shimura setting.
Assembles direct and inverse systems in tame and p-power level with restriction, corestriction and Hecke actions, and reexports CC's limits. The finite-level tower data overlaps CC.0.

Constructs the Borel–Serre compactification: rational parabolic boundary components, the manifold-with-corners structure at neat level, compactness of the quotient, the homotopy equivalence from the interior and the stratification spectral sequence. That is the compactification CC.0's compact-support target names, and the neat-level hypothesis CC.0's cofinal towers require.

targets.target: filtered colimits at fixed s in modules and complexes: exactness and independence under cofinal restriction
targets.note: Mathlib: AB5 for ModuleCat R (an unnamed instance in Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/AB.lean), exactness of colim under exact colimits of shape J, the direct limit of modules, and colimit(F ⋙ G) ≅ colimit G for final F. Tau Ceti: AB5 without universe restrictions, and homology of homological complexes commutes with colimits of any exact shape, so the colimit of the complexes computes the colimit of cohomology. The tower cohomology to which these apply does not exist (CC.0).

targets.target: action of the full local group on colim_K Hⁱ by conjugating levels, with open stabilizers so that the action is smooth
targets.note: The notion of a smooth action is present: continuity of an action on a discrete space ↔ open stabilizers (Mathlib); smooth discrete representations and M = ⋃_U M^U for profinite groups (Tau Ceti); the conjugation action of G on H¹(N, M) for normal N (Tau Ceti). The action of G(ℚ_p) on the colimit of tower cohomology, which needs non-normal levels and all degrees, is absent.

targets.target: commuting tame Hecke operators from double-coset correspondences with explicit pullback/trace normalization
targets.note: Abstract Hecke rings of double cosets exist, with product, associativity, degree and Shimura's commutativity criterion via an anti-involution (Tau Ceti), and classical double-coset operators act on modular forms. No Hecke correspondence acts on the cohomology of arithmetic quotients, and no pullback/trace normalization is set up.

targets.target: Mackey and restriction/corestriction identities with degree factors, without inverting them integrally
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the Mackey decomposition Res_K Ind_H A ≅ ⨁_{KsH} Ind Res(ˢA) with no finiteness hypothesis. It also proves cor∘res = [G:U] on continuous cohomology in degrees 0, 1 and 2 (and on Tate cohomology in degrees 0 and −1). Mathlib has restriction in all degrees but no cohomological corestriction. cor∘res = index in all degrees, and the double-coset formula res∘cor on cohomology, are absent.

evidence.name: Module.DirectLimit

duplicates.note: Constructs Hecke correspondences on the finite-level complexes through K∩gKg⁻¹ with pullback and trace, composition via the double-coset algebra and change of level: the same Hecke-operator target as CC.1, before passing to the colimit.
Proves restriction/corestriction identities and descent consequences for the generic continuous cohomology theory, the generic form of CC.1's restriction/corestriction identities.
Declared supplier: defines smoothness by open stabilizers and proves closure under filtered colimits, which CC.1 applies to the colimit of tower cohomology.

targets.target: inverse systems in s and their topological inverse limit as an O-module, with separatedness and completeness
targets.note: Mathlib has the I-adic completion of a module as compatible sequences in M/IⁿM, which is I-adically complete (separated and precomplete) for finitely generated I. For rings it has the equivalence with topological completeness, and limits of topological modules with the limit topology (unnamed instances in Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Topology/Basic.lean). The limit lim_s colim_K Hⁱ(Y(K), O/ϖ^s) itself, and a proof that this limit is ϖ-adically separated and complete, are absent.

targets.target: derived inverse limit of complexes, the lim¹ functor and the Milnor exact sequence 0 → lim¹ H^{i−1} → Hⁱ(R lim) → lim Hⁱ → 0
targets.note: No lim¹, derived limit, homotopy limit or Milnor sequence exists in either library; searches for lim1, lim¹, limOne, Milnor, holim and R lim found nothing. Mathlib's general right derived functors have not been applied to lim.

targets.target: surjectivity and Mittag-Leffler criteria for the vanishing of lim¹ at each use
targets.note: The Mittag-Leffler condition and its eventual-range consequences are formalized for functors to Type, and an ℕᵒᵖ-system with surjective transitions has lim → X₀ surjective. There is no Mittag-Leffler condition for module systems and no theorem that it kills lim¹, since lim¹ is not defined.

targets.target: comparison of the reduction of the completed module with its finite-coefficient counterpart under torsion/control hypotheses, with counterexample tests
targets.note: For modules Mathlib proves ker(M̂ → M/IⁿM) = Iⁿ·M̂ (I finitely generated) and exactness of completion on finite modules over a noetherian ring, and group cohomology has the long exact sequence usable for 0 → M → M → M/ϖ → 0. No comparison for completed cohomology or its reductions exists.

targets.target: the unitary Banach module obtained by inverting p on a complete bounded integral lattice, and continuity of the group and Hecke actions
targets.note: Only finite-rank lattice rationalization K ⊗ S ≅ V (Tau Ceti) and separately continuous representations (Mathlib) exist. There are no p-adic Banach representations and no unit-ball lattices; the separately continuous `ContRepresentation` does not give joint continuity of the action.

duplicates.note: The declared generic owner: constructs derived inverse limits and keeps lim¹ until a proved Mittag-Leffler condition removes it. CC.2's derived-limit and lim¹ targets are its targets applied to towers.
Proves the Mittag-Leffler and lim¹ statements before interchanging cohomology and inverse limits for lattices and their torsion quotients, the same interchange discipline as CC.2.
Proves derived Mittag-Leffler comparisons and keeps lim¹ for inverse systems of complexes over complete local rings, overlapping CC.2's derived-limit and Mittag-Leffler targets.

Defines p-completion as the derived inverse limit of the E/p^r system and constructs the Milnor lim¹ exact sequence together with the hypotheses under which it collapses to an ordinary inverse limit: CC.2's derived-limit, lim¹ and Milnor-sequence targets in the spectra setting.

targets.target: continuous O-linear and Pontryagin duals with the correct compact/discrete topologies
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Pontryagin dual A →ₜ* Circle with the compact-open topology, with instances making the dual of a compact group discrete and of a discrete group compact. It also has the algebraic character module Hom(A, ℚ/ℤ) with exactness of dualization and the continuous linear dual. There is no continuous O-linear dual Hom_cont(M, O) or Hom_cont(M, E/O) with its topology for profinite O-modules.

targets.target: the dual of the smooth torsion colimit as a projective system, and completed homology lim_K H_i(Y(K), O) with the transfer direction
targets.note: No completed homology and no inverse limit of homology exist. Corestriction on group homology could supply transition maps.

targets.target: module structure of completed homology over O[[K₀]] for compact open K₀, distinguishing left modules from the opposite action arising by duality
targets.note: No completed group ring O[[K]] = lim O[K/U] exists. Mathlib's p-adic 'abstract measures' are continuous linear functionals C(ℤ_p, R) → E with the Amice transform D(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) ≃ ℤ_p⟦X⟧ as a linear equivalence only (no convolution product). The contragredient and the right-action-on-dual construction are purely algebraic.

targets.target: biduality in the compact/discrete or admissible category
targets.note: Biduality is proved only for finite abelian groups (with enough roots of unity) and for algebraically reflexive modules. Pontryagin duality for compact or discrete abelian groups, and duality between compact O[[K]]-modules and discrete torsion smooth modules, are absent.

targets.target: compatibility of continuous duals with localisation and completion
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves A ⊗_R Hom_R(M, R) ≅ Hom_A(A ⊗ M, A) for finite projective M, covering localisations. Nothing covers continuous duals of compact or completed modules.

duplicates.note: Declared supplier: defines R[[G]] = lim (R/Iⁿ)[G/U] with its topology and continuous module actions, the completed group ring over which CC.3 puts completed homology.
Also constructs O[[G]] as an inverse limit over open normal subgroups and coefficient quotients, with topology and continuous module actions, for p-adic Lie groups: the same object as CC.3's O[[K₀]].
Constructs the duals and completed group-algebra actions of the smooth mod-p and admissible Banach categories of GL₂(ℚ_p), the GL₂ case of CC.3's duality between compact and discrete objects.

targets.target: cellular complexes on finite CW or Borel–Serre models, and equivariant lifted cell complexes on a cofinal torsion-free tower (including boundary chains)
targets.note: CW complexes exist as topological structures, simplicial sets have chain complexes, and Tau Ceti realizes abstract simplicial complexes. There is no cellular chain complex, no G-CW complex and no Borel–Serre model.

targets.target: comparison of cellular with singular/étale cochains and compatibility of refinement maps
targets.note: Singular chains are defined as the simplicial chain complex of the singular set, which is a definition rather than a comparison theorem. No cellular–singular comparison exists.

targets.target: bounded complexes of finite free/projective O[[K₀]]-modules computing completed homology for a finite-cell compact quotient and compact p-adic analytic K₀
targets.note: Projective resolutions, K-projective complexes and finite resolutions in exact categories exist. There are no perfect complexes, no completed group rings and no finite free complexes computing completed homology.

targets.target: derived finite-level coinvariants recovering the finite-level complex (not underived invariants)
targets.note: For a discrete group G, Mathlib identifies group homology with Tor over k[G] (derived coinvariants) and proves Shapiro's lemma for homology. Derived coinvariants of complexes over O[[K₀]], and the recovery of the finite-level complex C ⊗^L_{O[[K₀]]} O[K₀/K], are absent.

duplicates.note: Builds bounded finite projective cellular models of the finite-level cochains under finite-CW and neat hypotheses, and compares singular/cellular cochains with sheaf cohomology: CC.4's finite-level chain models before the tower.
Defines cellular homology from skeleta and proves the cellular-to-singular comparison naturally up to specified homotopy, the generic form of CC.4's cellular–singular comparison.
Compares finite-level cellular complexes, algebraic local systems and integral Hecke actions with derived coefficient and level change, overlapping CC.4's finite-level chain-model comparisons.

Its manifold-with-corners Borel–Serre model, boundary fibrations and finite stratification are the Borel–Serre cell models on which CC.4's equivariant lifted cell complexes and boundary chains are built.

targets.target: noetherianity of the completed group algebra O[[K₀]] of a compact p-adic analytic group (Lazard)
targets.note: Mathlib proves power series rings in finitely many variables over a noetherian ring are noetherian, which would give O[[ℤ_pᵈ]] ≅ O[[T₁,…,T_d]]. Neither the completed group ring nor that isomorphism is formalized, and Mathlib's Amice transform is only a linear equivalence. Tau Ceti has the pro-p Frattini subgroup and topological finite generation. p-adic analytic, uniform or powerful groups and Lazard's theorem are absent.

targets.target: finite generation of completed homology over O[[K₀]] from the finite-cell tower model
targets.note: Only a complete Nakayama lemma for adically precomplete modules is available, which is an ingredient of the compact-module finiteness argument.

targets.target: dual admissibility criterion and admissibility of completed cohomology in the torsion and unitary Banach categories, with explicit finiteness hypotheses
targets.note: Neither library has admissible smooth or Banach representations; the searches found only unrelated uses of 'admissible' (quiver ideals, adic spaces).

duplicates.note: Proves the noetherian and module-finiteness facts for completed group rings of p-adic Lie groups under exact group hypotheses, the Lazard input CC.5 uses.
Proves the finiteness and compactness results for the admissible unitary Banach and smooth mod-p categories of GL₂(ℚ_p), the GL₂(ℚ_p) case of CC.5's admissibility category.

targets.target: continuous Hochschild–Serre (descent) spectral sequence comparing tower and fixed-level cohomology, with its edge maps
targets.note: Only the degree-one inflation–restriction exact sequence exists: for discrete groups (Mathlib) and for continuous cohomology with a normal subgroup (Tau Ceti). Spectral sequences and spectral objects exist as general frameworks, but Mathlib lists the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence as a TODO in GroupCohomology/Basic.lean.

targets.target: derived-invariants formulation of fixed-level cohomology and its functoriality for Hecke maps
targets.note: Mathlib defines continuous cohomology of topological groups with functoriality, and group cohomology of discrete groups as Ext (derived invariants). Tau Ceti shows H¹ of a profinite group is the colimit of the finite-level H¹. No derived functor RΓ(K, –) on smooth or completed coefficient modules exists, and nothing is functorial in Hecke correspondences.

targets.target: classical comparison maps for algebraic coefficient systems V via finite-level evaluation, with hypotheses and degree ranges
targets.note: Algebraic representations (symmetric powers; points of a Hopf algebra acting on a comodule) exist, but there is no map (H̃ ⊗ V)^K → H*(Y(K), V) and no locally algebraic vectors.

duplicates.note: The declared generic owner of full continuous Hochschild–Serre with convergence hypotheses and five-term/edge maps, which CC.6 applies to towers.
Proves finite-level descent and the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application on the same tower, overlapping CC.6's descent comparison.

Relates classical finite-level cohomology with algebraic coefficients to completed cohomology for GL₂, the specialization of CC.6's classical comparison, and demands the same care about interchanging invariants and limits.

targets.target: the support triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_∂ passed through the derived tower construction: exactness and connecting morphisms
targets.note: The homological algebra exists: a short exact sequence of cochain complexes gives a distinguished triangle in the derived category and a long exact homology sequence with connecting maps (Mathlib), and Tau Ceti has the long exact sequence of a pair in singular homology. Compactly supported and boundary cohomology of arithmetic quotients, and their derived tower limits, are absent.

targets.target: relation of the derived limits with degreewise completed cohomology, including lim¹ and torsion errors
targets.note: No lim¹ or derived limit exists (see CC.2).

targets.target: completed interior cohomology as the specified image, with each comparison proved separately
targets.note: No interior, parabolic or cuspidal cohomology exists in either library, even at finite level (no Eichler–Shimura or modular-symbol cohomology).

duplicates.note: Declared supplier: proves the finite-level triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_boundary → functorially in level and coefficients, which CC.7 passes through the tower.

Distinguishes ordinary, compactly supported and parabolic cohomology of modular curves at finite level and proves their comparisons: the modular-curve instance of CC.7's support and interior-cohomology targets.

targets.target: identification of the generic completed object with the finite-level modular, Siegel, unitary and Hilbert tower models
targets.note: Neither library has modular curves, Shimura, Siegel, unitary or Hilbert modular varieties as spaces or schemes. Only congruence subgroups and their proper action on ℍ exist.

targets.target: transport of finite-level Galois and tame Hecke actions, their continuity and commutation with all transition maps
targets.note: Pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes is defined with no Galois action. No étale cohomology of Shimura varieties or Hecke action on it exists.

targets.target: localisation at a specified residual Hecke ideal (maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra)
targets.note: Tau Ceti maps the integral Hecke ring 𝕋(Δ₀(N), Γ₀(N), ℤ) to endomorphisms of the weight-k cusp forms with nebentypus χ, but does not form its image as a Hecke algebra 𝕋. Localisation at primes is general Mathlib. No Hecke algebra acting on tower cohomology, and no non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, exists.

targets.target: comparison with the conventions of Scholze's torsion paper §4.2 (support and lattice), exporting named comparison isomorphisms
targets.note: No completed cohomology exists in either library, so there is nothing to compare.

duplicates.note: Specializes CC.0–CC.8 to modular and Shimura curves, identifying the tower and transfer maps with ModularCurvesPartII and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves: the GL₂ instance of CC.8's identification.
Constructs the finite and infinite Shimura towers with their group actions and level changes, the tower models CC.8 identifies with the generic completed object.
Proves torsion-freeness and finiteness of modular-curve cohomology after localising at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, the finite-level form of CC.8's localisation at a residual Hecke ideal.

targets.target: GL₂ over local fields and over 𝔸_F as locally compact groups, specializing the generic restricted-product and reductive-group constructions
targets.note: The ingredients exist. A restricted product of locally compact groups over open subgroups, compact for cofinitely many factors, is locally compact. Units of a locally compact T₁ topological monoid form a locally compact group (an unnamed instance in Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Group/Units.lean), which covers GL₂(F_v) = M₂(F_v)ˣ. Finite completions of a number field are nonarchimedean local fields (Tau Ceti). GL₂(𝔸_F) is not assembled as a topological group, and `RestrictedProduct.unitsEquiv` is only a monoid isomorphism, not a homeomorphism.

targets.target: the chosen compact subgroups GL₂(𝒪_v), O(2) and U(2), and the adelic congruence subgroups K₀(N) and K₁(N), with their Iwasawa and Cartan decompositions
targets.note: Compactness of GL₂(𝒪_v) follows from Mathlib's compact 𝒪_v and compact submonoid units, and Tau Ceti proves unitary groups compact (so O(n), U(n)). The classical analogues are there: Γ₀(N), Γ₁(N) ≤ SL₂(ℤ), Smith normal form over ℤ (a Cartan decomposition for integer matrices), and the NA-section of SL₂(ℝ) → ℍ. targets.target: Central character and translation/modulation relations with the chosen Fourier convention

targets.note: Tau Ceti has newforms with multiplicity one and strong multiplicity one classically, the level-raising operator V_d (TauCeti.CuspForm.levelRaise) and the classical U_p at primes dividing the level, which are the ingredients of a p-stabilization f(z) - beta f(pz); but no p-stabilization is constructed, its U_p-eigenvalue is not computed, and there is no family to specialize.

targets.target: Fitting decomposition of a finite module under an endomorphism U into eventually invertible image and eventually killed kernel
targets.note: Mathlib proves the Fitting decomposition M = ker(f^n) ⊕ range(f^n) for large n, and M = (sup_n ker f^n) ⊕ (inf_n range f^n), for an endomorphism of a module over a ring that is [IsArtinian R M] and [IsNoetherian R M] — strictly more general than L0a's 'finite underlying module', which is both. The file has no sorry. That U restricts to a bijection of the stable image is not an exported lemma (it appears only as a step inside a proof in LinearAlgebra/Eigenspace/Zero.lean), but it follows in a few lines from the decomposition and IsArtinian.bijective_of_injective_endomorphism.

targets.target: U^(n!) eventually constant with value the projector e; e² = e, U-equivariance and naturality

targets.target: The profinite projector: e as the inverse limit of finite projectors over M = lim M/J, with pointwise convergence of U^(n!), continuity, image/kernel decomposition, invertibility on eM and topological nilpotence on (1-e)M

targets.target: Exactness of e for U-equivariant exact sequences of finite modules, then for inverse-limit sequences under Mittag-Leffler/compact-surjectivity hypotheses
targets.note: Mathlib has the Mittag-Leffler condition only for Type-valued cofiltered systems, where it is used for nonemptiness of sections, surjectivity of limit projections for towers of surjections, and exactness of I-adic completion on finite modules over a Noetherian ring (AdicCompletion.map_exact, proved without Mittag-Leffler systems); there is no exactness theorem for inverse limits of modules under Mittag-Leffler hypotheses (lim^1 is absent) and nothing about an ordinary projector.

targets.target: The compact U_p action on affinoid distribution-valued modular cohomology

targets.target: Partition functions and restricted partition families
targets.note: Partitions of a natural number are a finite type in Mathlib with the odd, distinct and part-restricted subfamilies; the file is sorry-free.

targets.target: Generating products for partition counts, as formal power series
targets.note: Mathlib builds the generating function attached to an arbitrary character f(i, c) of a part and its multiplicity and proves it equals the infinite product prod_i (1 + sum_j f(i,j) X^{ij}) in the X-adic topology; the specializations to restricted and count-restricted partitions are proved in Glaisher.lean. The module docstring records that the specialization giving the unrestricted partition function p(n) itself is still a TODO, so the classical product formula for sum p(n) q^n is not yet a named theorem (it is the always-true case of hasProd_powerSeriesMk_card_restricted). Mathlib also proves Euler's pentagonal number theorem prod_n (1 - X^(n+1)) = sum_k (-1)^k X^(k(3k-1)/2) in R[[X]] for any commutative ring (PowerSeries.WithPiTopology.tprod_one_sub_X_pow).

targets.target: Coefficientwise finiteness of infinite products and specialization maps
targets.note: Coefficientwise finiteness is proved in general: a product prod_i (1 + f_i) of power series whose orders tend to infinity is multipliable in the X-adic (pi) topology (PowerSeries.WithPiTopology.multipliable_one_add_of_tendsto_order_atTop_nhds_top, with a multivariable version for MvPowerSeries), and the partition products are instances of it. PowerSeries.subst and PowerSeries.rescale give the formal specialization maps. Analytic evaluation is kept separate, as the acceptance clause requires: Mathlib proves the pentagonal identity again for the Euler function at |x| < 1 in a complete normed ring (eulerFunction_eq_tprod).

targets.target: Theta functions with their transformation law and branch choice
targets.note: Mathlib proves theta(S.tau) = (-I tau)^(1/2) theta(tau) with the principal branch and theta(T^2.tau) = theta(tau), i.e. the half-integral-weight law at the two generators of the theta group, together with the two-variable functional equation and quasi-periodicity. Neither library has the multiplier system of theta on the whole theta group or on Gamma_0(4) as a function with its cocycle law, a half-integral-weight automorphy factor, or the behaviour of theta at cusps other than infinity, and the layer asks for theta functions with their multiplier systems matched to the metaplectic convention.

targets.target: The Dedekind eta function with its multiplier system
targets.note: eta is defined as q^(1/24) prod (1 - q^(n+1)), proved nonvanishing and differentiable on the upper half-plane, with logDeriv eta = E2 up to the standard constant and the S-transformation eta(-1/z) = (sqrt I)^(-1) sqrt z eta(z); Delta = eta^24 is a level-one cusp form of weight 12 with S- and T-invariance and first q-coefficient 1. Missing is the multiplier system of eta on all of SL_2(Z) (no Dedekind sums exist in either library: grep -rn -i 'dedekind sum' returns nothing) and any eta quotient of higher level.

targets.target: Jacobi forms with multiplier systems, weights and indices
targets.note: The two-variable theta function exists as an analytic function with its functional equation and its quasi-periodicity theta_2(z + tau, tau) = exp(-pi i (tau + 2z)) theta_2(z, tau) (jacobiTheta₂_add_left'), the elliptic law of this one function; but there is no definition of a Jacobi form, no index, and no elliptic transformation law for a general Jacobi form; grep -rn -i 'jacobi form' over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Cusp behaviour verified at every cusp
targets.note: Mathlib has cusps of a congruence subgroup and the vanishing condition at all of them in the definition of CuspForm, and Delta is shown to vanish at infinity; but for theta and eta only the behaviour at infinity and under the named generators is proved.

targets.target: The Hardy-Ramanujan asymptotic for p(n)
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'hardy.?ramanujan' over both trees returns nothing; there is no asymptotic for the partition function in either library.

targets.note: grep -rn -i 'kloosterman' over both trees returns nothing. Mathlib has Gauss sums over finite fields, which are a different exponential sum, and no Weil bound for Kloosterman sums.

targets.note: No Bessel function is defined in either library, and nothing is proved about the Rademacher series. targets.target: Effective error terms and the distinction between truncated approximations and the infinite identity

targets.target: Growth conditions and the holomorphic/nonholomorphic Fourier parts of a harmonic weak Maass form
targets.note: No non-holomorphic modular object exists in either library; Mathlib's ModularForm requires holomorphy. targets.note: Mathlib has holomorphic Eisenstein series at level one and for congruence subgroups, which are the Poincare series of index m = 0; general Poincare series and the Bruinier-Funke duality are absent.

targets.target: Indefinite theta functions in the sense of Zwegers

targets.note: grep -rn -i 'appell|lerch' over both trees returns nothing mathematical for this construction.

targets.note: grep -rn -i 'moonshine' over both trees returns nothing; there is no modular j-function, no hauptmodul and no genus-zero statement in either library.

targets.target: Eisenstein series with character E_k^{psi,phi,t} in M_k(N, psi phi), their q-expansions via generalized Bernoulli numbers and twisted divisor sums, E2(z) - t E2(tz), weight one, and the Gauss-sum translation to Mathlib's eisensteinSeries
targets.note: Mathlib has the level-Gamma(N) congruence-class series in weight k >= 3, the level-one q-expansion, E2 and Gauss sums, and Tau Ceti has the twisted divisor sums; missing are the character-twisted series in M_k(N, psi phi), generalized Bernoulli numbers B_{k,chi}, their q-expansions at level N, the weight-2 combination E2(z) - tE2(tz), weight-one Eisenstein series, and the Gauss-sum comparison.

targets.target: Cusp-Eisenstein decomposition M_k(N,chi) = S_k(N,chi) + E_k(N,chi): constant-term maps at all cusps, their common kernel, spanning by Eisenstein series, dimension of the Eisenstein subspace

targets.target: Abscissa of absolute convergence <= k/2 + 1 for cusp forms and <= k + 1 for modular forms of weight k >= 0, and the sharpening <= k for non-cusp forms
targets.note: Both proved bounds exist on arithmetic subgroups (Hecke's a_n = O(n^{k/2}) and a_n = O(n^k) for k >= 0 are Mathlib's). The tightened non-cuspidal abscissa <= k (a_n = O(n^{k-1}) resp. O(n^{k-1+eps})) is absent.

targets.target: Completed L-function via the Mellin transform of f(iy), Hecke's functional equation with the Fricke companion Lambda_N(k - s, f) = i^k Lambda_N(s, g), entireness and analytic continuation of L(s,f)

For a non-cusp form Mathlib's L = Lambda * 2/Gamma_C is still defined on all of C and, by WeakFEPair.differentiableAt_Λ, is differentiable away from s = 0 and s = k, although no modular-form lemma records this. Missing: the level-N completed Lambda_N and the stated equation with the normalized Fricke companion.

targets.target: Period map S_k(Gamma1(N)) -> Hom_Z(M N k, C): raw geodesic pairing, absolute convergence between cusps, Gamma1(N)-invariance, descent, Hecke and diamond equivariance

There is no pairing on Div^0 tensor Sym^{k-2}, no Gamma1(N)-invariance or descent, no period polynomials or cocycles, and no Hecke or diamond equivariance.

targets.target: Injectivity of the period map via the Eichler integral and Bol's identity, including 'bounded invariant function of weight <= 0 is constant'
targets.note: Mathlib proves that modular forms of weight 0 on arithmetic groups are constant and of negative weight vanish (the named sub-theorem once E_f is shown holomorphic and bounded at the cusps), and the slash rule for the normalized derivative; the Eichler integral, the iterated Bol identity and the injectivity theorem are absent.

targets.target: Integral Hecke algebra heckeAlgZ N k (generated by T_n and diamonds) is a finitely generated Z-module, via the free-algebra kernel inclusion
targets.note: The image of the integral Gamma0(N) Hecke ring in End(S_k(N,chi)) is available as a ring hom, but nothing is proved about Z-finiteness of any Hecke algebra (only C-finite-dimensionality of the form spaces).

targets.target: Hecke eigenvalues are algebraic integers and CoefficientField f = Q(a_n) is a number field (k >= 2; weight one via the Deligne-Serre lattice)

targets.target: Vanishing S_k = 0 for k <= 0

targets.target: Twists f tensor psi by Dirichlet characters (modularity, level bound, nebentypus chi psi^2, a_p(f tensor psi) = psi(p)a_p(f)), primitive associates, inner twists and CM self-twists
targets.note: Only the twist by a trivial character exists: Tau Ceti's coprime filter (Miyake Lemma 4.6.5) takes f in S_k(Gamma1(N), chi) and L != 0 whose primes all divide N to a cusp form of level rad(L)*N with nebentypus chi whose q-expansion is a_n(f) for (n, L) = 1 and 0 otherwise, which is f twisted by the trivial character mod L. Missing are twists by nontrivial Dirichlet characters (level bound, nebentypus chi psi^2, a_p(f tensor psi) = psi(p)a_p(f)), primitive associates, inner twists and CM self-twists; every other 'twist' in the modular-forms trees is the slash action or a nebentypus-weighted Hecke sum.

targets.note: The discriminant test (monic separable, char != 2), normal closures, full-symmetric-group criteria (prime degree with two non-real roots; transposition plus transitivity in Equiv.Perm) and Frobenius-orbit sizes over finite fields exist; Dedekind's theorem that the factorization mod p gives a Frobenius cycle type in Gal(f/Q), and the certificate checker, are absent.

targets.note: Holomorphic functions on a compact preconnected complex manifold are constant (H^0(X,O) = C); Mathlib's smoothSheafCommRing, taken over C, is the sheaf of holomorphic functions of any complex manifold (its docstring calls it the structure sheaf, and ChartedSpace.locallyRingedSpace makes the manifold a locally ringed space); and Mathlib has a Cech complex functor and Ext-based sheaf cohomology. There are no divisor sheaves O_D, no Leray theorem and no dbar-lemma (Tau Ceti's holomorphicSheaf lives on C).

targets.target: Hurwitz class numbers H(D) by weighted counts of reduced positive-definite binary quadratic forms, with H 0 = -1/12 and the values H 3 = 1/3, H 4 = 1/2, H 7 = 1, H 8 = 1
targets.note: Neither library has reduction theory or class numbers of binary quadratic forms (hits for 'binary quadratic form' are positivity lemmas and a Legendre-symbol section); only ideal class numbers of number fields exist.

targets.target: Weight polynomials P_k(t,n) with generating function 1/(1 - tx + nx^2), the root-quotient formula and the relation with Chebyshev U
targets.note: The Dickson polynomials of the second kind satisfy exactly the P_k recurrence (dickson 2 n (k-2) evaluated at t is P_k(t,n)) and are related to Chebyshev U in Mathlib. For n = 1, where dickson 2 1 is Chebyshev S, Mathlib also has the root-quotient formula in trigonometric form, S_m(2 cos theta) sin theta = sin((m+1) theta) for complex theta, and the boundary values S_m(2) = m + 1 and S_m(-2) = (-1)^m (m + 1). Missing are the generating function, and the root-quotient formula and boundary value for general n.

targets.note: No period polynomials, Eichler-Shimura maps or SL2(Z)-action on homogeneous polynomials in either library.

targets.target: Popa-Zagier machinery: determinant-n matrix module and group ring with PSL2(Z) actions, the element T-tilde_n with its period and exchange relations, trace reduction and the conjugacy-type contributions
targets.note: Only double-coset Hecke rings exist; no group ring of determinant-n matrices and no Manin/Choie-Zagier elements.

targets.note: Only disc(A) = tr^2 - 4 det for 2x2 matrices.

targets.note: a_1(Delta) = 1 and dim S_12 = 1 exist; tau(2) = -24, Delta as a Hecke eigenform and the traces are absent.

targets.target: Sumsets, difference sets and iterated sumsets of finite sets
targets.note: Pointwise operations are stated multiplicatively with @[to_additive], giving Finset.add, Finset.sub and the iterated sumset n • s (scoped in Pointwise), with cardinality bounds such as card_add_le.

targets.target: Additive energy and the basic energy inequalities
targets.note: The additive versions are Finset.addEnergy (notation E[s,t]), the Cauchy-Schwarz bound #s^2 #t^2 <= #(s+t) E[s,t] (le_card_add_mul_addEnergy) and the representation-count formula; the trivial upper bound E(A,B) <= |A|^2|B| is not stated.

targets.target: Convolution and Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups (characters, inversion, Parseval/Plancherel, convolution to product), with normalized counting measure
targets.note: Characters of a finite abelian group form a basis with orthogonality, the discrete Fourier transform with inversion exists on ZMod N, Finset.expect gives normalized averages, and the representation-count convolution of finsets exists (additive name addConvolution). Parseval and the expansion formula exist for every compact group through Tau Ceti's Peter-Weyl basis of L^2(haarProb G) (hasSum_norm_sq_peterWeylCoeff, hasSum_peterWeyl_expansion), and on a finite discrete group haarProb is the normalized counting measure (haarProb_eq_smul_count); convolution of functions is Mathlib's DiscreteConvolution.convolution (additive addConvolution) or MeasureTheory.convolution. Missing are a character-indexed Fourier transform on general finite abelian groups with Parseval stated for characters, and the identity taking convolution to the product of transforms.

targets.target: Plunnecke-Ruzsa inequality, Ruzsa triangle inequality and Ruzsa covering

targets.target: Homotopy-equivalence and quasi-isomorphism API for bounded complexes of finite projective modules
targets.note: Mathlib proves, in any abelian category, that a cochain complex of projectives which is bounded above is K-projective, and that a morphism between K-projective complexes is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when it is a homotopy equivalence (with the ℕ-indexed chain-complex form). ModuleCat over a complete Noetherian local O-algebra is a special case (the derived category is available through the `HasDerivedCategory.standard` construction, not an instance), so this API should be consumed; only finiteness bookkeeping is specific to the layer.

targets.target: Perfect complexes, defined through local finite projective resolutions
targets.note: No perfect complex, `Perf` subcategory or pseudo-coherence notion exists in either tree; 'perfect complex' occurs in no Lean file of Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

targets.target: Minimal representatives over a local ring and their uniqueness up to homotopy
targets.note: Only two-term pieces exist: Tau Ceti's minimal projective presentations P₁ → P₀ → M → 0 (projective cover plus superfluous kernel, image in the radical, unique up to isomorphism; existence over semiprimary rings), and Mathlib's freeness of finite flat modules over a local ring and the minimal number of generators as the dimension modulo m. Minimal complexes of arbitrary length over a local ring, and uniqueness of minimal representatives up to homotopy, are absent.

targets.target: Tor-amplitude, kept distinct from the amplitude of a chosen complex and from the degrees of nonzero cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib has the canonical t-structure on the derived category, with `IsLE`/`IsGE` characterised by vanishing of cohomology (the degrees of nonzero cohomology), and shows an object with cohomology in [a,b] is represented by a complex strictly concentrated in [a,b] (the amplitude of a chosen complex). Tor-amplitude, flat dimension and Tor dimension are absent from both trees.

targets.target: Duals of complexes and the derived tensor product
targets.note: Mathlib has the tensor product of homological complexes and Tor as left-derived functors of the tensor product; Tau Ceti makes cochain complexes of R-modules a symmetric monoidal category with the Koszul sign and builds the R-linear Hom complex. There is no derived tensor product or RHom on the derived category, and no duality theory for perfect complexes.

targets.target: Derived completion, derived Nakayama and specialisation/extension under derived completeness and finiteness
targets.note: Neither library has derived completeness or a derived Nakayama lemma; Mathlib's Nakayama lemmas are for modules only.

targets.target: Spectral sequence Tor_i^A(H^j(C),B) ⇒ H^{j−i}(C⊗ᴸ_A B) and its convergence
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the spectral sequence of a spectral object in an abelian category (with first- and third-quadrant E₂ versions) and the spectral object attached to a filtered complex in the homotopy category. No Tor or base-change spectral sequence is constructed, and the derived tensor product it abuts to is missing.

targets.target: Finite coefficient quotients before inverse limits: derived Mittag-Leffler comparisons and a retained lim¹
targets.note: Mathlib's Mittag-Leffler condition is stated for cofiltered systems of types (eventual ranges); an ℕ-indexed system with surjective transition maps has a limit mapping onto each stage; adic completion of finite modules over a Noetherian ring is exact. There is no lim¹, derived inverse limit or Milnor sequence, and no Mittag-Leffler theory for systems of modules or complexes.

targets.target: Morphisms, homotopies and Hecke actions compatible through the inverse system at chain level
targets.note: Nothing in either library about compatible chain-level actions on inverse systems of complexes.

targets.target: One-degree module theorem as a specialisation; integral support versus support after inverting p
targets.note: Mathlib relates module support to localisation (M[1/f] = 0 iff Supp M ⊆ V(f)) and to quotients (Supp(M/IM) = Supp M ∩ V(I) for finite M). targets.note: Ingredients exist: additivity of length and length along flat local extensions (Mathlib); in Tau Ceti, the Euler–Poincaré identity for any additive invariant on a strictly bounded complex, length(I/aI) = ord(a), and the decomposition of a module by a complete family of orthogonal idempotents. Derived actions of a finite algebra in D(S), their idempotent localisation, the length-valued Euler characteristic of a perfect complex modulo f, the generic-length formula and excellent rings are absent.

targets.target: The coefficient categories: Artinian local O-algebras with residue field k, and complete Noetherian local O-algebras with local continuous morphisms
targets.note: Every ingredient predicate exists, but neither library bundles them into a category with a fixed residue-field identification.

targets.target: Presentation of a complete local ring as the inverse limit of its Artinian quotients
targets.note: Mathlib proves the ingredients: an I-adically complete ring is its completion, with the universal property that compatible maps into all R/I^n lift uniquely (`IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom`, `eq_liftRingHom`); every Artinian quotient of a local ring contains a power of the maximal ideal, so the powers are cofinal; and R/I is Artinian when m is minimal over I in a Noetherian local ring. The single statement 'R is the limit of its Artinian quotients' in a coefficient category is not packaged.

targets.target: Continuous homomorphisms out of power-series rings into complete local rings, with uniqueness
targets.note: For a complete Hausdorff linearly topologised target S, a continuous coefficient map and elements that are topologically nilpotent and tend to zero, `eval₂Hom` is the continuous ring map out of `MvPowerSeries σ R`, and `eval₂_unique`/`aeval_unique` give uniqueness among continuous maps. A complete Noetherian local O-algebra with its m-adic topology satisfies these hypotheses.

targets.target: Completed tensor products over O, with the exact conditions under which they stay Noetherian and local
targets.note: No completed tensor product A ⊗̂_O B exists. Mathlib compares completion of a finite module with base change along the completed Noetherian ring and proves the completion of a local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal is local and complete; it has no theorem that the adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian (Tau Ceti has this only for strongly Noetherian Huber rings).

targets.target: Residue-field extension of the coefficient ring
targets.note: Residue fields, their functoriality and invariance under completion exist; W(k) is a p-adically complete DVR for a perfect field k of characteristic p; a finite étale extension of local rings has rank equal to its residue degree. The change of coefficients O → O' realising a given residue-field extension (the unramified extension of a complete DVR) is not constructed.

targets.target: Descent and ascent of finite generation along these maps
targets.note: The engine of topological Nakayama is in Mathlib: for M I-adically precomplete and N I-adically Hausdorff, a linear map that is surjective modulo I is surjective (no finiteness assumed). Also: finiteness modulo a finitely generated nilpotent kernel lifts, the span criterion modulo m for finite modules over a local ring, and transitivity. The statements in the layer's form (a complete local O-algebra, or a complete separated module, that is finite modulo the maximal ideal is finite) are not stated.

targets.target: APIs for nilpotent ideals, small extensions and square-zero extensions
targets.note: Mathlib has induction from nilpotent to square-zero ideals, the trivial square-zero extension, the bijection between lifts across a square-zero ideal and derivations, extensions of algebras and formally smooth lifting along square-zero ideals. Small extensions of Artinian local rings (surjections with principal kernel killed by the maximal ideal) are absent.

targets.target: Schlessinger's criterion in the form used for unframed deformation functors
targets.note: No functors on Artinian local algebras and no representability criterion in either tree; 'Schlessinger' occurs nowhere.

targets.target: Framed representability construction
targets.note: No deformation functors or deformation rings exist in either library.

targets.target: Tangent-space finiteness
targets.note: The representable case is present in pieces: the cotangent space m/m² of a local ring with dimension equal to the minimal number of generators of m (finite-dimensional for Noetherian rings), Tau Ceti's identification of dual-number points over a given point with derivations, and finiteness of the cotangent space of an augmented algebra. The tangent space F(k[ε]) of a general deformation functor and its finiteness are absent.

targets.target: Fibre products of Artinian local rings and the Schlessinger conditions on F(A×_C B) → F(A)×_{F(C)}F(B)
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the fibre product of ring and algebra maps and proves it is local when one factor is local and the other map is a local homomorphism. It does not prove the fibre product of Artinian rings is Artinian, and the Schlessinger conditions are absent.

targets.target: Hulls versus prorepresenting objects, and uniqueness of hulls
targets.note: No hulls, versal or prorepresentable functors on Artinian algebras (Mathlib's 'prorepresentability' concerns Galois categories).

targets.target: Presentation relations related to obstruction spaces
targets.note: Mathlib has the naive cotangent complex of a presentation, its first homology and the Jacobi–Zariski sequence, which measure the relations of a presentation, but no obstruction theory for deformation functors and no bound on relations by an obstruction space.

duplicates.note: Existence of universal framed rings and of unframed rings under absolute irreducibility, and the framed/unframed comparison by power-series maps.

Framed local representability with its tangent/obstruction description.
Pro-representability on Artinian local W(k)-algebras with residue field k, and a parameter criterion for generators of the maximal ideal of the prorepresenting ring.

targets.target: Regular sequences
targets.note: Weakly regular and regular sequences on modules over a commutative ring, with permutation, quotient, localisation and flat base-change lemmas.

targets.target: Depth
targets.note: Mathlib proves Rees' theorem (Noetherian R, finite M with IM ≠ M: an M-regular sequence of length n in I exists iff Ext^i(R/I, M) = 0 for i < n) but defines no depth invariant; `RegularSequence.lean` lists depth as a TODO.

targets.target: Cohen–Macaulay rings and modules
targets.note: No Cohen–Macaulay (or maximal Cohen–Macaulay, Gorenstein local) predicate in either tree.

targets.target: Projective dimension
targets.note: Projective dimension in abelian categories, with pd(M/xM) = pd(M)+1 for M-regular x in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring and pd_R(R/(x₁,…,x_n)) = n for a regular sequence (stated for `ModuleCat.{v} R` with `[Small.{v} R]`).

targets.target: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula
targets.note: Absent; 'Auslander' occurs only in Tau Ceti's Auslander–Reiten theory for Artin algebras.

targets.target: Complete-intersection criteria used in patching
targets.note: No complete-intersection predicate for local rings in either tree.

targets.target: Depth and dimension formulas under the local maps used
targets.note: The dimension half is largely present: ht(P) = ht(p) + ht(P/pS) under going-down (Matsumura 13.B Th. 19), and flat algebras have going-down, which gives dim B = dim A + dim B/m_A B for flat local maps; quotienting by a regular sequence drops dimension by its length. For power series only dim R + 1 ≤ dim R[[X]] is proved (`ringKrullDim_succ_le_ringKrullDim_powerseries`), and no depth formula exists.

targets.target: Equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules
targets.note: Associated primes (finitely many for finite modules over Noetherian rings), support, support dimension and the bijection between minimal primes and irreducible components of Spec are in Mathlib; equidimensionality is not defined.

targets.target: Catenarity and excellence as explicit hypotheses
targets.note: No catenary or excellent ring predicate in either tree; a Tau Ceti docstring records the absence of `IsExcellent`.

targets.target: Finite-over-a-subring criteria of KW II §10 and their completed versions

targets.target: Inverse-limit patching of finite-level rings, modules, presentations and transition data, with the compactness or diagonal-subsequence argument
targets.note: No patching construction in either tree. The abstract compactness principle (sections of a cofiltered system of nonempty finite sets) is in Mathlib.

targets.note: Absent.

targets.note: Absent; the depth comparison also lacks a depth invariant.

targets.target: Integral assertions kept separate from those after inverting π

targets.target: The abstract patching theorem with all numerical hypotheses and the faithfulness/support conclusion actually obtained
targets.note: Absent.

Constructs a patched completed module with finite generation and support assertions.

targets.target: Support transport along flat maps, coefficient changes, quotient maps and removal of framing variables
targets.note: Mathlib has the inclusion of the support over an algebra in the preimage of the support over the base, Supp(M/IM) = Supp M ∩ V(I) for finite M, vanishing after inverting f in terms of support, and monotonicity under surjections. The base-change formula Supp(B ⊗_A M) = preimage of Supp M along flat or finite maps, and anything about framing variables, are absent.

targets.target: When a patched module is faithful, nearly faithful or supported on a specified union of components
targets.note: Faithfulness as vanishing of the annihilator and minimal primes as irreducible components exist; near faithfulness and the patched support-on-components criteria do not.

targets.target: An explicit algebraic theorem for the torsion-free/reduced quotient at which R=T concludes, and a stronger theorem under extra hypotheses
targets.note: Radicals and the reduced quotient by a radical ideal exist; the R=T conclusions are absent.

duplicates.note: Same roadmap: the complex-level component-support transport, near faithfulness and union-of-components conclusions.

States when the generic-fibre or integral R=T statement strengthens, the arithmetic form of R03.6's last target.
Support and multiplicity assertions for patched modules.

targets.target: The multiplicative monoid generated by Φ_n(q), n ∈ S, ordered by divisibility, and its directedness
targets.note: Cyclotomic polynomials over any ring (monic, defined by base change from ℤ) and generated submonoids exist; the directed monoid used as an index set is not constructed.

targets.target: R[q]^S as the inverse limit of the quotients R[q]/(f), with projections, compatible quotient maps, independence of representatives and the dense polynomial map
targets.note: The generic constructions exist: the linear topology on a ring defined by a filter of ideals, its separated completion, limits of commutative rings, and (Tau Ceti) all small limits of complete Hausdorff topological commutative rings. R[q]^S itself, its projections and its identification of the completion with lim R[q]/(f) are not constructed; nothing named Habiro exists in either tree.

targets.target: Completeness, separatedness, extensionality by finite quotients and the universal property for continuous maps to complete separated rings
targets.note: The universal property of the separated completion of a topological ring (existence, and uniqueness in Tau Ceti) and the adic-complete lifting property exist in general; they are not specialised to R[q]^S or to its finite quotients.

targets.target: Injectivity of R[q] → R[q]^S only under hypotheses on R and S
targets.note: Tau Ceti identifies the kernel of A → Â with the closure of 0, the general tool for such injectivity statements; the cyclotomic-completion statements and their hypotheses are absent.

targets.target: For S = ℕ_{>0}: cofinality of P_N(q) = ∏_{i≤N}(1−q^i), identification with lim_N R[q]/(P_N) and with the (q^m−1)-completions, counting cyclotomic multiplicities
targets.note: q^n − 1 = ∏_{d|n} Φ_d over any ring (the input for the multiplicity count), equality of topologies from mutually cofinal submodule bases (Tau Ceti) and lifting from a cofinal subsequence of powers in the adic case exist. P_N(q) has no carrier (Mathlib lists q-Pochhammer symbols as a TODO) and the cofinality and limit comparisons are absent.

targets.target: Continuous functoriality in R, contravariant restriction in S, identity and composition laws, equivalences for cofinal systems, and completed versus uncompleted base change
targets.note: Functoriality of completion, the cofinal-bases principle and the Noetherian finite comparison of adic completion with base change exist; the statements for cyclotomic completions do not.

targets.target: Representatives successively modulo P_N and a convergent factorial expansion ∑ a_N(q)P_N(q) of every compatible element
targets.note: No factorial expansion exists; only the general convergence criterion in complete nonarchimedean groups (multiplicative form cited; the additive form is generated from it).

targets.target: Normalised degree-bounded expansion by division by monic polynomials, with existence and uniqueness
targets.note: Division with remainder by a monic polynomial over any commutative ring, with the degree bound and uniqueness, is in Mathlib and each P_N is monic; the normalised expansion built from it is not stated.

targets.target: Addition, multiplication and coefficient-extraction algorithms on normalised expansions, each with a congruence correctness theorem and finite-precision dependence
targets.note: Tau Ceti has executable, proved-correct arithmetic modulo a monic polynomial (synthetic division on coefficient lists) and exact ℤ[q]/(Φ_e) arithmetic; algorithms on factorial expansions of Habiro-ring elements are absent.

targets.target: q is invertible in the Habiro ring, its inverse at finite precision, and the comparison of polynomial and Laurent-polynomial constructions

duplicates.note: Also proves q invertible in the completed coefficient ring and warns against confusing completion with inverting q^m − 1.
Builds finite truncations of cyclotomic (q;q)_n expansions and proves coefficient compatibility before passing to the completion.

targets.target: Evaluation at a root ζ of order d ∈ S into R[ζ] through a finite quotient, independent of the truncation
targets.note: R[q]/(Φ_d) as `AdjoinRoot`, Φ_d as the minimal polynomial of a primitive root over ℤ, and Tau Ceti's exact ℤ[ζ_e] identified with `AdjoinRoot Φ_e` exist; evaluation out of the completion does not.

targets.target: The Taylor map into R[ζ][[q−ζ]] from compatible quotient maps, with constant term the evaluation
targets.note: For polynomials Mathlib has f ↦ f(X + r) as an algebra automorphism whose constant coefficient is f(r); the Taylor map of the completed ring into power series in q − ζ is absent.

targets.target: Higher Taylor coefficients identified with Hasse derivatives, keeping factorial denominators when comparing with ordinary derivatives
targets.note: At polynomial level this is exactly Mathlib: coefficient n of `taylor r f` is (hasseDeriv n f)(r), and n!·hasseDeriv n is the n-th derivative. It should be consumed; only the passage to finite quotients and the completion is missing.

targets.target: Naturality under coefficient change, root conjugation, order restriction and q ↦ q^a
targets.note: Coefficient change for Hasse derivatives and cyclotomic polynomials and the substitution q ↦ q^p on cyclotomic polynomials exist at polynomial level; completed versions do not.

targets.target: p-adic re-expansion maps, defined through topological nilpotence in a complete coefficient ring, with their cocycle law
targets.note: Mathlib's substitution into power series requires exactly the nilpotence hypothesis the layer insists on and proves composition of substitutions; the specific re-expansions and their cocycle identity are absent.

Root-of-unity choices, change-of-choice invariance and convergence of the p-adic substitutions in the Taylor presentation of the relative ring.
Takes the Taylor expansion at q = 1 (the Ohtsuki series) and root-of-unity evaluations of one completed element.

targets.note: Module completion with functoriality and finite products exists for a single ideal (adic case) only; completion of modules along a directed family of cyclotomic ideals is absent.

targets.target: Hypotheses for exactness of the module completion, or a derived-limit correction
targets.note: Exactness of adic completion on finite modules over Noetherian rings and the Mittag-Leffler condition for systems of types exist; there is no lim¹ or derived-limit correction.

targets.target: Extension of the connectedness/injectivity theorem using p-adic separation of M (Habiro §7.3)

targets.target: gcd, Bézout identity and the (extended) Euclidean algorithm
targets.note: The extended Euclidean algorithm is computable (`Nat.xgcd`, `EuclideanDomain.xgcd` under `[DecidableEq R]`) and Bézout holds in every Euclidean domain and Bézout domain; `Nat.gcd` itself is in core Lean.

targets.target: Prime factorization: existence and uniqueness
targets.note: For ℕ as a list of primes or a finsupp (`n ≠ 0`), and up to associates in any UFD; every PID is a UFD (instance).

targets.target: Congruences and residue rings
targets.note: Congruence on ℕ and ℤ, the ring ZMod n with its dictionary to congruences, Euler–Fermat, and congruence modulo a submodule.

targets.target: Chinese remainder theorem for coprime moduli and pairwise-coprime families
targets.note: Computable ℕ versions for two moduli and finite families, the ring isomorphism ZMod (mn) ≃ ZMod m × ZMod n, and the ideal-theoretic CRT for pairwise comaximal ideals of any commutative ring.

targets.target: Chinese remainder theorem at non-coprime moduli with the compatibility hypothesis a ≡ b mod gcd(m,n)
targets.note: `Nat.chineseRemainder'` takes exactly the hypothesis `a ≡ b [MOD gcd n m]` and returns a solution below lcm(n,m); uniqueness mod lcm holds over ℕ and ℤ. Stated for natural-number residues (a public ℤ-existence form and the fibre-product form R/(I∩J) ≅ R/I ×_{R/(I+J)} R/J are not stated).

targets.target: p-adic valuations, multiplicities and Legendre's formula for factorials
targets.note: Valuations on ℕ, ℤ and ℚ, multiplicity in any monoid, Legendre's formula in both the sum form and the digit-sum form (p−1)v_p(n!) = n − s_p(n); adic valuations of Dedekind domains are `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation`.

targets.target: Arithmetic functions (σ_k, φ, μ, Λ, ω, Ω, d) and multiplicativity
targets.note: σ_k, μ, Λ, ω (`cardDistinctFactors`), Ω and the divisor count are all defined with their multiplicativity; φ is `Nat.totient` with coprime multiplicativity, though not bundled as an `ArithmeticFunction`. Zero cases follow Mathlib's convention f 0 = 0.

targets.target: Dirichlet convolution and the ring of arithmetic functions
targets.note: Mathlib's convolution is the multiplication of the (commutative) semiring of arithmetic functions, with Dirichlet inverses when f 1 is invertible; Tau Ceti extends convolution to functions on nonzero ideals of a number field.

targets.target: Möbius inversion, instantiated at divisor sums
targets.note: (∀ n > 0, ∑_{d|n} f d = g n) ↔ (∀ n > 0, ∑ μ(x) g(y) = f n) over any ring, with additive-group and multiplicative versions and poset Möbius inversion; Tau Ceti adds ideal Möbius inversion (`TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.convolution_one_eq_iff`).

targets.target: General finite-sum and multiplicative identities for divisor sums
targets.note: ∑_{d|n} φ(d) = n, ζ * pow k = σ_k, ∑_{d|n} Λ(d) = log n and multiplicativity of divisor sums over coprime factors are all proved.

targets.target: Finite cyclic groups, cyclicity of (ℤ/n)ˣ and primitive roots
targets.note: (ℤ/n)ˣ is cyclic iff n ∈ {1,2,4,p^k,2p^k} (odd p), finite subgroups of units of a domain are cyclic, and a cyclic group has φ(d) elements of order d. The explicit decomposition of (ℤ/2^k)ˣ into cyclic factors is not stated.

targets.target: Power residues: the n-th power residue criterion and n-th power residue symbols (mod p and in number fields)
targets.note: Only the quadratic case exists (Euler's criterion over ZMod p and finite fields); the number of d-th powers in a cyclic group, the Kummer map with kernel (Kˣ)ⁿ and the Frobenius action σζ = ζ^{N𝔭} are ingredients. Missing: the general criterion a^{(q−1)/gcd(n,q−1)} = 1 and any n-th power residue symbol.

targets.target: Gauss sums and Jacobi sums with their norm and product identities
targets.note: Over any finite commutative ring with a primitive additive character: g(χ,ψ)g(χ⁻¹,ψ⁻¹) = #R for χ ≠ 1, g² = χ(−1)#F for quadratic χ, and J(χ,φ) = g(χ)g(φ)/g(χφ) when χφ ≠ 1. The trivial-character cases are separate lemmas; |g|² = q is two lines from these, not a named lemma.

targets.target: Quadratic reciprocity for Legendre and Jacobi symbols, with the supplementary laws at −1 and 2
targets.note: For distinct odd primes and for odd positive integers (Jacobi), with (−1/p) = χ₄(p) and (2/p) = χ₈(p); Mathlib has no Kronecker symbol (Tau Ceti assembles prime-discriminant characters instead).

targets.target: Residue symbols at 2 and at the infinite places (local Hilbert symbols at 2 and ∞)
targets.note: The dyadic supplementary characters χ₄, χ₈, the sign homomorphism Kˣ → ∏_{real v} {±1} and Br(ℝ) ≅ ℤ/2 exist. Missing: the Hilbert (norm-residue) symbol at 2 or at a real place and the product formula tying the local symbols together.

targets.target: Higher reciprocity through class field theory (cubic, quartic, Eisenstein, general power and Artin reciprocity), with ramified primes excluded
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Artin symbol at unramified primes, the ideal-theoretic Artin map away from S (its kernel and image are not determined), class formations without a reciprocity map, and the Artin map of the genus field of a quadratic field. No cubic, quartic, Eisenstein or general Artin reciprocity law is proved.
