targets.target: Linear recurrences, their relation to companion matrices and eigenvalues (without extending scalars)
targets.note: Mathlib has the solution space of a linear recurrence (≃ initial values), its characteristic polynomial and the geometric solutions from its roots; companion matrices exist only in rank 2 (Tau Ceti). Missing: closed forms with repeated roots, the general companion matrix with charpoly = the recurrence polynomial, and the state-vector/eigenvalue relation.

targets.target: Divisibility sequences: Fibonacci strong divisibility, Lucas sequences U_n(P,Q), elliptic divisibility sequences
targets.note: Fibonacci is a strong divisibility sequence (Mathlib) and Tau Ceti proves Mathlib's TODO that `normEDS b c d` is an elliptic net and a divisibility sequence over any commutative ring. Missing: general Lucas sequences and their strong divisibility, and strong divisibility of EDS.

targets.target: Bernoulli numbers and Euler numbers
targets.note: Bernoulli numbers are complete (both sign conventions, formal generating function over ℚ-algebras, Faulhaber, von Staudt–Clausen, Bernoulli polynomials). Euler numbers (secant/zigzag numbers) are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Binomial identities (Vandermonde, Lucas, Kummer)
targets.note: Vandermonde (also in binomial rings), Lucas's theorem (alias `Choose.lucas_theorem`), Kummer's carry formula for v_p of a binomial coefficient and the binomial theorem in commutative semirings.

targets.target: Rational and formal generating functions (rational power series; generating function of a linear recurrence)
targets.note: Formal power series with inverses, (1−X)^{−d} expansions, the partition product and Catalan functional equation exist, and rational functions embed in Laurent series. Missing: a rationality predicate for power series and the theorem that a sequence satisfies a linear recurrence iff its generating function is P/Q with Q the reversed characteristic polynomial.

targets.target: Radix expansions (integers, reals, p-adics)
targets.note: Base-b digits of naturals with uniqueness and digit-sum congruences, and base-b expansions of reals in [0,1) (existence, no uniqueness statement). p-adic digit expansions ℤ_p ≃ (ℕ → Fin p) are absent.

targets.target: Automatic sequences (k-automatic sequences, automata with output)
targets.note: Only acceptor DFAs exist; there are no automata with output, k-kernels, Thue–Morse or Cobham's theorem in either library.

targets.target: Farey sequences (mediants, neighbour property)
targets.note: Nothing named Farey, mediant, Stern–Brocot or Ford circle; the nearest statement is the determinant identity for consecutive continued-fraction convergents.

targets.target: Combinatorial number families (Catalan, Stirling, Bell, partition numbers, derangements)
targets.note: All named families are defined with their basic closed forms or recursions (Catalan = central binomial/(n+1), Stirling numbers of both kinds, Bell numbers, partition generating function, derangement counts).

targets.target: Christol's theorem (algebraic power series over F_q ↔ p-automatic coefficients)
targets.note: Searched Christol, automatic, and algebraicity of power series over finite fields: nothing in either library.

targets.target: Analytic specializations of formal identities with separate convergence theorems
targets.note: Binet's formula, ζ(2k) and ζ(−n) via Bernoulli numbers, the derangement limit and (Tau Ceti) the convergent Hermite generating function exist. Missing: the convergent Bernoulli generating function z/(e^z−1) for |z| < 2π and a general formal-to-analytic transfer theorem.

targets.target: Integer-valued polynomials (binomial-coefficient basis, Int(ℤ), Pólya's theorem)
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves that the (X choose n) form a basis of K[X] over any ℚ-algebra and a ℤ-basis of their span (closed under multiplication, `TauCeti.mul_mem_ringChooseSpan`), plus integral Newton interpolation; Mathlib has binomial rings and Mahler's basis for C(ℤ_p). Missing: the ring Int(ℤ) itself and Pólya's theorem identifying it with that ℤ-span (a TODO in Mathlib's `Binomial.lean`), and Int(𝓞_K).

targets.target: Irreducibility criteria
targets.note: Eisenstein (prime ideals of domains), Gauss's lemma, the rational root theorem, irreducibility of cyclotomic polynomials over ℚ (and over number fields unramified at q in Tau Ceti), Selmer's X^n−X−1 and Capelli for X^n−a when n is prime, odd, or p^k with p ≠ 2. Not present: Capelli's criterion when 4 | n, and the Perron, Cohn and Newton-polygon criteria.

targets.target: Resultants
targets.note: Sylvester-matrix resultant with the root-product formula for split polynomials, vanishing over a field iff not coprime, the Bézout-type identity and multiplicativity; Tau Ceti identifies the norm in AdjoinRoot g with Res(g,p). Resultants of binary forms are a Mathlib TODO.

targets.target: Discriminants of polynomials
targets.note: Res(f,f′) = ±lc·disc (Mathlib); the root-difference formula over any commutative ring, disc(fg) = disc f·disc g·Res(f,g)², separability over a field iff disc ≠ 0, and reduction mod p separable iff p ∤ disc (Tau Ceti). Trinomial discriminant formulas are absent.

targets.target: Smith normal form with invertible change-of-basis matrices, the reconstruction equation and d_i | d_{i+1}
targets.note: Tau Ceti: for A ∈ M_n(ℤ) with det A ≠ 0 there are L, R ∈ GL_n(ℤ) with LAR = diag(d), d_i | d_j, unique. Mathlib: basis-level Smith form of a submodule of a free module over a PID, without the divisibility chain. Missing: existence for rectangular or singular matrices (uniqueness, `Matrix.smith_normal_form_unique`, already covers singular diagonals), general PIDs, and any algorithm with termination — the existence theorem is an `∃ L R d` statement, not a procedure.

targets.target: Hermite normal form over ℤ
targets.note: Only HNF-shaped coset representatives for Hecke double cosets, row-echelon predicates and Gauss–Jordan elimination over division rings; no existence or uniqueness of Hermite normal form over ℤ.

targets.target: Rational canonical form and invariant factors (of endomorphisms and of finitely generated modules over a PID)
targets.note: The structure theorem is present in elementary-divisor form R^n × ⊕ R/(p_i^{e_i}); rational canonical form exists only for non-scalar 2×2 matrices over a field (Tau Ceti), and invariant factors only for Gram matrices of integral lattices. Missing: the invariant-factor form d_1 | d_2 | … and the rational canonical form in general.

targets.target: Effective ideal arithmetic (ideal bases via HNF, terminating normal-form algorithms)
targets.note: The ideal norm as |det| of a basis change and an existential multivariate division theorem exist; there is no algorithm computing ideal bases, no Gröbner-basis algorithm and no terminating normal-form procedure.

targets.target: Pell equations: nontrivial solutions, fundamental solution, classification of all solutions through units with positivity conventions
targets.note: For d > 0 not a square, solutions of x² − dy² = 1 form the unitary group of ℤ√d, a fundamental solution exists, and every solution is ±a₁ⁿ with a unique positive generator. The negative and generalized Pell equations x² − dy² = −1, N and the continued-fraction algorithm are not classified.

targets.target: Sums of squares: two squares, three squares, four squares, representation counts

targets.target: Elementary descent: x⁴ + y⁴ = z², Fermat for n = 3, 4, Pythagorean triples
targets.note: Infinite descent for x⁴ + y⁴ = z², FLT for exponents 3 and 4 (`fermatLastTheoremThree` is a `public theorem`, missing from the index) and the classification of Pythagorean triples.

targets.target: Source-scoped exponential Diophantine equations (Catalan–Mihăilescu, Ramanujan–Nagell, 2^a − 3^b = ±1, …)
targets.note: Only tools: the lifting-the-exponent lemma and the polynomial (Mason–Stothers) analogue of Catalan/FLT. No exponential equation over ℤ is solved.

targets.target: Routing of genus-one and higher-genus equations to rational-point owners, preserving primitivity and local solubility

targets.target: Linear Diophantine equations and systems
targets.note: Solvability of ax + by = n (over ℤ and Bézout domains) and nonnegative solvability beyond (p−1)(q−1) are proved. The parametrization of all solutions and integer linear systems Ax = b (via Smith form) are absent.

targets.target: Numerical semigroups and Frobenius numbers
targets.note: The Frobenius number of coprime m, n > 1 is mn − m − n, and a Frobenius number exists iff the generators have gcd 1 (and 1 is not a generator). Numerical-semigroup theory (genus, Sylvester's gap count (a−1)(b−1)/2, Apéry sets, symmetry) is absent.

targets.target: Derived I-completeness and the derived completion functor for an I-adically complete coefficient ring Λ with I generated by a regular sequence
targets.note: Mathlib has only classical I-adic completeness and completion of modules (complete when I is finitely generated), regular and weakly regular sequences, and algebraic local cohomology as colim Ext(R/Jᵗ, M). There is no derived-complete object in any derived category, no derived completion functor and no Koszul-complex model.

targets.target: D_ét(X,Λ) for adic Λ: derived I-complete objects of the v-derived category that are étale after derived reduction mod I, distinguished from D_ét of Λ as a discrete ring
targets.note: Only the derived category of an abelian category, sheaf cohomology as Ext on a site and Grothendieck-abelianness of sheaves on the small étale site of a scheme exist. v-sheaves, diamonds and D_ét with any coefficients are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: ECD Proposition 26.2 at the enhanced level: presentability and stability, and equivalence with the limit of the categories for Λ/Iⁿ
targets.note: Mathlib has locally presentable 1-categories and the definition of quasicategories, but no stable or presentable ∞-categories and no limit-of-categories reconstruction.

targets.target: Completed tensor product and completed colimits, with the failure of the uncompleted inclusion to preserve them
targets.note: Only module-level statements: R̂ ⊗_R M ≃ M̂ for R noetherian and M finite, flatness of R̂, and base change of restricted power series over complete noetherian Tate rings. No completed tensor product of complexes or sheaves.

targets.target: Six operations for the adic coefficient system with finite-level compatibility, regular-sequence dévissage for right adjoints and internal Hom, and detection of equivalences modulo I
targets.note: Nakayama-type detection exists for finitely generated modules only (I ⊆ Jacobson radical of an I-adically complete ring). No étale, diamond or adic six-functor formalism exists.

targets.target: Adic forms of the basic theorems for Λ = ℤ_ℓ, I = (ℓ), ℓ ≠ p, and rational ℓ-adic coefficients by a separate localization
targets.note: Mathlib defines Hⁿ(X, ℤ_ℓ) of a scheme only, as pro-étale cohomology of U ↦ C(U, ℤ_ℓ), with no theorems and no comparison with lim Hⁿ(X, ℤ/ℓⁿ); there are no ℚ_ℓ-coefficient categories and nothing for diamonds.

duplicates.note: E4 extends derived adic completion to sheaves and compatible coefficient systems, proves the reconstruction from the categories with coefficients Λ/Iⁿ under the same regular-sequence hypotheses and supplies completed tensor products and colimits; it says L0 only applies this to étale objects.
DD.1 constructs derived I-completeness, the derived completion functor, completed tensor products and completed colimits, the generic module-level targets underlying L0.
C2 defines D_ét for diamonds and proves its presentability and stability, the discrete-coefficient version of the category L0 completes.

targets.target: The small v-sheaf of a characteristic-p scheme via Spa(A, integral closure of F_p in A), independent of the affine cover, functorial and factoring through perfection
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines Spa(A, A⁺) as a set of continuous valuations bounded by 1 on A⁺ and proves it is unchanged when A⁺ is replaced by its integral closure; Mathlib has the perfection of rings with its universal property. There is no v-topology, no v-sheaf or diamond, no gluing of Spa over a scheme and no perfection of schemes.

targets.target: Étale and pro-étale comparison morphisms of sites between the scheme and its v-sheaf
targets.note: Mathlib has the small étale and small pro-étale sites of a scheme, the inequality of the big étale and pro-étale topologies and pushforward along continuous functors, but no morphism of sites to any v-site or diamond site.

targets.target: Mixed-characteristic version over a complete DVR O with perfect residue field: marked untilts over Spa(O,O) with a map of locally ringed spaces to the scheme, and the relative representability statements of ECD 27.5
targets.note: Mathlib has the multiplicative untilt map PreTilt O p → O for p-adically complete O, Fontaine's θ : W(R♭) → R and the abstract notion of a relatively representable functor. Marked untilts as a v-sheaf and the representability statements are absent.

targets.target: Comparison maps between the (k,k) convention and the (k, integral closure of F_p) convention at a residue field, where such maps exist
targets.note: A discrete ring with A⁺ = A is a Huber pair, every valuation on a discrete ring is continuous, and enlarging the plus ring shrinks Spa (so Spa(k,k) ⊆ Spa(k, F̄_p ∩ k) as sets). No comparison of the associated v-sheaves or adic spaces is stated.

duplicates.note: D6 constructs Spd ℤ_p and Spd(A,A⁺) by marked untilts, the same marked-untilt construction L1 uses over Spa(O,O), though D6 restricts to Tate pairs and analytic adic spaces rather than schemes.

targets.target: Noetherian approximation: limits of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps
targets.note: For a given limit cone of a cofiltered diagram of quasi-compact (or qcqs) schemes with affine transition maps, Mathlib proves nonemptiness, quasi-compactness, that affineness of the limit descends to a stage (Stacks 01Z2, 01Z6) and that finite affine covers descend. Missing: the existence of such limits in general and absolute noetherian approximation of a qcqs scheme by finite-type ℤ-schemes (Stacks 01ZA).

targets.target: Finite-presentation descent of morphisms and diagrams to a finite stage, with eventual recognition of properties (separated, proper, closed immersion, étale)
targets.note: Morphisms from the limit to a scheme locally of finite presentation factor through a stage, two stage maps that agree on the limit agree later (finite type), and Hom_S(−, X) turns these limits into colimits. Missing: descent of finitely presented schemes and diagrams themselves (Stacks 01ZM) and eventual separatedness, properness, closed immersion or étaleness; only affineness and quasi-affineness are proved eventually.

targets.target: Étale and cohomological continuity under such limits
targets.note: Only global sections commute with these limits; there is no continuity of étale sites or of étale cohomology (Stacks 09YQ).

targets.target: Reduction of a separated finite-type morphism to a closed immersion into a separated finitely presented morphism
targets.note: Searched the limit and finite-presentation files and the index for embeddings of finite-type morphisms into finitely presented ones (Stacks 09ZP): nothing.

targets.note: The scheme-theoretic image is the closed subscheme cut out by the kernel ideal sheaf, with the factorization of f and its universal property via the ideal-sheaf/kernel adjunction; for quasi-compact f the factor X → image is dominant.

targets.target: Nagata compactification of separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes (nonnoetherian)
targets.note: Searched Nagata, compactification, compactifiable: the only related geometry is Zariski's Main Theorem (proper and locally quasi-finite ⇒ finite; a separated quasi-compact locally quasi-finite morphism locally of finite type is an open immersion into its relative normalization).

targets.target: Compactly supported direct image Rf_! for separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes, by extension by zero and proper pushforward, with independence of compactification, composition, base change and projection formula
targets.note: Only generic pushforward and pullback of sheaves along functors of sites exist; no extension by zero, proper base change or Rf_! for étale sheaves on schemes.

targets.target: Extension from finite coefficient rings by colimit and perfect-complex arguments, and passage to perfections through topological invariance of the étale site
targets.note: Mathlib proves Spec f is a homeomorphism when ker f is nil and every element has a power in the image (Stacks 0BR8), but has no universal homeomorphisms of schemes, no perfection of schemes and no equivalence of étale sites (Stacks 04DY).

targets.target: Orthogonality relations for additive and multiplicative characters

targets.target: Surjectivity (the Tate conjecture for Drinfeld modules / t-motives, Taguchi–Tamagawa)
targets.note: Absent. No analogue of Tate's isogeny theorem exists in either library even for abelian varieties.

targets.target: Semisimplicity of the rational Tate representation
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Taelman's convergent Euler-product L-value for an integral Drinfeld module
targets.note: Mathlib's Euler products are indexed by the primes of ℕ, for multiplicative functions valued in a complete normed field or ring; Tau Ceti adds formal Euler products over the primes of a number field. There is no characteristic-p Goss L-value, no product over the monic irreducibles of A or the closed points of a curve, and no convergence statement in C_∞.

targets.target: The exponential unit lattice U(phi/A) and the finite class module H(phi/A)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Normalized lattice covolume and Fitting polynomial of the class module
targets.note: Absent; Mathlib has no Fitting ideals of modules at all (the only `Fitting` names are Lie-theoretic `posFittingComp`).

targets.target: The determinant / nuclear-operator identity
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Taelman's class-number formula
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti does prove finiteness of the divisor class group and defines a function-field class number (`TauCeti.Divisor.classNumber`, TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/ClassNumber.lean:202), but that is the classical Pic^0, not Taelman's class module, and there is no special-value identity.

targets.target: The chain of vector bundles with Frobenius modification attached to a Drinfeld module (elliptic sheaf)
targets.note: Absent; `grep -rn -i shtuka` and `grep -rn -i 'elliptic sheaf'` return nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Distinguished pole at infinity, characteristic leg and periodicity conditions
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The elliptic-sheaf equivalence with Drinfeld modules in its normalized range
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Prime-to-characteristic Tate realizations, and local-shtuka comparison interfaces
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: DM.7 explicitly exports its construction as the rank-r special case of GS.2's global shtuka stacks; both state the Frobenius-modification definition, and neither is in the libraries.
The local-shtuka and comparison interfaces DM.7 promises are the objects HS2 constructs (local shtuka moduli and bounds); the overlap is the local realization, not the global elliptic sheaf.

targets.target: Neutral Tannakian category of rigid analytically trivial pre-t-motives with its fibre functor
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Tannakian reconstruction in the Hopf-algebra direction — the points functor of a commutative Hopf algebra is isomorphic to the tensor-automorphism functor of its comodule category — but there is no general 'neutral Tannakian category ⇒ affine group scheme' theorem, and no category of t-motives to apply it to.

targets.target: The Frobenius-difference Galois group of a t-motive
targets.note: Absent; there is no difference- or differential-Galois (Picard–Vessiot) theory in either library.

targets.target: The analytic trivialization matrix and the specialization/lifting criterion identifying period transcendence degree with the group dimension
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Algebraic independence of Carlitz logarithms of algebraic arguments under linear independence
targets.note: Mathlib has the algebraic-independence and transcendence-degree API (transcendence bases, `Algebra.trdeg` and its additivity in towers) and Liouville's theorem, but no transcendence theorem for periods or logarithms in any characteristic, and there is no Carlitz logarithm.

duplicates.note: States the same Tannakian package — tensor automorphism groups of a fibre functor, torsors between two fibre functors, pro-algebraic reconstruction and period torsors — for motives rather than for rigid analytically trivial t-motives.

targets.target: One-variable function fields over a base field, as an intrinsic predicate
targets.note: Tau Ceti's intrinsic `IsFunctionField k F` (transcendence degree one plus essential finite type) is proved equivalent to Mathlib's chosen-generator `FunctionField F K`, and is stable under finite extension. No hypothesis that k is finite or perfect.

targets.target: Closed points identified with discrete valuations trivial on the constants
targets.note: `Place k F` is a surjective `Valuation F ℤᵐ⁰` trivial on kˣ; its valuation ring is a DVR and determines the place. The ideal-theoretic dictionary is built: places finite on a Dedekind affine model R correspond to `HeightOneSpectrum R` (`Place.heightOneSpectrumEquiv`), and the places of k(x) are the monic irreducibles plus ∞ (`Place.ratFuncEquiv`). Missing: the projective curve itself, hence the identification of places with its scheme-theoretic closed points.

targets.target: Normalization of a projective model; the contravariant equivalence between one-variable function fields and smooth projective curves over a perfect field
targets.note: The affine half is there: the integral closure of k[x] in F is a Dedekind domain with fraction field F, and its height-one primes correspond to the places not at infinity. Mathlib defines the function field of an integral scheme as the stalk at the generic point. Missing entirely: gluing the two affine normalizations into a projective curve, properness, and the anti-equivalence of categories — there is no `Curve` object in either tree over which to state it.

targets.target: The exact constant field, and its finiteness when k is finite
targets.note: The constant field k̃ = algebraicClosure k F is finite-dimensional over k, and F/k̃ is a function field with exact constants. Over a finite k, Mathlib's `Module.finite_of_finite` turns finite-dimensionality into finiteness of k̃, so the finite-field case is covered by the general statements (it is not stated separately). `algebraicClosure_ratFunc` is the F_q(t) acceptance case.

targets.target: Geometric connectedness after choosing the exact constant field
targets.note: Mathlib has `GeometricallyConnected` for scheme morphisms and Tau Ceti has the constant compositum and geometric degree of a function-field extension, but the theorem 'exact constants ⇒ the curve is geometrically connected' (equivalently F ⊗_k k̄ is a field) is not proved anywhere.

targets.target: Finite morphisms from finite field extensions, with inseparable degree and induced residue-field maps
targets.note: The place-level shadow is built: every place of the base extends (`restrict_surjective`), with e and f, the tower formulas, the residue-field extension, and the inseparable residue degree in the inertia count. Missing: the curves, hence the finite morphism C' → C attached to F'/F and its degree decomposition.

targets.target: Divisors, effectivity, and degree weighted by residue degrees
targets.note: `Divisor k F` is the free abelian group on places with `degree` weighted by `Place.degree`, with effectivity, lattice operations, positive/negative parts, the conorm along a finite extension and the cross-multiplied degree identity.

targets.target: The principal divisor map and the product formula deg(div f) = 0
targets.note: `deg (f)_∞ = [F : k(f)]` (`Divisor.degree_poles`, and `degree_zeros` for the zero divisor) gives `degree_principal : deg (div f) = 0`, hence the degree map on the class group; `div f = 0` iff f is algebraic over k.

targets.target: Riemann--Roch spaces L(D) and their dimensions
targets.note: L(D) is finite-dimensional with the bound ℓ(D) ≤ deg D₊ + 1, monotone, and invariant under linear equivalence; `Divisor.dim` is ℓ.

targets.target: Canonical divisors, the canonical class and deg K = 2g-2
targets.note: Built from Weil differentials (linear forms on the repartition space vanishing on A(D)+F); ℓ(W)=g and deg W = 2g-2 are proved, under the standing hypotheses `IsFunctionField k F` and `IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F` (exact constants).

targets.target: The Riemann--Roch theorem
targets.note: `ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 - g + ℓ(W-D)` for every D, with W the divisor of any nonzero Weil differential (Stichtenoth 1.5.15), plus the deg D ≥ 2g-1 corollary. Proved without sorry; hypotheses are `IsFunctionField k F` and exact constants, with no finiteness assumption on k — more general than FA.1's F_q setting.

targets.target: Finiteness of Pic^0 over a finite constant field
targets.note: `finite_ker_degreeClass` is exactly 'Cl⁰(F) is finite for a finite constant field' (Stichtenoth 5.1.3), with the class number defined and positive; the affine class group of a holomorphy ring is also finite.

targets.target: Rational divisor classes versus chosen rational points
targets.note: The distinction is respected throughout: hypotheses are stated as 'a divisor of degree one' and the existence of a degree-one *place* is derived only where Riemann--Roch produces it (genus 0 and genus 1 cases).

targets.target: Residue maps
targets.note: What exists is the *local component* ω_P of a Weil differential and the abstract residue theorem ∑_P ω_P(x) = 0 (the file's own docstring says this holds 'before any residue map has been constructed'). The residue map Res_P : Ω_F → k on Kähler differentials and its comparison with Weil differentials (Stichtenoth IV.3) are not built: `Kaehler.lean` only proves dim_F Ω[F/k] = 1 for a separating element and sets up the derivative.

targets.target: Bases of L(D) from certified presentations (an algorithm)
targets.note: Only the explicit P^1 computation L(n·∞) = polynomials of degree ≤ n exists (an acceptance case of FA.1); there is no algorithm computing a basis of L(D) on a general curve and no certificate format.

targets.target: The adele ring of K as a restricted product of local completions with respect to their valuation rings
targets.note: The general restricted-product construction and the finite adeles of a Dedekind domain (hence of an affine model of the curve, with adic completions and their integer rings) are in Mathlib. What is missing is the adele ring of a function field itself: the places at infinity are not adjoined, and Tau Ceti's `repartitionSpace` is the completion-free repartition space, not a topological ring.

targets.target: Local compactness of the adele ring
targets.note: The general criterion (each factor locally compact, the distinguished subgroups open and almost all compact) is proved for restricted products, and Tau Ceti makes every adic completion with finite residue field a nonarchimedean local field (so locally compact, with compact integers), which covers the finite places of a function field over F_q. Local compactness of a function-field adele ring would follow once the ring is constructed; the instance itself is not in the libraries.

targets.target: Discreteness and cocompactness of K in its additive adeles
targets.note: Discreteness and closedness of the diagonal are proved for number fields only, and cocompactness is not proved even there. For function fields Tau Ceti proves the algebraic shadow — A(D) ∩ F = L(D) and dim_k A_F/(A_F(D)+F) = i(D) < ∞ — which is the finite-dimensionality behind cocompactness, but with no topology on the repartition space.

targets.target: The idele group, the idele degree map and the compact degree-zero idele class group
targets.note: Mathlib defines the idele and idele class groups of a number field but proves nothing about them; there is no degree map, no degree-zero subgroup and no compactness statement, and nothing at all in the function-field case.

targets.target: Local residue characters from a nonzero differential and self-dual Haar measures
targets.note: The ambient machinery is more general than one might expect: Mathlib has Haar measure on any locally compact group, `AddChar` valued in the circle, and `VectorFourier.fourierIntegral` for an arbitrary commutative ring 𝕜 with a unitary additive character, a bilinear pairing and a measure — so the adelic Fourier integral is expressible. What is missing is everything specific: no additive character of a positive-characteristic local field built from a residue, no self-duality of a measure, and Fourier inversion only for finite abelian groups (`ZMod.dft_dft`, `AddChar.doubleDualEquiv`) and finite-dimensional real inner product spaces.

targets.target: The global residue pairing and Poisson summation on the adeles
targets.note: Mathlib's Poisson summation is ∑_{n∈ℤ} f(n) = ∑ 𝓕f(n) on ℝ with decay hypotheses. Pontryagin duality is proved only for finite abelian groups (`AddChar.doubleDualEquiv`, with Fourier inversion `ZMod.dft_dft`) and the circle (Tau Ceti); there is none for general LCA groups, no adelic Fourier transform and no adelic Poisson summation.

duplicates.note: The same construction and the same discreteness/cocompactness statements, for number fields; FA.2 explicitly says the archimedean arguments cannot be imported unchanged, so the overlap is in the statements, not the proofs.
Owns the idele group and the idele class group in the number-field case, including strong approximation.
AA.1 constructs adelic points of algebraic groups over a global field as restricted products with their topology; the underlying adele ring and its local compactness are shared with FA.2.
Owns the repartition (completion-free adele) space and the filtration A_F(D), which FA.2 re-uses as the algebraic skeleton of its adele ring.

Owns restricted products of locally compact groups: local compactness, compact-open cylinders and restricted products of Haar measures normalized on almost all places — exactly FA.2's first two targets in group-theoretic generality.

targets.target: Integral closures in finite separable extensions and the places above a place
targets.note: The fundamental identity ∑ e_i f_i = [F':F] is proved (separably, and on an affine model), together with Kummer's factorization theorem and integral bases.

targets.target: Decomposition and inertia groups
targets.note: Galois transitivity on the fibre, the decomposition field with its degree, and the inertia group with |I| = e·(inseparable residue degree) are all proved for place extensions of function fields.

targets.target: The different and the discriminant
targets.note: Dedekind's different theorem is proved in part: d(P'|P) ≥ e−1 always, and d = e−1 at tame places with separable residue extension, plus transitivity in towers. The converse half (d ≥ e at wild places, Stichtenoth 3.5.1(b)/3.5.5) is only remarked in a docstring. Mathlib supplies `differentIdeal` and the discriminant underneath. The wild different is therefore bounded below but not computed.

targets.target: Lower and upper ramification filtrations
targets.note: Only the lower-numbering filtration G_i is built, with the quotient embeddings into the residue field and the p-group structure of G_1. The Herbrand function φ/ψ and the upper numbering are absent from both libraries, so the wild conductor computation FA.3's acceptance demands is not available.

targets.target: Riemann--Hurwitz including the wild different
targets.note: Absent: `grep -rn -i hurwitz` matches only Hurwitz zeta functions in Mathlib. The different divisor exists, but 2g'-2 = [F':F](2g-2) + deg Diff(F'/F) is not stated anywhere; note also that Tau Ceti's genus theory is in place, so this is a missing theorem rather than missing vocabulary.

targets.target: Artin--Schreier and Witt-vector descriptions of cyclic p-power extensions
targets.note: Mathlib has Witt vectors and Frobenius/Verschiebung but no Artin--Schreier theory (its Kummer-extension file lists it as a TODO): the only `artinSchreier` names are characteristic-2 quadratic-splitting lemmas in Tau Ceti (a general polynomial file and the elliptic-curve node polynomial). The classification of ℤ/p-extensions by F/℘(F) and of ℤ/p^n-extensions by Witt vectors is absent, as is the equivalence relation on the defining elements.

targets.target: Purely inseparable extensions by Frobenius, treated separately
targets.note: Mathlib's general purely inseparable field theory is available, Tau Ceti keeps the inseparable residue degree visible in the inertia count, and over a finite constant field Tau Ceti computes the Frobenius subfield degrees [K(X) : K(X)^q] = q (and the same for an elliptic function field). There is no general treatment of F^{1/p}/F for a function field: no [F : F^p] = p, and nothing on its places, genus, different or the absence of a Galois or étale-cover interpretation.

targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Ray class fields with conductor data
targets.note: Absent for function fields, and ray class fields are absent everywhere. Tau Ceti has ray class groups of number fields with finiteness and the ray class number formula (`GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup`, `card_rayClassGroup`), with no class field attached.

targets.target: The Euler product over closed points by degree, and the zeta function of the curve
targets.note: The convergence ingredient is there — only finitely many places have degree ≤ n — and Mathlib has Euler products for multiplicative functions on ℕ, but the zeta function Z_C(t) = ∏_P (1-t^{deg P})^{-1} of a curve over a finite field is not defined in either library.

targets.target: Rationality of the zeta function and its numerator, via Riemann--Roch and the independent Weil theorem
targets.note: The two facts the Riemann--Roch rationality proof needs — finitely many effective divisors of bounded degree, and finiteness of Cl⁰ — are proved in Tau Ceti; the L-polynomial, its degree 2g, its functional equation and the Riemann hypothesis for curves are not.

targets.target: Artin local factors on inertia invariants for a finite Galois cover, including ramified places
targets.note: Inertia subgroups of place extensions exist, but there is no Artin L-function of a Galois representation in either library (Mathlib's L-series are Dirichlet/Hurwitz/modular).

targets.target: A function-field Chebotarev theorem retaining the degree congruence imposed by the constants
targets.note: Tau Ceti's Chebotarev directory is number-field infrastructure in progress (Frobenius prime sets, auxiliary primes, von Mangoldt counting); the density theorem itself is not proved there, and there is nothing for function fields, where the constant-field degree obstruction is the whole point.

targets.target: Error terms recorded with genus, conductor and representation dimension
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Owns the Chebotarev density theorem in the number-field case; FA.5 wants the function-field analogue with the degree congruence.

targets.target: The adelic quotient G(K)\G(A_K) for a connected reductive K-group
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a substantial affine-group-scheme library including reductivity, tori, Borels and root data, but no adelic points of an algebraic group, and no adele ring of a function field to take points in.

targets.target: Compact-level functions, central characters, constant terms and cuspidal subspaces
targets.note: Absent: `grep -rn -i cuspidal` in the Lean sources matches only cusp forms for congruence subgroups in Tau Ceti's classical modular-forms development.

targets.target: Reduction-theoretic finiteness of cuspidal spaces at fixed level and central character
targets.note: Absent; there is no reduction theory (no Siegel sets, no Harder--Narasimhan reduction) in either tree.

targets.target: Hecke correspondences and the unramified Satake dictionary with normalized Frobenius
targets.note: Abstract Hecke rings of a Hecke pair exist for any group (Mathlib `HeckeRing`; Tau Ceti's double-coset rings, with GL₂ congruence-subgroup and SL_n(ℤ) ⊂ GL_n(ℚ) instances and the p-local Hecke ring of GL_n ≅ ℤ[X₁, …, X_n] for n ≤ 2), but none is instantiated for G(K_v) with a compact open subgroup, and `grep -rn -i satake` returns nothing in either library, so the Satake isomorphism does not exist in any form.

targets.target: Complex or characteristic-zero ell-adic coefficient models with descent of eigenvalues
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Packaging divisor arithmetic, ray characters, conductors, L-polynomials and normalized local completions as independently checkable data
targets.note: This is an export/packaging obligation rather than a theorem. Its inputs that exist are divisor arithmetic and adic completions; its inputs that do not exist are ray characters, conductors and L-polynomials, all of which belong to FA.4 and FA.5.

targets.target: Certified finite-field factorization and place enumeration
targets.note: Places of bounded degree on k(x) are enumerated by monic irreducibles and Kummer's theorem reduces places above P to factorization of a minimal polynomial mod P; but there is no certified factorization algorithm, no cost model and no executable enumeration in either library.

targets.target: Riemann--Roch linear algebra with a stated representation and complexity
targets.note: The P^1 case is fully computed (ℓ(D) and genus 0), which is FA.7's first worked example; no general algorithm or complexity statement exists.

targets.note: The uniqueness step is built for the explicit carriers. kostantToralGroupScheme_hom_ext says a homomorphism out of a toral Kostant carrier over Z (the construction behind SlStd, SpStd and the spin, minuscule and Geck carriers) is determined by its values on the numbered positive and negative simple root subgroups and on the weight torus. targets.target: Rank one: maximalProPQuotient p Ẑ ≅ lim ℤ/p^n ≅ ℤ_p as topological groups; freeProP p (Fin 1) ≅ Multiplicative ℤ_[p]; Sylow characterization in Ẑ
targets.note: Mathlib has only the algebraic half of step 2: compatible families of ring homomorphisms into the ZMod (p^n) lift uniquely to ℤ_[p] (`PadicInt.lift`), and elements are determined by their reductions (`ext_of_toZModPow`). targets.target: Abelian pro-p groups: continuous ℤ_p-exponentiation, topological ℤ_p-module structure, automatic ℤ_p-linearity of continuous homomorphisms; topologically finitely generated ⇒ finitely generated ℤ_p-module

targets.target: Trivial-filtration theorem: a nonzero finite discrete p-primary module over a pro-p group has nonzero invariants, hence a G-stable filtration with trivial one-dimensional factors, and additive invariants equal length times the value at 𝔽_p
targets.note: Mathlib supplies the finite input (a p-group acting on a finite set of order divisible by p with a fixed point has another fixed point). Missing: the module statement for pro-p groups acting through a finite quotient, the filtration and the length formula.

targets.target: Dévissage from elementary abelian to all finite p-primary modules, and vanishing of H² for all such modules implying vanishing in all degrees ≥ 2 by dimension shifting through Coind_1^G
targets.note: All-degree tools exist, but not the continuous ones this layer needs. Mathlib's `continuousCohomology n` is defined in every degree, Tau Ceti adds an all-degree finite-quotient system (`finiteQuotientSystem`, without its colimit comparison), and Mathlib's Shapiro isomorphism `groupCohomology.coindIso` holds in every degree for abstract groups. For continuous cohomology Tau Ceti has coinduced discrete modules and Shapiro only in degrees 0 and 1 (closed subgroups, profinite G), and its long exact sequence stops at H². There is no acyclicity of Coind_1, no dimension shifting and no dévissage.

targets.target: Pro-p Nielsen–Schreier: an open subgroup of index m in a free pro-p group of rank n ≥ 1 is free pro-p of rank 1 + m(n − 1)
targets.note: Only the abstract Nielsen–Schreier theorem (subgroups of free groups are free) exists, without the index formula.

targets.target: IsDemushkin p G (pro-p, dim H¹ finite, dim H² = 1, nondegenerate cup pairing) with derived topological finite generation, demushkinRank, one-relator presentation and invariance under isomorphism

targets.target: First examples: ℤ/2 is the unique finite and the unique rank-1 Demushkin group at p = 2; free pro-p groups are not Demushkin; ℤ_p × ℤ_p is Demushkin with q = 0; no rank-1 Demushkin group for odd p

targets.target: Abelianization structure G^ab ≅ ℤ_p^{n−1} × ℤ_p/qℤ_p, well-definedness of demushkinQ, and D₀^ab ≅ ℤ₂² × ℤ/2

targets.target: Prescription property (Labute Prop. 6): equivalence of surjectivity of H¹(G, I(χ)/p^i) → H¹(G, I(χ)/p), vanishing connecting maps, and compatible crossed homomorphisms with prescribed values
targets.note: No such statements in either library.

targets.target: Canonical character: a Demushkin group has a unique continuous χ : G → ℤ_pˣ with the prescription property; closed image, isomorphism invariance, Im χ = 1 + qℤ_p for q ≠ 2

targets.target: Closed subgroups of ℤ₂ˣ (U^(f), V^(f), U^[f]) with exhaustiveness, procyclicity and indices; ℤ_pˣ ≅ μ_{p−1} × (1 + pℤ_p) and the p-adic logarithm 1 + pℤ_p ≅ pℤ_p for odd p; closed subgroups of 1 + pℤ_p

targets.target: Dimension two: an infinite Demushkin group has cd_p G = 2

targets.target: Duality package: trace isomorphism H²(G,𝔽_p) ≅ 𝔽_p, perfect cup pairings on the I(χ)/p^i system, naturality with restriction and corestriction, role of χ

targets.target: Three-term Euler formula for t.f.g. pro-p G with cd_p ≤ 2 and finite H⁰, H¹, H²

targets.target: Open-subgroup theorem: U open in infinite Demushkin G is Demushkin with n(U) − 2 = [G:U](n(G) − 2) and χ_U = χ_G|_U

targets.target: gradedBracket gr_j × gr_k → gr_{j+k+1} and gradedPow gr_k → gr_{k+1} with bilinearity, alternation, Jacobi, additivity except in degree 0 at p = 2, the dyadic identities and naturality (Labute Props. 1–2)

In Mathlib, one-sided nondegeneracy implies nondegeneracy for finite free modules over a domain (`Nondegenerate.ofSeparatingLeft`/`ofSeparatingRight`, `nondegenerate_iff_ker_eq_bot`), `congr` transports forms along linear equivalences, and `LinearMap.BilinForm.Equivalent` is the existence of an isometry equivalence, with nondegeneracy transported by `Nondegenerate.congr`.

targets.target: Alternating implies skew-symmetric in every characteristic; at p = 2 skew-symmetric equals symmetric and x ↦ b(x,x) is semilinear; for odd p symmetric and alternating forces zero

Only the characteristic-2 comparisons are not stated: skew-symmetric equals symmetric, and x ↦ b(x,x) is additive and semilinear.

targets.target: Resolving subcategories: repleteness, zero and biproduct closure, extension closure, closure under kernels of admissible epimorphisms, finite P-resolutions of all objects, explicit induced exact structure
targets.note: No resolving-subcategory package (grep IsResolving, "resolving subcategor" finds only docstrings); extension closure and ambient kernel closure exist separately.

targets.target: Euler class of a finite resolution: independence of length, padding and choice, and additivity on conflations by the common-refinement argument for general resolving P
targets.note: Invariance under isomorphism, zero padding and direct sums holds for every extension-closed P containing zero and closed under binary biproducts (`eulerClassFullSubcategory_ofIso`, `_zeroPad`, `_pad`, `_biprod`). Independence of the choice of resolution and additivity on conflations are proved only for P consisting of E-projectives (Schanuel and horseshoe); the file docstring states that the general resolving case via the common-refinement argument is not carried out. The ambient-K₀ class is independent for trivial telescoping reasons.

targets.target: Resolution theorem: under resolving hypotheses the inclusion induces an isomorphism on exact K₀ with inverse the alternating resolution class, natural in compatible exact functors and invariant under equivalence
targets.note: Only P ≤ E.isProjective (closed under zero and biproducts, essentially small) is covered, with both inverse identities; naturality, equivalence invariance and the general resolving case are missing.

targets.target: Projective horseshoe lemma and Schanuel lemma in exact categories

targets.target: Comparison maps from a resolution to a fixed projective resolution, unique up to chain homotopy, under enough projectives
targets.note: Mathlib has comparison maps and homotopy uniqueness for projective resolutions in abelian categories; nothing for FiniteResolution in exact categories and no bridge between the two.

targets.target: Graded resolutions: graded finite P-resolutions, graded resolving subcategories, graded Euler class and resolution theorem, graded comparison and horseshoe, agreement with ungraded Euler classes at q = 1

targets.target: A conflation X ↪ Y ↠ Z produces the standard triangle X → Y → Z → ΣX
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib's only analogue is for cochain complexes: degreewise split short exact sequences give distinguished triangles in the homotopy category.

targets.target: The triangulated axioms for the standard triangles, including rotation, morphisms of triangles and the octahedral axiom (Happel's theorem)
targets.note: Absent. The only triangulated quotient category in either library is Mathlib's HomotopyCategory C (up ℤ) (anonymous instances at HomotopyCategory/Pretriangulated.lean:515 and Triangulated.lean:208), built from mapping cones rather than from a Frobenius exact structure; grep for Happel finds only bibliography entries.

targets.target: An exact functor sending projective-injectives to projective-injectives descends to a triangle functor, with natural-transformation and equivalence APIs and restriction to extension-closed Frobenius exact subcategories
targets.note: Tau Ceti has exact (conflation-exact) functors between exact structures, with identity, composition and transport along equivalences. It also has the induced exact structure on an extension-closed full subcategory, with its conflation-exact inclusion. Nothing shows that an exact functor preserves relative projectives or injectives, and nothing descends an exact functor to a stable category or constructs a suspension comparison.

targets.target: For a finite-dimensional algebra self-injective on both sides, the abelian exact structure on finite-dimensional right modules is Frobenius with projective-injectives exactly the projectives

targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti's split exact structure is the fully split one (every object projective-injective), not the componentwise split structure; Mathlib characterizes contractible complexes as zero objects of the homotopy category.

targets.target: Identification of the stable categories with K₁(A) and K_n(A), and the structure package on K_n(A): preadditive, zero object, ℤ-shift generated by the cyclic shift, Pretriangulated, IsTriangulated, cone triangles distinguished, both triangulations agreeing

targets.target: Parity/cyclic homology objects, exact-acyclic periodic complexes, quasi-isomorphisms, and D_n(A) both as a localization and as a Verdier quotient of K_n(A), with the comparison equivalence and the triangulated package
targets.note: Homology objects, quasi-isomorphisms and the localization at quasi-isomorphisms exist for any complex shape. Missing: acyclicity for an exact structure, the Verdier-quotient description and its comparison with the localization, and all triangulated structure on D_n (DerivedCategory exists only for up ℤ).

targets.target: The eight named comparison functors: compression, Verdier localization, stalk/complete resolution, forgetting finite projectivity, base change to S/(w), cokernel to stable MCM, uncurved DG at w = 0, and the left/right opposite dictionary

Mathlib's `HomologicalComplexUpToQuasiIso.Qh` is, for every complex shape, the functor from the homotopy category to the localization at quasi-isomorphisms, proved to be a localization, with the needed instances for ZMod n-indexed shapes. targets.target: The resulting classes satisfy the unramified, ramified Steinberg and ordinary-at-p local conditions of a Selmer group
targets.note: Nothing of the target exists. There are no Galois representations attached to automorphic forms, no unramified, Steinberg or ordinary local conditions, and no Selmer groups defined inside H¹ by local conditions. The Selmer groups in the libraries are defined by valuations or local points: Mathlib's K(S, n) ⊆ Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ, and Tau Ceti's 2-descent Selmer group of an elliptic curve with its local conditions. Nearby ingredients: inflation–restriction for continuous and discrete H¹; Tau Ceti's Galois-cohomological Kummer map Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ → H¹(G_K, μₙ), proved injective; and Mathlib's decomposition and inertia subgroups (`ValuationSubring.decompositionSubgroup`, `inertiaSubgroup`). The subgroups are defined for any field extension, hence for G_K at any place of K̄, but nothing relates them to local Galois groups.

targets.target: Control of extension modules and their lengths by congruence ideals at height-one primes
targets.note: The length and height infrastructure is present (module length with additivity, Krull's principal ideal theorem, the order of vanishing ord x = length(R/xR), and Tau Ceti's length(I/aI) = ord a); no statement bounds or computes lengths of extension or Selmer modules at height-one localizations in terms of congruence ideals.

targets.target: An explicitly oriented divisibility of characteristic ideals
targets.note: Absent: there is no characteristic ideal, Iwasawa-module structure theorem, pseudo-isomorphism or Fitting ideal. The declarations named after Fitting are the Lie-module Fitting components, Mathlib's Fitting decomposition of an endomorphism and Tau Ceti's Fitting lemma. Present ingredients: Weierstrass preparation over complete local rings, the structure theorem over a PID, noetherianity of power-series rings, 'contains implies divides' for invertible ideals, and unique factorization in R⟦X⟧ for a PID R (Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Ideal.lean:202), so ℤ_p⟦X⟧ is a UFD.

targets.target: Comparison of primitive and imprimitive Selmer groups through the local cohomology exact sequence, matching every removed Euler factor analytically
targets.note: Absent: no Poitou–Tate or local/global Tate duality, no primitive or imprimitive Selmer groups and no L-functions with removed Euler factors (grep for Poitou, imprimitive, removed Euler). Long exact sequences in group and low-degree continuous cohomology, local Euler factors of elliptic curves and restriction of Dirichlet series to prime supports are the nearby material.

duplicates.note: Proves changes of local conditions and the primitive/imprimitive exact sequences for Selmer structures, the same comparison this layer states for its Selmer groups.

targets.target: The inverse limit of ray class groups of p-power conductor and fixed tame modulus, its reciprocity interpretation, and its character space
targets.note: Tau Ceti has ray class groups for every modulus, with surjective transition maps `classMap` for 𝔪 ∣ 𝔫, forming an inverse system by `classMap_comp_classMap`. It also has the ideal-theoretic Artin map, whose docstring says that nothing about a factorization through ray class groups is proved. Mathlib identifies continuous characters of ℤ_p with topologically nilpotent elements. Generic tools exist but are not instantiated: Mathlib's `ProfiniteGrp.limit` of any diagram of profinite groups, the abelianization of G_K (`Field.absoluteGaloisGroupAbelianization`), and for F = ℚ the cyclotomic reciprocity Gal(ℚ(ζ_n)/ℚ) ≃ (ℤ/n)ˣ (`galCyclotomicEquivUnitsZMod`) with the p-adic cyclotomic character. Missing: the limit over p-power conductors with its profinite topology, the reciprocity identification with the Galois group of the maximal abelian extension unramified outside p𝔫, and its character space.

There is no limit (local units at p), no closure of the global units and no Leopoldt defect; 'Leopoldt' has no hits. The regulators in either library are real-valued: the regulator of number-field units and Tau Ceti's Néron–Tate regulator of an elliptic curve. There is no p-adic regulator.

targets.target: Locally algebraic Hecke characters with algebraic and p-adic avatars through chosen embeddings, conductors, infinity types and local factors

Over a general number field there is no Hecke character, Grössencharakter or infinity type (grep for HeckeChar, Grossen, infinityType). Mathlib's idele class group is only the defining quotient, used nowhere else. Tau Ceti's `UnitaryIdealWeight` is a multiplicative function on ideals that takes finite-order characters, with Euler factors but no conductor or infinity type.

Tau Ceti has restricted series over non-archimedean topological rings, and multiplicativity of the Gauss norm of restricted series over ultrametric normed rings.

targets.target: Annuli and convergent Laurent series on them, and residues of differentials
targets.note: Tau Ceti has two-sided coefficient families tending to 0: the functions on the circle |X| = 1, with a bilinear convolution but no ring structure. Residues exist only for complex meromorphic functions, as Mathlib's formal residue pairing on Laurent polynomials, and as the abstract residue theorem for Weil differentials of function fields, where no residue map is constructed. Mathlib's Laurent series are formal. Tau Ceti's Laurent-domain rational localizations give annulus coordinate rings only abstractly. Absent: annuli r ≤ |z| ≤ s over a non-archimedean field, their Laurent-series rings, and residues of such differentials.

targets.target: Exact differentials and termwise differentiation and integration of power series with the convergence domain of the result
targets.note: Formal and analytic termwise differentiation are present over any nontrivially normed field: the radius does not shrink, and the derivative is the termwise series on the same ball. There is no formal antiderivative of a power series and no statement about the radius of an integrated series. Exact differentials exist only over ℂ and ℝ: Mathlib's `Complex.IsExactOn`, exactness of holomorphic functions on discs, and the real/complex Poincaré lemma. None applies to a non-archimedean field.

targets.target: The unique primitive with chosen base value on a disc
targets.note: In the non-archimedean setting only the formal uniqueness is present: two power series over a torsion-free ring with equal derivative and constant term are equal, and one-variable expansions are unique. Over ℂ the target exists in pieces. A holomorphic function on a disc has a primitive (`DifferentiableOn.isExactOn_ball`), which `Complex.IsExactOn.with_val_at` normalizes to any base value, and the mean-value results give uniqueness on connected sets. These are for ℝ and ℂ only and do not apply to totally disconnected ultrametric discs, where existence of the primitive is missing.

For an elliptic curve over the completion at a height-one prime, it identifies the residue disc of the origin (the kernel of reduction) with the formal-group points on the maximal ideal. Mathlib has good reduction only for elliptic curves. Missing: rigid or adic spaces with a structure sheaf (Tau Ceti's presheaf is not yet identified with 𝒪_X), wide opens, dagger/Monsky–Washnitzer algebras, tubes, residue discs in general, and smooth proper curves with good reduction as a package.

targets.target: Frobenius lifts on a cover of the curve
targets.note: Absent: no lift of Frobenius is constructed on any p-adically complete or overconvergent algebra (grep for Frobenius lift, δ-ring). What exists: the Witt-vector Frobenius, the characteristic-p identity f(X^p) = f^p on power series, semilinear pullback of Kähler differentials, and Mathlib's predicate `AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt` (φ(x) ≡ x^q mod Q). With Q = pS that predicate says φ lifts Frobenius, and it has a uniqueness theorem in the unramified case.

targets.target: Finite-dimensional rigid/de Rham cohomology in the degree used for integration, independence of the Frobenius lift, and the comparison of cohomological and local analytic pullback
targets.note: Present: Kähler differentials, the one-dimensionality of Ω[F/k] for a function field, the genus-dimensional space of regular Weil differentials, sheaf cohomology of 𝒪_X-modules, and Mathlib's analytic exterior derivative `extDeriv`. That derivative works over any nontrivially normed field, with d ∘ d = 0 for analytic forms and compatibility with pullback. Absent: the algebraic de Rham complex and H¹_dR, Monsky–Washnitzer or rigid cohomology, their finiteness, and any Frobenius action. Apart from an unrelated docstring, grep for de Rham finds only the B_dR period ring.

targets.target: The Frobenius polynomial argument giving analytic continuation of primitives (Dwork), and the Coleman uniqueness principle
targets.note: Absent; grep for Coleman, Dwork, locally analytic and analytic continuation in a p-adic setting finds nothing (the Coleman hits are provenance comments for Chabauty–Coleman code).

targets.target: Coleman functions from compatible local analytic functions with Frobenius continuation data, with pullback, differentiation, products and integration, independence of auxiliary Frobenius choices, and the good-reduction and unipotence assumptions
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: A direct construction on P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} by successive (unipotent) extensions
targets.note: Absent. Grep for unipotent connection, iterated integral, thrice-punctured and successive extension finds nothing relevant: the literal hits are Fubini-type iterated integrals, permutation triples for covers of the thrice-punctured sphere, and extension of scalars.

duplicates.note: Constructs rigid cohomology from overconvergent de Rham complexes on frames and proves that different Frobenius lifts induce the same operator, the cohomology and independence-of-lift targets here.
Constructs dagger affinoid algebras, strict overconvergent neighbourhoods and overconvergent de Rham complexes, the overconvergent-neighbourhood target of this layer.
Constructs compatible Frobenius lifts on overconvergent algebras and records their coordinate dependence, overlapping the Frobenius-lift target.

targets.target: Li_1(z) = −log_p(1 − z) and Li_k by dLi_k = Li_{k−1}(z) dz/z with the power series Σ_{n≥1} z^n/n^k on |z| < 1
targets.note: No p-adic polylogarithm exists, and the p-adic logarithm is only the series definition without convergence noted in L0. Mathlib has only real, complex and formal analogues: Σ zⁿ/n = −log(1 − z) for |z| < 1 over ℂ and ℝ, the formal power series log(1 + X), and Σ e^{2πian}/nˢ = expZeta a s on the unit circle for Re s > 1. Grep for polylog, dilog and Li_k finds no definition.

targets.target: Existence and uniqueness of Li_k in the Coleman category, the differential recursion, and the tangential base-point normalization at zero
targets.note: Absent; there is no Coleman category.

targets.target: Distribution, inversion and Frobenius relations for the p-adic polylogarithms
targets.note: Absent for polylogarithms. Mathlib has the complex inversion relation only on |z| = 1 for k ≥ 2 (as a Fourier series of Bernoulli polynomials) and the multiplication formula for Bernoulli polynomials.

targets.target: Evaluation at roots of unity different from 1, including p-power order, and the norm/trace compatibilities needed by primitive characters
targets.note: Absent for p-adic polylogarithms; cyclotomic fields, ∏(1 − μ^k) = n and the twisting behaviour of Gauss sums of primitive characters are the available ingredients.

targets.target: Compatibility with coefficient embeddings, and the complex polylogarithm formula
targets.note: The complex values Li_s(e^{2πia}) exist as Mathlib's expZeta (its Dirichlet series for Re s > 1, with meromorphic continuation), and L-functions of additive characters on ZMod N are identified with it; a named complex Li_k on |z| < 1 and any comparison with a p-adic polylogarithm through coefficient embeddings are absent.

targets.target: RJW Theorem 6.7: L_p(θ, k) = (1 − θ(p)p^{−k})/G(θ^{−1}) · Σ_c θ^{−1}(c) Li_{k,p}(ξ_N^c) for nontrivial primitive θ and every k ≥ 1
targets.note: Absent: there is no p-adic L-function of any kind (grep for Kubota, Leopoldt, p-adic L-function, p-adic zeta over both trees).

targets.target: The corresponding complex formula for L(θ, k) through the Gauss sum and polylogarithm values at roots of unity
targets.note: Both ingredients are in Mathlib: the L-function of a discrete Fourier transform is Σ_j Φ(j)·expZeta(−j/N, s), and for primitive χ the Fourier transform of χ is χ⁻¹(−·) times the Gauss sum (with the Euler factors of a change of level). The combined formula expressing a Gauss-sum multiple of L(χ⁻¹, s) as Σ_j χ(j)·expZeta(∓j/N, s) is not stated, and expZeta is never identified with Li_k.

targets.target: Pairing convention of the existing elliptic height, and its comparison with each source's pairing
targets.note: At the baseline the height is lim h_x(2ⁿP)/(2·4ⁿ): the height for the divisor (O), which is half the x-height (Silverman's ĥ). Here h_x is Mathlib's logHeight, relative to the base field, so over K it is [K:ℚ] times the absolute height. The pairing is QuadraticMap.associated', so ⟨P,P⟩ = ĥ(P). This contradicts the layer's premise that the existing height is the x-height normalisation. Over ℚ it also makes Tau Ceti's regulator 2^(−r) times the regulators of Silverman (⟨P,Q⟩ = ĥ(P+Q)−ĥ(P)−ĥ(Q)) and Cremona, which both have ⟨P,P⟩ = lim h_x(2ⁿP)/4ⁿ. No comparison lemma with another convention exists.

targets.target: Rigid analytic space representing continuous characters G → A^× on affinoid algebras, for compact abelian p-adic analytic G, with its universal character
targets.note: For G = ℤ_p Mathlib identifies continuous characters valued in a complete normed ℤ_p-algebra R with bounded ℤ_p-action (no ultrametric hypothesis) with the topologically nilpotent elements of R, and with {r : ‖r‖ < 1} only when the norm is strictly multiplicative (NormMulClass); there is no rigid space, representability or general G.

targets.target: Generic-fibre construction from the completed group ring, finite-character components, polydisc charts, pullback in G and affinoid base change, with the separate p = 2 chart
targets.note: Tau Ceti has only closed polydiscs as adic spectra of restricted power series rings; open discs, weight spaces and their charts are absent.

targets.target: Separate domains of integral, rigid and locally analytic characters; factorization through the abelianization for nonabelian G

targets.note: No Matlis-type duality in either library.

targets.note: Only the generic linear dual exists.

targets.target: Betti/de Rham realization comparison matrices for a motive with a chosen complex embedding
targets.note: Neither library has motives, algebraic de Rham cohomology of a variety, or a Betti realization. Mathlib has Kaehler differentials (KaehlerDifferential, 127 declarations) but no de Rham complex of a scheme; the only 'DeRham' names in Mathlib are the perfectoid period rings BDeRham/BDeRhamPlus in Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean, which are Fontaine's rings, not a realization functor. Tau Ceti has singular homology (TopPair.singularHomology) and quasi-coherent scheme cohomology, but no comparison between them.

targets.target: Basis-independent determinant lines and the effect of changing bases
targets.note: The linear algebra of a single top exterior power is present: Tau Ceti identifies the top exterior power of a module with a basis indexed by Fin n with the scalars (exteriorPower.topEquiv) and proves an endomorphism acts on it by its determinant (map_top_eq_det_smul, with a basis-free form), which is the change-of-basis rule for the line. Missing is any determinant line/determinant functor formalism (graded lines, Knudsen-Mumford, determinants of complexes) and any statement that a period class is well defined modulo a change of basis.

targets.target: Complex conjugation eigenspaces, Hodge filtration and Tate twists
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Hodge-theoretic linear algebra, sorry-free: a bounded decreasing filtration opposed to its conjugate in weight n (for any conjugate-linear involution, in particular the one induced by an integral lattice), the Hodge pieces with conjugation exchanging H^{p,q} and H^{q,p}, Tate twists with their effect on F, Hodge numbers, polarizations, rational substructures, mixed Hodge structures and the Deligne splitting. Missing is the 'complex conjugation' of Deligne's period formalism: no real Frobenius F_infinity acting on a Betti realization and hence no eigenspaces H_B^+ and H_B^- (the Conjugation structure is the antilinear involution defining the real form, not F_infinity), and no Hodge structure is produced from a variety.

targets.target: Period classes modulo coefficient-field units; effect of changing embeddings
targets.note: No declaration in either library names a period of a motive or of a variety; grep for 'period' in the name column returns only periodic functions, period lattices of elliptic curves and Tau Ceti's Hodge period domain (TauCeti.Hodge.PeriodDomain.Point), which is the classifying space, not a period matrix.

duplicates.note: MC.2 constructs the realization functors themselves and compares Betti/de Rham realizations over embeddings into C; PS.0 consumes them and is declared to have MC.2 as an input, so the realization-comparison target is stated twice.

C5 owns the algebraic de Rham-Betti comparison for smooth complex varieties, including integral Betti lattices and rational structures retained before complexification; PS.0's comparison matrices are the matrix form of exactly that comparison.

HodgeStructures L0 owns pure Hodge structures with the conjugation symmetry of the Hodge pieces and the Tate twist - the filtration/conjugation/Tate-twist part of PS.0 T2 that TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge now delivers.

targets.target: Completed motivic L-function from local Weil-Deligne data
targets.note: No Weil-Deligne representation and no motivic L-function in either library; grep for weilDeligne/WeilDeligne in names returns nothing, and grep -rn -i 'Weil-Deligne' over both trees returns no definition. The only Euler-product-from-local-data constructions are Tau Ceti's EulerProductData (abstract multiplicative ideal weights) and Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.LFunction.

targets.target: Critical integers derived from archimedean Gamma factors
targets.note: Mathlib has the archimedean Gamma factor of a Dirichlet character (even and odd cases) and the poles of Gamma, which is what a criticality condition is read off from, but there is no definition of a critical integer and no statement that criticality is a simultaneous regularity condition for two infinity factors.

targets.target: Deligne-type normalized-value statement (sign, powers of 2 pi i, coefficient field, Galois equivariance)
targets.note: Nothing in either library states an algebraicity-up-to-a-period result. There is no period to divide by, and no Galois equivariance statement for L-values.

targets.target: The Dirichlet/Tate case: special values of Dirichlet L-functions with their functional equation and rationality
targets.note: The analytic half is in Mathlib and sorry-free: continuation of L-functions of functions on ZMod N, the completed L-function, the functional equation for primitive characters with explicit root number, zeta(-n) = -B_{n+1}/(n+1), zeta(2k) as a rational multiple of pi^{2k}, and Hurwitz zeta at negative integers via Bernoulli polynomials. The rationality half is missing for nontrivial characters: Mathlib records only the trivial zeros of Dirichlet L-functions, defines no generalized Bernoulli numbers B_{k,chi}, and never states L(chi, 1-k) = -B_{k,chi}/k or its algebraicity (its HurwitzZetaValues TODO asks to extend the values to Dirichlet L-functions). Nothing is phrased as a critical value normalized by a period.

targets.target: The modular-form case with ramified and imprimitive corrections
targets.note: Mathlib defines the completed L-function Lambda and the L-function L of a modular form for an arithmetic subgroup, proves the Dirichlet-series identity on the convergence half-plane and, for cusp forms, entire continuation; its WeakFEPair pairs f with f|S, so the abstract functional equation relates Lambda(f) to Lambda(f|S) (no Fricke/Atkin-Lehner sign for Gamma_0(N)). Tau Ceti adds Hecke's abscissa bounds, identifies the LSeries of the q-expansion coefficients with Mathlib's L, and has Atkin-Lehner and Fricke eigenspace decompositions. There is no period of a modular form, no algebraicity of L(f,j)/period and no treatment of imprimitive or ramified corrections.

duplicates.note: AL.1 (Tate's thesis) defines L, epsilon and the real/complex gamma factors of Hecke characters and proves the global functional equation - the GL_1 archimedean factors of PS.1 T1 and the Dirichlet/Tate case of T3.
AN.1 owns the Dirichlet-series/continuation apparatus PS.1 needs for the Dirichlet/Tate case.
M.8 also exports Galois realisations with their Frobenius Euler polynomials, overlapping PS.1's local-factor bookkeeping.

AL.5 supplies imprimitive/primitive comparisons, critical-value normalization, functional-equation signs and algebraicity inputs for GL_2/Rankin families - PS.1's modular-form case with its imprimitive corrections (T2, T4).
DirichletPadicLFunctions L0 constructs generalized Bernoulli numbers and proves the algebraicity of Dirichlet L-values against the complex L-functions - the missing half of PS.1 T3.
ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions L1 defines period lines Omega_f^+- and proves algebraicity of the period-normalized critical values L(f,chi,j+1) - PS.1's modular-form case (T4).

targets.target: Algebra of formal periods with linearity, change-of-variables and Stokes relations
targets.note: No formal period algebra in either library. Mathlib has the divergence theorem and integration by parts for interval integrals, but nothing that presents an algebra by generators (X, D, omega, gamma) modulo the period relations.

targets.target: Comparison with the coordinate ring of the Nori period torsor
targets.note: No Nori motives, no Tannakian category of motives and no torsor of tensor isomorphisms between two fibre functors. The neutral reconstruction exists: Mathlib proves Tannaka duality for finite groups (TannakaDuality.FiniteGroup.equiv), and Tau Ceti identifies the A-points of a commutative Hopf algebra with tensor automorphisms of the scalar-extension fibre functor on finite-dimensional comodules (TauCeti.Tannaka.fgPointTensorIsoEquiv). A name search for 'Nori' matches only knot-theory names containing 'unoriented'.

targets.target: Evaluation map into C and the separation of forced identities from injectivity
targets.note: Absent for the same reason; there is no period object to evaluate.

duplicates.note: MC.6 constructs tensor-isomorphism torsors between fiber functors and explicitly says it exports period torsors to PeriodsAndSpecialValues; the torsor half of PS.2 is MC.6's target restated.

targets.target: Rational motivic cohomology
targets.note: No motivic cohomology, no higher Chow groups and no higher algebraic K-theory in either library. The only K-theory is Tau Ceti's K_0: Grothendieck groups of split, exact, abelian and triangulated categories, and K_0 of finitely generated projective modules over a ring with the Cartan map; Mathlib's AlgebraicCycle has no rational equivalence or cycle classes.

targets.target: Real/Deligne regulators and leading-term lines
targets.note: No Borel regulator, no Deligne regulator, no Beilinson regulator: the only declarations whose names contain 'regulator' are the Dirichlet unit regulator (Mathlib) and the Neron-Tate regulator of a Weierstrass curve (Tau Ceti).

targets.target: The zero-rank and nonzero-rank Borel cases for a number field, with embedding multiplicities and covolume normalization
targets.note: The weight-one Borel case is the Dirichlet regulator, and that is complete and sorry-free: Mathlib defines the regulator as the determinant of the logarithmic embedding of a fundamental system, proves it positive, independent of the family up to index (regOfFamily_div_regulator), and proves the Dirichlet class number formula as the residue of the Dedekind zeta function at s = 1, with the explicit 2^{r1}(2 pi)^{r2} R h / (w sqrt|d|) constant. Tau Ceti adds the rank-zero degeneration regulator = 1. Higher-weight Borel regulators (K_{2n-1} of a number field to R) are absent, and Mathlib's residue statement is a one-sided real limit, not an analytic continuation of zeta_K.

targets.target: Comparison of higher K-theory and motivic regulators via the actual comparison maps; torsion kept separate from lattices
targets.note: No higher K-theory in either library, so no comparison map exists.

duplicates.note: R.7 owns the Borel/Beilinson comparison, the factor-of-2 normalization and the zero-rank and rank-one recoveries; PS.3's acceptance test restates R.7's.

M.8 constructs the rational regulator from motivic cohomology, the Chern-character compatibility and the separation of integral lattices from rational 'integral parts' - the same three targets as PS.3.
ER.5 owns the elliptic-curve regulator/leading-term example PS.3 lists as an input and re-exports.

targets.target: Integral determinant lines of perfect global/local cohomology complexes
targets.note: Neither library has perfect complexes over a ring or a determinant functor on them; 'IsPerfect' in both trees means a perfect matching or a perfect group, and there is no detLine/determinantFunctor anywhere.

targets.target: Finite/singular local conditions and archimedean corrections, with the real comparison trivialization
targets.note: No Selmer-style local conditions attached to a determinant line; Tau Ceti's continuous cohomology (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology) provides the cohomology but no finite/singular decomposition.

targets.target: Invariance under quasi-isomorphism and change of lattice
targets.note: Meaningless without the determinant line; no such invariance statement exists.

targets.target: Contribution of finite kernels and cokernels; Fitting ideals versus determinant generators
targets.note: Only the order bookkeeping exists: Mathlib's multiplicativity of cardinalities along a submodule and quotient, and Tau Ceti's Euler-Poincare theorem for any invariant additive on short exact sequences. Neither library defines Fitting ideals of a module - every 'Fitting' declaration is the Fitting decomposition of a Lie module or of an endomorphism (Mathlib Lie/Weights, Tau Ceti KrullSchmidt) - or determinant lines, so the Fitting-versus-determinant comparison the layer insists on cannot be stated.

targets.target: Bad-prime Euler and Tamagawa factors
targets.note: Mathlib defines the local Euler factor of a Weierstrass curve over a nonarchimedean local field, split by good/split multiplicative/nonsplit multiplicative/additive reduction, so the bad-prime Euler factors exist for elliptic curves. No Tamagawa number exists in either library (name search for 'tamagawa' returns nothing).

duplicates.note: D7 owns the compact-support and local-condition cochain complexes of number fields with derived local/global duality and their perfectness and amplitude, with modified real-place terms at p = 2 - the perfect global/local complexes of PS.4 T0 and T1.
M.8 also builds Selmer complexes from explicit local conditions and their determinants for the Tate and elliptic representations.
L2 owns Selmer structures with finite/singular local conditions and their duals, which PS.4 restates as 'finite/singular conditions'.

PMIA L5 constructs determinant lines of perfect complexes compatible with quasi-isomorphism and relates them to characteristic divisors of torsion cohomology and finite modules - PS.4 T0, T2 and T3 (AUDIT-26 lists the reverse link).

L3 asks for the determinant-line formulation of perfect Iwasawa complexes and its relation to characteristic ideals, the Iwasawa-theoretic case of PS.4 T0/T2 (the reverse of the existing L3 -> PS.4 link).

targets.target: Zeta elements and the equivariant Tamagawa-number conjecture in a relative K-group
targets.note: There is no K_1, no relative K-group and no zeta element in either library; Tau Ceti's K-theory stops at K_0 (of exact categories and of finitely generated projective modules).

targets.target: Reduced norms and noncommutative K1 (not replaced by scalar units)
targets.note: No reduced norm of a general central simple or semisimple algebra and no K_1 in either library. The only reduced norm is Tau Ceti's norm form of a quaternion algebra (QuaternionAlgebra.normForm); Mathlib's BrauerGroup is a bare quotient, with the group structure and Br(R) = Z/2 in Tau Ceti.

targets.target: Adapters for the proven Tate/Artin and abelian cases
targets.note: Absent; there is no Artin L-function in either library either (the only L-functions are Dirichlet, modular and Weierstrass).

targets.target: Recovering the commutative determinant formula on specialization
targets.note: Absent for the same reason.

duplicates.note: NE.3 owns reduced norms, SK1 and Artin evaluation, exactly the K1 targets PS.5 restates.
I.7 states the equivariant Tamagawa-number formulation for the integral Brumer-Stark setting, overlapping PS.5's equivariant statements.
NE.5 formulates localized-K1 zeta elements and proves agreement with the commutative determinant formulas on specialization - PS.5 T0 and T3 (AUDIT-26 lists the reverse link).

targets.target: Adapters identifying fundamental-line terms with Mordell-Weil regulator, torsion, local Tamagawa numbers, periods and Sha
targets.note: Of the five terms only the Mordell-Weil regulator and the torsion subgroup exist: Tau Ceti defines the regulator as the absolute determinant of the Neron-Tate Gram matrix with basis-independence and nonnegativity, and proves E(K)_tors finite (finite_torsion) with Nagell-Lutz over Q. Tamagawa numbers, the real period and Sha do not exist in either library, and no adapter to a fundamental line can be formed.

targets.note: The phrase 'iterated integral' in Mathlib refers to Fubini/Tonelli for product measures and to Sobolev inequalities, not to Chen iterated integrals along a path.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has tensor words (TauCeti.TensorWords, all tensor powers of a module) with the deconcatenation coproduct and its subword calculus, but no shuffle or quasi-shuffle (stuffle) product, so no shuffle Hopf algebra; every 'shuffle' name in both trees is a sign convention or a tensor rearrangement.
