targets.target: Euler product / Dirichlet series of E over a number field
targets.note: Mathlib defines the L-function of a Weierstrass curve over any number field as the Euler product over the height-one spectrum of the ring of integers of the local Euler factors, with the four reduction cases (1 - a_p T + |p| T^2, 1 - T, 1 + T, 1) written out, and the associated LSeries. This is more general than the roadmap's E/Q. The file is sorry-free. No convergence, meromorphic continuation or uniqueness-from-a-connected-domain statement is proved about it.

targets.target: Modular entire continuation and completed functional equation of L(E,s)
targets.note: There is no modularity theorem in either library (a name search for modularity/taniyama over both trees returns only an unrelated combinatorics lemma), so the continuation cannot be transported from the modular side, and nothing proves continuation directly. Mathlib does have the completed L-function of a modular form and its functional equation, and entire continuation for cusp forms, so the target of the transport exists but the bridge does not.

targets.target: Analytic rank as the order of vanishing at s = 1, proved finite
targets.note: The general notion the layer wants - the order of vanishing of an analytic function at a point, with order 0 equivalent to a nonzero value and finiteness from non-vanishing nearby - is complete in Mathlib in full generality (also meromorphicOrderAt). What is missing is an analytic function L(E,-) to apply it to; the layer's own warning that 'an arbitrary analytic germ is not a witness' is the obstruction.

targets.target: Root-number parity relation for the analytic order
targets.note: There is no root number of an elliptic curve and no conductor of an elliptic curve in either library (name searches for conductor return only conductors of Dirichlet characters and of ring extensions). Mathlib has DirichletCharacter.rootNumber, which is the Dirichlet analogue, not the elliptic one.

targets.target: Quadratic twist with every local Euler-factor comparison and the factorization L(E/K,s) = L(E,s) L(E^K,s)
targets.note: The twist itself is built and sorry-free in Tau Ceti: over any commutative ring for quadraticTwistOf and by a separable quadratic extension for quadraticTwist, with the scaling of b2, b4, b6, c4, c6 and Delta, equality of j, the point isomorphism E^L(M) = E(M) twisted by the quadratic character, and the explicit Galois cocycle exhibiting it as an L-form. No local Euler-factor comparison between E, E^K and E/K is proved (this is a local statement about Mathlib's localPolynomial and needs no continuation), and the factorization L(E/K,s) = L(E,s) L(E^K,s) is not stated even as an identity of formal Euler products.

targets.target: Coefficient-field/rationality bridge from weight-two newforms with rational coefficients
targets.note: Tau Ceti has an extensive newform theory (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms: multiplicity one, strong multiplicity one, Atkin-Lehner, eigenvalue fields, nebentypus descent) and Mathlib has the modular L-function, so the modular side of the bridge is substantially built; the bridge to an elliptic curve is not, because modularity is absent.

targets.target: Mordell-Weil lattice modulo torsion, with finite generation and finite torsion
targets.note: The Mordell-Weil theorem is proved in Tau Ceti for an elliptic curve over a number field and, more generally, over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain with per-factor class-group and unit-group finiteness; the weak Mordell-Weil theorem is proved by explicit 2-descent into square classes. The quotient by torsion (PointModTorsion) and the fact that torsion lies in the kernel of the Neron-Tate pairing are both proved. All the files are sorry-free.

targets.target: Regulator and canonical height
targets.note: The canonical height is constructed by Tate's averaging with the standard 1/2 normalization (the docstring notes that the naive x-height belongs to the divisor 2(O)), the exact parallelogram law is proved, height zero is equivalent to finite order, and the regulator is the absolute determinant of the Neron-Tate Gram matrix, proved independent of the basis even across different index types. Sorry-free.

targets.target: Finite-level Selmer groups
targets.note: Only the 2-Selmer group exists, defined by square classes with trivial norm class satisfying the local condition at every finite place and at an auxiliary family of fields, together with the rank bound 2^rank * #E(K)[2] <= #S for any finite S containing the image of the descent map. Its own file records that it does not prove the Selmer group finite; the auxiliary group selmerGroupA is proved finite. There is no Selmer group at general m, no Selmer structure on a general Galois module, and no Sha at all.

targets.target: Rank identity rank E(K) = rank E(Q) + rank E^K(Q) and its lattice-index correction
targets.note: The eigenspace inputs are in Tau Ceti, sorry-free: for a separable quadratic L/K and any field M over L, quadraticTwistPointEquiv identifies E^L(M) with E(M), and transports the action of every sigma in Aut(M/K) to chi(sigma|L) times the action on E(M) - so E^L(K)-points are the sigma = -1 part of E(L) - while exists_baseChange_eq_of_map_eq descends sigma-fixed points of E(L) to E(K). Not proved: the rank identity rank E(L) = rank E(K) + rank E^L(K), the trace/restriction maps on points, or the index of E(K) + E^L(K) in E(L).

targets.target: p-primary Selmer/Sha comparison at odd p and restriction/corestriction at p = 2
targets.note: The finite-group cohomology machinery the layer needs exists: Mathlib has group cohomology with restriction and Shapiro's lemma, and Tau Ceti adds corestriction, Tate cohomology with the Herbrand quotient and continuous (profinite) cohomology with restriction/corestriction/inflation and cup products. But no Selmer or Sha group is built from it, so the comparison itself is absent.

targets.note: Mathlib has integral and minimal models over a DVR and the good/multiplicative/split-multiplicative/additive trichotomy; Tau Ceti has the invariant differential and minimal-model transfer of split multiplicative reduction. Neron models, component groups, Kodaira types, Tate's algorithm, Tamagawa numbers, the real period and Cassels' isogeny-invariance theorem are all absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Compact continuous cochains and continuous cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib defines continuousCohomology in every degree as the homology of homogeneous continuous cochains for a topological group acting continuously on a topological module (so compact coefficients are covered), but computes only H^0 and lists long exact sequences and the comparison with groupCohomology as TODOs. Tau Ceti builds the explicit inhomogeneous complex in degrees <= 2, compares its H^0 with Mathlib's continuousCohomology, compares H^0, H^1 and H^2 with Mathlib's group cohomology when the group is discrete, and proves the colimit description of H^1 over the finite quotients of a profinite group. All files are sorry-free. Nothing compares cohomology with inverse-limit coefficients.

targets.note: Neither library has lim^1 of an inverse system of abelian groups or the Milnor sequence; a name search for lim1/limOne/Rlim/derivedLimit over both trees finds only category-theoretic 'closed under limits' lemmas. Mathlib has AddCommGrp inverse limits but no derived functor of lim.

targets.note: Only the degree-one inflation-restriction sequence 0 -> H^1(G/N, M^N) -> H^1(G, M) -> H^1(N, M) is proved, in Mathlib (discrete) and in Tau Ceti (continuous); Tau Ceti's degree-two inflation only has res o infl = 0. There is no transgression, no five-term sequence, no Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence and no edge map; Mathlib's general spectral-sequence API is not applied to group cohomology.

targets.target: Continuous cup products, twists, duals, corestriction, Shapiro, projection formulas
targets.note: Cup products exist for every bidegree of total degree at most two (00, 01, 10, 02, 20, 11) with associativity, the projection formula in each of those bidegrees, corestriction in degrees 0, 1 and 2 with transversal-independence and cor o res = index, and Shapiro in degrees 0 and 1. Internal Hom of continuous representations is built (ContCohomology/InternalHom.lean). What is not there is a Tate twist of a Galois module, a dual in the sense the roadmap means (Pontryagin dual of a discrete module with contragredient action) or anything in degree >= 3.

targets.target: Integral Kummer comparison H^1(F, Z_p(1)) = lim_m F^x/(F^x)^{p^m}
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the Kummer map K^x -> H^1(G_K, mu_n) for n invertible in K, computes it on cocycles, proves its kernel is (K^x)^n and hence that K^x/(K^x)^n injects into H^1(G_K, mu_n); its own docstring says surjectivity (Hilbert 90 for K^sep/K through the finite-quotient colimit) is the single missing input for the isomorphism at finite level. The p-adic limit over m, the Z_p(1) coefficient module and the comparison with a tensor-product expression for units and S-units are all absent. Mathlib's IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup is the group K(S,n) of S-units mod n-th powers, the target of the S-restricted Kummer map.

targets.target: Which inverse-limit hypotheses hold for each tower (Mittag-Leffler bookkeeping)
targets.note: Mathlib has the Mittag-Leffler condition and eventual ranges for cofiltered systems of types (so for the underlying sets of a tower of groups), with nonempty-sections theorems, and proves that the limit of a tower of surjections surjects onto each term. Missing: lim^1 and the statement that it vanishes under Mittag-Leffler for abelian groups or modules, exactness of inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems, and any tower of Galois cohomology groups to which the bookkeeping could be applied.

duplicates.note: Layer 5 owns the long exact sequence, inflation-restriction and the five-term sequence with transgression - the low-degree part of the Hochschild-Serre target L0 T2 (only the three-term inflation-restriction sequence is delivered, in TauCeti ContCohomology/Inflation).
L0's own text says these general theorems are imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02 and must not be reimplemented; the overlap is by design but the targets are stated in both places.
R02.2 builds the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence with its low-degree identification and restriction/corestriction identities - L0 T2.

D7 is the declared owner of derived inverse limits with lim^1 and Mittag-Leffler conditions, full continuous Hochschild-Serre with edge maps, and the cup/cores/Shapiro normalizations - L0 T1, T2, T3 and T5.
Layer 6 owns corestriction in degrees 0-2 with transversal independence - part of L0 T3 (delivered in TauCeti ContCohomology/Corestriction).
Layer 7 owns coinduced modules and Shapiro's lemma - part of L0 T3 (delivered in degrees 0 and 1).
Layer 8 owns low-degree cup products and the projection formula - part of L0 T3 (delivered in TauCeti ContCohomology/Cup and ProjectionFormula).
Layer 9 owns profinite Hilbert 90 and the Kummer isomorphism at finite level, the input L0 T4 specializes to H^1(F, Z_p(1)).

targets.target: Local invariant map and Tate local duality
targets.note: Neither library has the invariant map of a local field, local Tate duality or a perfect cup-product pairing H^i(K,M) x H^{2-i}(K,M') -> Q/Z. Tau Ceti has an abstract class-formation scaffolding (TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.Formation with levels, normal layers, norms and Tate cohomology carriers) but no invariant map and no reciprocity axiom discharged.

targets.target: Local Euler-characteristic formula
targets.note: Absent; the only eulerChar declarations in either library are Euler characteristics of homological complexes and of coherent sheaves.

targets.target: Cohomology with compact support and the modified real-place terms at p = 2
targets.note: Absent; there is no cohomology with compact support of a global Galois module and no real-place modification in either library.

targets.target: Poitou-Tate nine-term exact sequence
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Finiteness and cohomological-dimension theorems
targets.note: No cohomological dimension of a profinite group in either library, and no finiteness theorem for Galois cohomology of a number field. Tau Ceti proves finiteness of class groups, ray class groups and narrow class groups, which are the classical shadows of these statements, not the statements themselves.

targets.target: Annihilators and saturation of the chosen Selmer local conditions and their unramified/bad-prime comparison terms
targets.note: Depends on the Selmer local conditions of L2, which do not exist.

duplicates.note: R02.3 proves finiteness of finite-coefficient cohomology of G_{F,S}, cohomological-dimension bounds with real-place exceptions and compactly supported cohomology - L1 T2 and T4.
R02.4 proves Poitou-Tate duality and the nine-term sequence with local invariant maps - L1 T3.
D7 owns compact-support arithmetic cohomology and finite/lattice Poitou-Tate duality with the real-place corrections at p = 2 - L1 T2 and T3.
ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 owns the local invariant map, local Tate duality for finite modules and the local Euler-characteristic formula - L1 T0 and T1 (D7 defers local duality to it).
ES.0 verifies the square relating propagated local conditions and annihilators under local duality, with saturated lattice conditions - L1 T5 (AUDIT-24 lists the reverse link).

targets.target: Local conditions as submodules or maps of complexes; unramified, strict, relaxed and Greenberg conditions
targets.note: No Selmer structure on a Galois module exists in either library. The only 'local condition' in either tree is Tau Ceti's elliptic-curve 2-descent local condition (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/LocalCondition.lean), which is the square-class condition of explicit 2-descent, not a submodule of H^1(K_v, T).

targets.target: Selmer group as the kernel of the global-to-local map, with semilocal direct sums
targets.note: Two concrete instances of the pattern exist - the 2-Selmer group of an elliptic curve cut out by local conditions at every finite place, and the S-unit Selmer group K(S,n) - but neither is an instance of a general Selmer structure, and neither is defined as the kernel of a global-to-local map on Galois cohomology.

targets.target: Compact Pontryagin dual with contragredient action and the involution convention
targets.note: Mathlib has the topological Pontryagin dual A ->t* Circle with the compact-open topology (compact for discrete A, discrete for compact A) and its contravariant functoriality PontryaginDual.map, and the character module Hom(A, Q/Z) of an abelian group. Missing: the contragredient Galois action on the dual of a discrete torsion Galois module, the involution convention, and double duality beyond finite abelian groups.

targets.target: Selmer complex as an actual mapping fibre, with its H^1 recovering the classical Selmer group
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib has mapping cones and fibres of morphisms of complexes in general homological algebra, so the categorical tool exists, but there is no Galois cochain complex over a number field to apply it to.

targets.target: Changes of local conditions, primitive/imprimitive exact sequences, lattice-change formulas
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: That layer sets up Selmer structures for a general Galois module first (local-condition subgroups unramified almost everywhere, with the Selmer group inside H^1(K,M)), which is exactly L2's first target.
M.8 also constructs Selmer complexes from explicit local conditions for the Tate and elliptic representations.
PS.4 restates the finite/singular local conditions and their determinant lines.
ES.0 constructs Selmer data from local submodules/subcomplexes of actual cohomology with propagation between T, V and V/T - L2 T0 (AUDIT-24 lists the reverse link).
AutomorphicCongruences L0 compares primitive and imprimitive Selmer groups through the local cohomology exact sequence - L2 T4 (AUDIT-23 lists the reverse link).

targets.target: Iwasawa cohomology H^i_Iw(F,T) via corestriction, identified with cohomology of the induced completed-group-ring representation
targets.note: Corestriction in degrees 0, 1 and 2 exists in Tau Ceti and would be the transition map of the inverse system. Mathlib has the closest thing to the coefficient ring: abstract measures on Z_p with values in Q_p and the Amice transform identifying them with power series, which its own docstring calls the definition of the Iwasawa algebra - but as an analytic object, not as a completed group ring Z_p[[Gamma]], and with no module theory (no characteristic ideal, no structure theorem). There is no Z_p^d-extension, no inverse limit of cohomology groups along corestriction, and hence no Iwasawa cohomology.

targets.target: Finite generation, base change, duality and specialization spectral sequences for Iwasawa cohomology
targets.note: Absent; none of the objects exists.

targets.target: Control theorems with explicit kernels and cokernels
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Determinant-line formulation for perfect Iwasawa complexes and its relation to characteristic ideals
targets.note: No perfect complexes, no determinant functor and no characteristic ideal of a finitely generated torsion Iwasawa module in either library.

targets.target: Infinite-level local conditions defined by limits
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: PG.5 owns the psi-complex and the derived Iwasawa comparison, the same Iwasawa cohomology object from the (phi,Gamma)-module side.
PS.4 also asks for determinant lines of perfect complexes and their invariance, which L3 states for Iwasawa complexes.
PMIA L5 constructs determinant lines of perfect complexes and relates them to characteristic ideals, with specialization exact sequences - L3 T1/T3, which L3 itself says it takes from that layer.

targets.target: Recovering class-group and p-ramified modules from Selmer groups of Tate twists
targets.note: The class group, its finiteness and the class number are complete in Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and Mathlib has the mod-n and p-adic cyclotomic characters that define Tate twists. But there is no Selmer group of a Tate twist and no comparison exact sequence, so the recovery statement cannot be formed.

targets.target: Plus/minus, Tate-dual and involution comparisons
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Finite Bloch-Kato and ordinary local conditions with their exceptional factors
targets.note: No period rings of p-adic Hodge theory beyond the perfectoid B_dR constructions in Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean, and no crystalline or de Rham local condition in either library.

targets.target: Hodge/gamma-factor notion of criticality on explicit realization data
targets.note: The layer's own instruction is to use the HodgeStructures carrier for the archimedean linear algebra, and that carrier exists and is sorry-free in Tau Ceti, with Hodge numbers, Tate twists and conjugation. The gamma factor exists for Dirichlet characters. No definition of criticality is stated anywhere in either library.

targets.target: Statement of RJW Conjecture 13.21 with its criticality, ordinary-filtration, corank and analytic hypotheses
targets.note: No conjecture of this kind is stated in either library, and there is no p-adic L-function to state it about.

duplicates.note: M.8 also constructs the crystalline/semistable local conditions at p for the Tate and elliptic representations and their Selmer complexes.
L1 of PadicHodgeRegulators owns the Bloch-Kato maps and the finite local condition that L4 defines once R09 supplies the period rings.
MIMC L5 states the Greenberg and Coates-Perrin-Riou conjectures from RJW as propositions - L4 T4 (AUDIT-26 lists the reverse link).
APL L5 states the Coates-Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence problem on a specified realization, critical set and periods without asserting it - L4 T3 and T4 (AUDIT-23 lists the reverse link).

targets.target: W_2(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(2)) as a cyclotomic Galois module, and w_2(F) = #W_2(F)
targets.note: The coefficients exist: Mathlib has the mod-n cyclotomic character and the Z_p^x-valued p-adic cyclotomic character (continuous on Galois groups), Tau Ceti has mu_n of the separable closure as a discrete G_K-module (KummerCoeff) with H^0 of discrete G_K-modules, and w_1(F) is NumberField.Units.torsionOrder. What is missing is Q/Z(2) as a Galois module, W_2(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(2)) and w_2(F); the layer explicitly warns that torsionOrder is not a substitute.

targets.target: K_2(O_F), its Steinberg/tame-kernel comparison, and its finiteness
targets.note: No K_2 in either library: no Steinberg group or Steinberg symbols (the Steinberg names are Lie-theoretic, and Tau Ceti's quaternion 'Steinberg relation' is about algebras), no Milnor K-theory, no tame symbol or tame kernel and no finiteness theorem. Tau Ceti's K-theory is K_0 only (exact categories, and finitely generated projective modules over a ring).

targets.target: The analytically continued Dedekind zeta function
targets.note: Mathlib defines zeta_F as the LSeries of the ideal-counting function and proves the Dirichlet class number formula for the residue at s = 1 as a one-sided real limit; Tau Ceti proves its Euler product and its nonvanishing on Re s > 1 and computes the exact abscissa of convergence. Neither library continues zeta_F past Re s = 1, so zeta_F(-1) is not defined (Mathlib's LSeries is 0 by convention outside the region of convergence). The file's own TODO asks only to generalize the construction.

targets.target: The proposition BirchTate(F): zeta_F(-1) = (-1)^[F:Q] #K_2(O_F)/w_2(F)
targets.note: Cannot be stated: both sides are missing. Mathlib does have Module.finrank Q F for the degree and NumberField.IsTotallyReal for the hypothesis.

duplicates.note: N.4 owns the roots-of-unity-with-twists module, which is exactly B.1's W_2(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(2)).
T.5 identifies K_2(O_F) with the tame kernel of K_2(F) via the localisation theorem and gives finite presentations - B.1 T1.

AL.1 proves continuation and the functional equation of Tate zeta integrals, which give the continued Dedekind zeta function B.1 T2 asks for (R.5 and DirichletPadicLFunctions L0 both import it from AL.1).

targets.target: zeta_F(-1) is nonzero and rational for totally real F
targets.note: zeta_F is not continued to s = -1 in either library, so neither rationality nor nonvanishing there can be stated. The analogous statement for Q is available (see B.3).

targets.target: Sign from the functional equation and positivity in the convergent half-plane
targets.note: Mathlib has a general abstract framework (WeakFEPair / IsStrongFEPair) for deriving a functional equation from a self-duality of a Mellin pair, and uses it for Dirichlet characters and modular forms; Tau Ceti proves zeta_F is nonzero for Re s > 1, which is the positivity input. There is no functional equation for zeta_F, so no sign.

targets.target: The gamma-factor limit rather than evaluation of a product containing a gamma pole
targets.note: The archimedean factors Gammaℝ and Gammaℂ that the Dedekind zeta function's completion needs are defined in Mathlib, with the residue of Gammaℝ at 0, the reflection quotient Gammaℝ(s)/Gammaℝ(1-s) and the reciprocal at 2 - s, all sorry-free; the file's own docstring says these are the factors needed for the Dedekind zeta function. Only the limit statement for zeta_F itself is missing, because zeta_F has no completion here.

targets.target: Equality of prime valuations v_l(#K_2) = v_l(w_2) + v_l(|zeta_F(-1)|)
targets.note: Every quantity is absent.

targets.target: A general lemma reconstructing a positive rational from all its prime valuations
targets.note: Mathlib proves that two nonzero naturals are equal iff all their p-adic valuations agree; the rational version the layer asks for is not stated but follows from it via numerator and denominator, and padicValRat with its arithmetic is available. This is the one target of the layer that is nearly library-complete.

targets.target: Denominator integrality only after the identity or an independent Deligne-Ribet result
targets.note: No Deligne-Ribet integrality and no p-adic L-function in either library.

duplicates.note: PS.1 also asks for normalized-value statements with sign and coefficient field, of which B.2's sign theorem is the Dedekind-zeta instance.

APL L3 constructs the Deligne-Ribet pseudo-measure including algebraicity of negative critical values and integral congruences - the rationality of zeta_F(-1) (T0) and the Deligne-Ribet integrality B.2 T5 refers to.

targets.target: zeta_Q(-1) = -1/12 from the existing Bernoulli/zeta theory
targets.note: Mathlib proves zeta(-k) = (-1)^k * bernoulli(k+1)/(k+1) for every natural k, from the Hurwitz-zeta special values, with the full analytic continuation of riemannZeta behind it; with bernoulli_two : bernoulli 2 = 1/6 this gives zeta(-1) = -1/12 in one rewrite. The general theorem covers the layer's target in more than the stated generality, sorry-free.

targets.target: K_2(Z) = Z/2, proved independently of Birch-Tate
targets.note: No K_2 and no K_1 in either library; Tau Ceti's K-theory is K_0 only, so K_2(Z) = Z/2 cannot be stated.

targets.target: w_2(Q) = 24 by explicit cyclotomic computation
targets.note: W_2 is not defined; Mathlib's cyclotomic theory (primitive roots, cyclotomic fields, their Galois groups) would supply the computation but the object is missing.

targets.target: A real quadratic example: certified tame kernel, explicit w_2 and the factorization into Riemann and Dirichlet L-functions
targets.note: Mathlib has Dirichlet L-functions with continuation, and Tau Ceti has a detailed quadratic-field library (minimal polynomial and degree, rings of integers, splitting and inertness, class groups, genus theory, narrow class groups), so both factors of the would-be factorization exist as objects; the factorization zeta_F = zeta * L(chi_D) itself is not proved in either library, and the tame kernel does not exist.

evidence.target: zeta_Q(-1) = -1/12 from the existing Bernoulli/zeta theory

duplicates.note: N.8 owns the certified K-theory examples, including K_2(Z), that B.3 wants to import.
T.5 proves K_2(Z) = Z/2 with generator {-1,-1} and a certified tame-kernel presentation of a nontrivial arithmetic example - B.3 T1 and T3.

targets.target: Tate's comparison of K_2 with Galois cohomology
targets.note: Needs K_2, which is absent, and Galois cohomology of a number field with Z/l(2) coefficients, which is also absent; Tau Ceti's continuous cohomology exists only in degrees <= 2 for a general topological group, with no arithmetic input.

targets.target: Localisation sequence from O_F to O_F[1/l]
targets.note: No K-theory localisation sequence. Mathlib does have the S-integers of a Dedekind domain and their unit and class groups, which is the degree-<=1 shadow of the sequence.

targets.target: Identification of the finite Euler characteristic with the interpolated zeta-value
targets.note: No p-adic zeta function and no Iwasawa-theoretic Euler characteristic in either library.

targets.target: N(v) - 1 is an l-adic unit at a prime above l
targets.note: The elementary ingredient - the absolute norm of a prime and the fact that the residue field has order a power of the residue characteristic, so N(v) - 1 is prime to it - is entirely within Mathlib's ramification theory, and Mathlib even proves torsionOrder divides N(v) - 1. The statement in the K-theoretic diagram the layer wants is absent because the diagram is.

targets.target: Identification of the denominator group with the l-primary part of W_2(F)
targets.note: W_2 is absent.

duplicates.note: N.6 owns the even K-groups and their arithmetic cohomology comparison - Tate's K_2-to-Galois-cohomology map is its degree-two case.
N.2 owns the localisation sequence and finite support that B.4 uses to pass from O_F to O_F[1/l].
M.3 proves Tate's degree-two theorem K_2(O_{F,S})/l^r = H^2_et(O_{F,S}, mu^{(x)2}) - B.4 T0.
T.7 proves Tate's K_2-Galois-cohomology comparison for local and global fields and S-integers - B.4 T0, which names T.7 as sufficient.
I.5's stated endpoint is the equality of finite arithmetic Euler characteristics with the p-adic valuation of zeta_F(-1) - B.4 T2.

targets.target: Birch-Tate for totally real abelian F/Q including the 2-primary part
targets.note: Neither side of the formula exists.

targets.target: The classical abelian main conjecture (Mazur-Wiles) route
targets.note: No Iwasawa main conjecture of any kind in either library; there is no Iwasawa algebra, no characteristic ideal and no p-adic L-function.

targets.target: The 2-adic comparison
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The hypothesis that F/Q is abelian and totally real, applied to F rather than to layers of its cyclotomic Z_2-extension
targets.note: The hypothesis itself is a Mathlib class with its basic API (real embeddings, no complex places, transfer along ring equivalences and to subfields), and abelian Galois extensions are standard Mathlib. Only the theorem the hypothesis would feed is missing. Kronecker-Weber is not proved in general; Tau Ceti proves its exponent-two case (a Galois extension of Q with Galois group of exponent dividing 2 embeds in a cyclotomic field).

duplicates.note: I.5 proves the Mazur-Wiles abelian-Q main conjecture and Wiles's totally real odd-primary main conjecture, the classical main-conjecture route B.5 states as its own proof step.

targets.target: The main-conjecture formulation needed for Kolster's implication (from I.9/I.10)
targets.note: Absent; no Iwasawa main conjecture over a totally real field exists in either library.

targets.target: Formalisation of Kolster's implication to the 2-primary Birch-Tate identity, with finite descent and real-place correction
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The explicit comparison table (Iwasawa module, dual/twist, compact-support convention, specialisation character, finite cohomology groups, archimedean contribution, S-Euler factors, W_2)
targets.note: None of the eight entries exists as a library object; this is a bookkeeping table over absent mathematics rather than a separable process task.

targets.target: Absence of finite submodules in the relevant Iwasawa module
targets.note: Absent; there is no Iwasawa module.

targets.target: Combination of B.4 and B.6 through B.2 to the full totally real theorem
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: I.10 compares the Kurihara formulation with Kolster's classical one used in the implication to 2-primary Birch-Tate, with twists, duality, omitted primes, finite modules and real places - the same comparison table B.6 requires (AUDIT-25 lists the reverse link).
I.9 formalises Kurihara's all-prime determinant main conjecture over an arbitrary totally real base with F = k allowed, the main-conjecture formulation B.6 lists as its first target.

targets.target: #K_2(O_{F,S}) = #K_2(O_F) * prod_{v in S} (Nv - 1) from localisation
targets.note: No K_2 and no localisation sequence in either library.

targets.target: zeta_{F,S}(s) = zeta_F(s) prod_{v in S} (1 - Nv^{-s}) through an Euler-factor API
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Euler-factor API the layer asks for: local Euler factors at height-one primes, the Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function on Re s > 1, restriction of Euler-product data away from a set of primes (EulerProductData.restrictAway) and the finite Euler product over a finite set S. Not stated: zeta_{F,S}(s) = zeta_F(s) prod_{v in S}(1 - Nv^{-s}) as an identity of L-series, and anything at s = -1, since zeta_F is not continued.

targets.target: The compatible S-formula zeta_{F,S}(-1) = (-1)^{[F:Q]+|S|} #K_2(O_{F,S})/w_2(F)
targets.note: Absent for the same reasons as B.1.

targets.target: Commutation of changing S with the regulator/cohomology comparisons
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: N.2 owns the localisation sequence and the finite-support statement from which B.7's K_2 product formula is read off.
T.5 obtains, for S-integers, the exact sequence comparing their tame kernel with the integral one - the localisation step of B.7 T0.

targets.target: Statement infrastructure for Lichtenbaum formulas at all negative integers
targets.note: Absent; requires higher K-groups, Borel regulators and determinant lines, none of which exists in either library.

targets.target: Odd-primary totally real even-weight consequences from the appropriate Iwasawa theorem
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Real-place and 2-primary corrections from the etale/motivic comparison
targets.note: Absent; no etale or motivic cohomology in either library.

targets.target: Higher regulator formula for fields with complex places, with order of vanishing and normalised covolume
targets.note: The weight-one instance of the statement is complete: Mathlib defines the covolume regulator of the unit lattice and proves the class number formula, and the general notion of order of vanishing of an analytic function is available. Higher Borel regulators and the leading terms at negative integers are absent.

targets.target: Separate statement of the integral/equivariant refinement and of Borel's rational-proportionality theorem
targets.note: Borel's theorem on the ranks of K-groups of a number field and its regulator proportionality is absent, as is any equivariant refinement.

duplicates.note: PS.3 states the same Beilinson-type leading-term and regulator-determinant targets from the motivic side.

R.5 proves the order of vanishing of zeta_F at 1-j and Borel's regulator theorem with the rational proportionality between leading coefficient and regulator covolume - B.8's higher regulator formula and its separately stated Borel theorem.

targets.target: Arithmetic carriers: number field, ring of integers, primes, O_{F,S} as a localisation, independence of presentation and compatibility with enlarging S
targets.note: The carriers exist: Mathlib defines the S-integers and S-units of the fraction field of any Dedekind domain by valuations, with O_empty = R, and Tau Ceti proves O_S is a Dedekind domain whose ideals are all extended from R and that the S-units grow with S. The layer's two theorems do not: Tau Ceti's SInteger/Basic.lean states that the S-integers are 'not in general a localization of R' and treats them only as an overring, and neither library proves that O_{F,S} is a localization of O_F for a number field (no IsLocalization instance), independence of that presentation, or monotonicity of the ring O_S in S (only the unit group, Set.unit_mono).

targets.target: K_0(O_{F,S}) is Z + Cl(O_{F,S})
targets.note: Both sides exist separately but the isomorphism does not. Tau Ceti defines K_0 of the finitely generated projective modules of any ring as the exact K_0 of finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure R, proves that structure is the split one, and builds the Cartan map to G_0 with the resolution theorem; Mathlib identifies the class group with Pic, and Tau Ceti proves Cl(O_S) = Cl(R) modulo the classes of the primes of S, with finiteness. Nothing computes K_0 of a Dedekind domain or of O_{F,S} as Z + Cl (no rank/determinant map, no Steinitz classification).

targets.target: K_1(O_{F,S}) is O_{F,S}^x by the determinant, kept distinct from K_1(F) = F^x
targets.note: Again only the right-hand side: Mathlib identifies the S-units of K with the units of the ring of S-integers, and Tau Ceti proves that group finitely generated (Dirichlet's S-unit theorem in the finite-generation form). There is no K_1 of a ring and no determinant map out of it in either library, and no Whitehead group.

targets.target: Comparison of norms and extension of ideals with K-theory transfer and pullback
targets.note: Extension of ideals to O_S and the relative norm on class groups exist in Tau Ceti, which is the degree-zero shadow of pullback and transfer; the K-theoretic maps themselves do not exist.

duplicates.note: Z.4 proves K_0(A) = Z + Pic(A) by rank and determinant for Dedekind domains and specialises to O_F and O_{F,S} as the quotient of the class group by the primes in S - exactly N.1 T1 ("import Z").
U.4 proves SK_1(O_{F,S}) = 0 (Bass-Milnor-Serre) and K_1(O_{F,S}) = O_{F,S}^x, distinguishing it from K_1(F) - exactly N.1 T2 ("import U").

targets.target: The localisation long exact sequence for K_n of O_{F,S}, F and the residue fields
targets.note: No K-theory, hence no localisation sequence. Mathlib and Tau Ceti have long exact sequences in homological algebra and in group cohomology, but nothing K-theoretic.

targets.target: Finite support of the maps to the direct sum, and compatibility with field extensions
targets.note: The finite-support statement at the level of valuations - a nonzero element has nontrivial valuation at only finitely many primes - is proved in Tau Ceti; the K-theoretic statement is absent.

targets.target: Interpretation in degrees 0-2: tame-kernel sequence, S-unit valuation sequence, ideal-class-group sequence
targets.note: Two of the three named consequences are proved in classical form in Tau Ceti and are the layer's degree-0 and degree-1 rows: the S-unit valuation sequence 1 -> R^x -> (O_S)^x -> Z^S is Set.unitValuation_ker, and the ideal-class-group sequence Cl(R) -> Cl(O_S) -> 1 with kernel generated by the classes of the primes of S is ker_integer_extendedHom plus integerClassGroupEquiv. They are not derived from a K-theoretic localisation sequence, and the tame-kernel row (degree 2) is absent because K_2 is.

targets.target: The odd-degree isomorphism K_n(O_{F,S}) = K_n(F) for n >= 3 as a separate theorem
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: K.3 proves devissage and Quillen localisation for a Serre subcategory of an abelian category; N.2's localisation sequence for O_{F,S}, F and the residue fields is its Dedekind-domain case.
B.7 restates the S-integer localisation consequence #K_2(O_{F,S}) = #K_2(O_F) prod (Nv - 1).
T.5 proves the tame-kernel exact sequence 0 -> K_2(O_F) -> K_2(F) -> (+) k(p)^x -> 0 and its S-integer version - the degree-two row of N.2 T2.

targets.target: Finite generation of K_n(O_{F,S}) for every n >= 1 (Quillen)
targets.note: The n = 1 case in classical form - finite generation of the S-units - is proved in Tau Ceti for an arbitrary Dedekind domain with finitely generated units, and Cl(O_S) is finite, which is the n = 0 case. Quillen's arithmetic-group finiteness, the finite-type homotopy input and stable general linear groups are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Rank formula for K_n(O_{F,S}), n >= 2: r1+r2 for n = 1 mod 4, r2 for n = 3 mod 4, 0 for n even
targets.note: Absent; Borel's stable cohomology theorem is not in either library.

targets.target: rank K_1 is the S-unit rank, distinct from the n = 1 mod 4 formula
targets.note: For S empty this is Dirichlet's unit theorem, complete in Mathlib: rank = #InfinitePlace - 1 = r1 + r2 - 1, with the unit lattice, its rank, a fundamental system and the regulator. The refinement to rank + |S| for general S is explicitly noted as absent in Tau Ceti's own S-unit file.

targets.target: Positive even groups of S-integers are finite; positive even groups of F are infinite torsion
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: R.1 owns arithmetic groups and the finiteness infrastructure that Quillen's finite-generation proof needs, and Borel's stable cohomology theorem supplies the rank formula.
R.3 proves the period-four rank formula for K_n of rings of S-integers - N.3 T1.

targets.note: Absent; Mathlib has the cyclotomic fields, their Galois groups and primitive roots that the test would use.

targets.note: Absent: there is no K-theory beyond K_0 in either library, so no odd K-groups.

targets.note: Absent. Mathlib has NumberField.IsTotallyComplex and the counts r1, r2 (nrRealPlaces, nrComplexPlaces), so the shape of the statement is expressible but no group is there to compute.

targets.target: Naturality of the e-invariant/Chern maps, their kernels and the extension classes
targets.note: Absent; there is no topological K-theory, no e-invariant and no Chern character in either library.

targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Finite cohomological descriptions of the even K-groups, with inverse-limit, real-place and exceptional-field corrections
targets.note: Absent; requires etale cohomology of arithmetic schemes and the motivic-to-etale comparison, neither of which exists in either library.

targets.note: The class-group and unit inputs exist and are finite/finitely generated; local norm groups exist in Tau Ceti's local field unit filtration; the cohomological descriptions they would feed do not.

targets.note: Neither tame nor wild kernel exists; there is no K_2 to take a kernel of, and no tame symbol.

targets.target: The arithmetic Bernoulli convention B_1 = -1/2 and conversion from the topologists' numbering
targets.note: The arithmetic convention is Mathlib's: bernoulli has bernoulli_one = -1/2, sorry-free, with von Staudt-Clausen and the p-adic valuation of B_2k. The 'topologists' numbering' the layer asks to convert from is not bernoulli' (the B_1 = +1/2 convention that bernoulli_eq_bernoulli'_of_ne_one relates): Weibel's K-book VI, which the roadmap cites, uses 'the topologists' B_k from [MSt], all of which are positive; number theorists would write it as (-1)^{k+1} B_2k'. Neither library defines that sequence or proves the sign of B_2k (it is only implicit in riemannZeta_two_mul_nat), so the conversion is absent.

targets.target: Finite cyclotomic character eigenspaces related to class groups, Bernoulli numerators and the Kummer regular-prime criterion
targets.note: There is no definition of a regular prime in either library (grep -rn -i 'regular prime' over both trees returns nothing) and no Herbrand-Ribet or Kummer criterion; Mathlib's cyclotomic-field theory (Galois group, discriminant, PID cases, the Q(zeta_3) and FLT-three material) is the raw material but the eigenspace projectors are absent.

targets.target: For an odd regular prime l, vanishing of the l-primary part of the tame kernel of Q(zeta_l)
targets.note: Absent: no tame kernel, no regular primes.

targets.note: The arithmetic inputs exist: Mathlib proves that p has a unique prime above it in Q(zeta_p), with ramification index p - 1 and inertia degree 1, and Tau Ceti computes the effect of inverting primes on class groups (Cl(O_S) = Cl(R)/<S>). The K-theoretic conclusion about the l-primary residue-field term is not stated.

Absent. Mathlib has Z[i] as GaussianInt with its Euclidean structure, so the carrier exists.

targets.target: The S-integer exact sequence for Z[1/p]
targets.note: The degree-0 and degree-1 rows of the sequence for an arbitrary Dedekind domain and finite S, hence for Z[1/p], are proved in Tau Ceti; the K-theoretic rows are absent.

targets.target: For Q: K_2(Q) infinite while the tame kernel K_2(Z) has order 2
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Restriction of scalars (Weil restriction) for algebraic groups, and the induced arithmetic subgroup
targets.note: Neither library has Weil restriction of scalars for group schemes or algebraic groups: greps for `weilRestriction`, `WeilRestriction`, `RestrictionOfScalars` over group objects return nothing. Only module/algebra-level restriction of scalars (Mathlib's `RestrictScalars`, Tau Ceti's `CommAlgCat.restrictScalars`) exists, which is the wrong direction.

targets.target: Haar measure and Tamagawa measure on an adelic algebraic group
targets.note: General Haar measure on a locally compact group and the adele ring of a number field both exist, but nothing named or described as a Tamagawa measure does: `grep -rn -i tamagawa` over both trees returns no hits. The convergence factors, local measures and their product are absent.

targets.target: Reduction theory: minimal rational parabolics, Siegel sets, finite covering of the arithmetic quotient, finite volume
targets.note: Only the classical SL₂(ℤ) case exists. Mathlib proves every point of ℍ is SL₂(ℤ)-equivalent to a point of the standard fundamental domain 𝒟 (ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd); Tau Ceti proves 𝒟 has finite invariant volume (ModularGroup.volume_fd_lt_top), that its interior is a measure-theoretic fundamental domain for PSL₂(ℤ) (isFundamentalDomain_fdo), and tiles a fundamental domain for every subgroup by cosets. Minimal rational parabolics, Siegel sets, finite covering and finite volume for a general arithmetic group — AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.3's targets — are absent; the value vol(SL₂(ℤ)\ℍ) = π/3 is not proved either.

targets.target: Borel–Serre compactification, finite-complex models for arithmetic quotients, torsion-stabilizer descent
targets.note: `borel.serre` matches nothing in either library; there is no manifold-with-corners compactification of a locally symmetric space and no finiteness-property theory for arithmetic groups.

targets.target: Orders in central division algebras over a number field, and Borel's block-inclusion maps
targets.note: Central simple algebras, Wedderburn, Skolem–Noether, splitting and the Brauer group are developed in both libraries (Mathlib.Algebra.Central/BrauerGroup, TauCeti.Algebra.CentralSimple/BrauerGroup), but the *arithmetic* of orders — maximal orders in a division algebra over a number field, their unit groups as arithmetic groups — is absent (`maximal order` matches nothing).

targets.target: Finite generation / finite-type homotopy properties of arithmetic groups
targets.note: Finite generation is available for the simplest arithmetic groups only. Mathlib proves SL₂(ℤ) = ⟨S, T⟩ (SpecialLinearGroup.SL2Z_generators), Schreier's lemma that finite-index subgroups of finitely generated groups are finitely generated (instance Subgroup.fg_of_index_ne_zero), finite index of the congruence subgroups Γ(N), Γ₀(N), Γ₁(N), and finite generation of (𝓞_K)ˣ (a Monoid.FG instance in Units/DirichletTheorem.lean); Tau Ceti proves SL_n(ℤ) is generated by elementary transvections. Group.FG for SL₂(ℤ) or its congruence subgroups is not stated, and there is no finite-generation or finite-presentation theorem for general arithmetic groups (Borel–Harish-Chandra), no finite-type classifying space and no finite-type homotopy result.

duplicates.note: AA.3 is the declared owner of Siegel sets, reduction theory, finite covering and finite volume; R.1 restates the same targets as an import and then specialises them to division-algebra orders.
ALS.2 owns the Borel–Serre compactification, its manifold-with-corners structure and the homotopy equivalence from the interior, which R.1 lists as imported targets.

N.3:finite-generation proves finite generation of K_n(O_{F,S}) and explicitly develops 'the arithmetic-group finiteness and finite-type homotopy input in Quillen's proof', the same finiteness infrastructure R.1 asks for.
AA.1 constructs the base-change and restriction-of-scalars equivalences for adelic points, the restriction of scalars R.1 lists first among its imported targets.
AA.2 constructs Tamagawa measures from invariant differential forms and convergence factors, the Haar/Tamagawa-measure target R.1 imports.

targets.target: Continuous group-cochain complex of a topological group with topological coefficients
targets.note: Mathlib defines the homogeneous continuous cochain complex TopRep.homogeneousCochains and continuousCohomology for any topological group acting on a topological module (action continuous on the module only), built from iterated C(G, C(G, …)) rather than C(Gⁿ, M); its TODO lists the n-ary description, the comparison with group cohomology and long exact sequences as missing. Tau Ceti adds restriction and inflation in all degrees on this object, and a separate explicit inhomogeneous model (TauCeti.ContCohomology) in degrees ≤ 2 with a long exact sequence, Shapiro (degrees 0–1), corestriction (0–2) and low-degree cup products. This covers the continuous-cochain complex; it is not specialised to real Lie groups, and there is no differentiable-cochain complex or smoothing comparison.

targets.target: Relative Lie-algebra cochain complex C*(g,K;V) and its cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib has only the bottom of the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex — one- and two-cochains with d₁₂, d₂₃ and two-cocycles, built for Lie-algebra extensions (file is sorry-free). There is no cochain complex in all degrees, no Lie-algebra cohomology functor, and nothing relative to a compact subgroup K.

targets.target: Complex of G-invariant V-valued differential forms on G/K and its identification with relative Lie cochains
targets.note: No invariant-form complex on a homogeneous space; `invariant forms` and `G/K` searches find only Lie-theoretic invariant bilinear forms (Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.InvariantForm), which is unrelated.

targets.target: van Est isomorphism H*_cont(G,V) ≅ H*(g,K;V)
targets.note: `vanest` matches no declaration and `van Est` no docstring in either tree.

targets.target: Comparison to the arithmetic subgroup; compatibility with block inclusions, primitive classes and coefficient extension
targets.note: Depends on the previous three targets and on arithmetic quotients, none of which exist.

evidence.target: Continuous group-cochain complex of a topological group with topological coefficients
evidence.name: TopRep.homogeneousCochains

The full ALS.5 compares Betti, de Rham and relative Lie algebra cohomology of the arithmetic quotients in characteristic zero via local systems, using AF.1a; this is the arithmetic-subgroup comparison R.2 says it will construct.

targets.target: Stable cohomology of the compact duals of the classical groups (exterior algebra on primitive generators)
targets.note: Neither library computes H*(U(n);ℚ), H*(O(n);ℚ) or their stable limits; there is no cohomology ring of a Lie group at all, and no fibration-based computation.

targets.target: Stable-range comparison between arithmetic-group cohomology and the compact dual, with explicit bounds
targets.note: Requires the arithmetic quotients of R.1 and the invariant-form complex of R.2; none present.

targets.target: Rational Hurewicz theorem
targets.note: `hurewicz` matches no declaration in either library; Mathlib has no Hurewicz theorem, rational or integral.

targets.target: Plus-construction comparison K_n(R) = π_n(BGL(R)⁺)
targets.note: No plus construction: `plusConstruction`, `quillenPlus`, `BGL` all return nothing. There is no higher algebraic K-theory in either library.

targets.target: Borel's Proposition 12.2: rank K_i of an order in a central division algebra, period-four pattern 0, r₁+r₂, 0, r₂
targets.note: Only the invariants r₁, r₂ and the unit rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 of Dirichlet's theorem exist (K₁(O_F) ≅ O_F^× by Bass–Milnor–Serre, which neither library has; the class group belongs to K₀, not K₁). The theorem itself has no statement, since K_i is undefined for i ≥ 2.

targets.target: The component regulator for an embedding F ↪ ℂ and complex-conjugation parity
targets.note: No construction. The regulators in the libraries are Mathlib's unit regulator NumberField.Units.regulator (and regOfFamily) and Tau Ceti's Néron–Tate regulator of an elliptic curve, WeierstrassCurve.Affine.regulator; there is no Borel regulator or any map on higher K-groups.

targets.target: The assembled map r_j : K_{2j-1}(F) → V_j(F) with dim V_j = r₁+r₂ (j odd), r₂ (j even), and its naturality/transfer/Adams-weight compatibilities
targets.note: K_{2j-1}(F) does not exist, so neither the source nor the map can be stated; Adams operations on K-theory are also absent.

targets.target: Determinant line, regulator covolume of the torsion-free K-group, and full-lattice image
targets.note: The j=1 instance of this exact package is fully proved in Mathlib: the unit lattice is a full ℤ-lattice (Dirichlet), its covolume is `NumberField.Units.regulator`, and `ZLattice.covolume` is the general covolume machinery with basis-independence. The roadmap document does not mention this. For j≥2 nothing exists.

targets.target: The Dedekind zeta function of a number field
targets.note: ζ_F is defined in Mathlib as the L-series of the ideal-counting function, and Tau Ceti proves its Euler product, non-vanishing for Re s > 1 and abscissa of absolute convergence. Both are sorry-free.

targets.target: Completed zeta with archimedean factors, analytic continuation and functional equation
targets.note: Mathlib has completion, continuation and the functional equation only for the Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions over ℚ (via Hurwitz zeta and Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.AbstractFuncEq), together with Deligne's Γℝ/Γℂ factors. Nothing continues ζ_F past Re s > 1 for a general number field, and there is no Hecke/Tate proof; `NumberField.dedekindZeta` has no continuation lemma.

targets.target: Tate integrals / Poisson summation route with normalised Haar measures and discriminant
targets.note: Poisson summation over ℝ and the adele ring exist, but there are no adelic Schwartz–Bruhat functions, no local or global Tate zeta integrals, and no adelic Poisson summation.

targets.target: Order of vanishing of ζ_F at 1−j equals dim V_j(F), for j≥2, and the leading coefficient
targets.note: Not statable: ζ_F is only defined on its half-plane of convergence, and V_j(F) is undefined. For F = ℚ Mathlib proves only vanishing and values at negative integers — ζ(−2n) = 0 (riemannZeta_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one), ζ(−n) via Bernoulli numbers, and the trivial zeros of even and odd Dirichlet L-functions — with no order-of-vanishing statement (no analyticOrderAt/meromorphicOrderAt result for any zeta or L-function) and no leading coefficient.

targets.target: Borel's regulator theorem: rational proportionality of the leading coefficient and the regulator covolume
targets.note: The j=1 analogue — the Dirichlet class number formula relating the residue of ζ_F at s=1 to the regulator, class number, torsion order and discriminant — is fully proved in Mathlib, sorry-free. That is the only proportionality statement available; Borel's theorem for j≥2 is absent.

evidence.target: The Dedekind zeta function of a number field
evidence.name: NumberField.dedekindZeta

duplicates.note: AL.1 owns the Tate zeta integrals, local functional equation, gamma factors and the global continuation/functional equation by Poisson summation that R.5's first paragraph imports.
B.2 proves that ζ_F(−1) is nonzero (and rational) for totally real F from the functional equation — the j=2, r₂=0 case of R.5's order-of-vanishing statement at 1−j.

targets.target: Local Haar/Tamagawa measures on an algebraic group over a local field and their product over all places
targets.note: Only the general existence/uniqueness of Haar measure on a locally compact group and the adele ring are available; there is no measure on an adelic group, no convergence factors, and no Tamagawa number.

targets.target: Finite-volume integrals of the adelic quotient and the discriminant/archimedean conversion factors
targets.note: No finiteness-of-volume theorem for G(F)\G(𝔸)¹ exists and `Tamagawa` has no hits. targets.target: Primitive cohomology pairings and the comparison of Bloch's Tamagawa formulation with Borel's
targets.note: Both sides of the comparison (R.3/R.4 Borel classes and the Tamagawa description) are absent.

targets.target: The Beilinson/Deligne regulator on motivic cohomology
targets.note: No Deligne cohomology (`DeligneCohomology`, `deligne cohomology` have no hits) and no motivic cohomology, so the target of the comparison does not exist.

targets.target: The precise scalar between Borel's and Beilinson's normalisations (the factor-of-2 convention) and its r-th power on determinants
targets.note: Both maps are absent, so the scalar is not statable.

targets.target: Weight-two test against the Bloch–Wigner regulator
targets.note: The Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z) and Li₂(z) are not defined in either library (the only textual mention of the dilogarithm is a docstring aside in Mathlib's LogTrigonometric.lean). Mathlib does have Li_s on the unit circle: HurwitzZeta.expZeta a s continues Σ e^{2πian}/n^s, and its imaginary part sinZeta a 2 is the Clausen function, i.e. D restricted to roots of unity. No Bloch-group descent or comparison with a regulator exists.

targets.target: Zero-rank cases over ℚ and the rank-one weight-two regulator of an imaginary quadratic field
targets.note: Requires K₃ and the Bloch–Wigner map; neither exists.

targets.target: Coordinate-free maps versus computational matrices, with the linking equality
targets.note: Nothing to export.

M.8 constructs the real Deligne cycle-class maps and the rational regulator from motivic cohomology — the Beilinson/Deligne regulator that R.7 lists as its first target and compares with Borel's map.

targets.target: The smooth projective scheme of a Weierstrass equation over a field, with its section at infinity
targets.note: Mathlib has Proj of an ℕ-graded ring as a Scheme, and Weierstrass curves in affine, projective and Jacobian coordinates, but no elliptic curve is ever produced as an `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`: `grep -rn Scheme` over both libraries' EllipticCurve directories returns nothing. The projective model is a quotient of a point set, not a scheme.

targets.target: Affine-chart equations, smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness, regularity of the curve
targets.note: Nonsingularity of a Weierstrass point is defined pointwise in Mathlib, but there is no scheme to be smooth, proper, geometrically connected or regular; Tau Ceti's AlgebraicGeometry/Scheme/Regular.lean and Morphisms/Smooth/GeometricallyReduced.lean are general and unconnected to curves.

targets.target: Identification of the function field of the scheme
targets.note: Both halves exist separately: Mathlib defines the function field of an irreducible scheme and the function field of a Weierstrass curve as the fraction field of its coordinate ring, but the two are never compared, because the scheme does not exist.

targets.target: Comparison of scheme-valued F-points and their group law with the existing Weierstrass point group
targets.note: The Weierstrass point group with its group law is fully built in Mathlib (affine, projective and Jacobian, with equivalences between them), but there is no scheme-valued functor of points to compare it with.

targets.target: Comparison of function-field isogenies with scheme morphisms; degree, separability, kernels, pullbacks of divisors, invariant differentials
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a complete function-field isogeny theory — coordinate pullbacks, degree, separability, kernel, differential, Frobenius, [n], base change — which is the 'existing function-field isogenies' side of the comparison and which the layer already treats as given. Every target of this layer nevertheless needs the scheme, which does not exist, so the comparison itself, the treatment of the zero morphism as a scheme map and the identification of divisor pullbacks under it are all absent.

targets.target: K₀(X) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(X) for a connected regular noetherian curve (rank–determinant isomorphism)
targets.note: K₀ of a scheme (of vector bundles or coherent sheaves) is never defined, so the isomorphism has no statement for a projective curve. In the affine case both sides exist separately — Tau Ceti's K₀(proj R) as exact K₀ of finitely generated projectives over any ring, and Mathlib's Picard group CommRing.Pic (a group, ≅ ClassGroup for domains) — but no rank or determinant map K₀ → Pic, no Steinitz theorem and no K₀(R) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(R) for Dedekind domains exist. For schemes the Picard group is not a group: TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.LineBundleClass is only a commutative monoid.

targets.target: Class of a closed point, class of a line bundle, degree map, Euler characteristic, pushforward to the base
targets.note: The ingredients exist without K₀: Tau Ceti has the Euler characteristic Σ(−1)ⁱ dim Hⁱ(X, M) of a sheaf of modules on a scheme over a field, additive on short exact sequences (Scheme.Modules.eulerCharBelow), the degree of scheme Weil divisors relative to a morphism weighted by residue degrees (SchemeWeilDivisor.relativeDegree) and the function-field divisor degree; Mathlib pushes cycles forward along quasi-compact morphisms (AlgebraicCycle.map). None is a map out of a scheme's K₀, the degree of a line bundle is not defined, and no pushforward of K-classes to the base exists.

targets.target: Picard decomposition by degree on an elliptic curve with rational origin

targets.target: The essentially small exact category Proj_fg(A) built from the module category with projectivity and finiteness predicates
targets.note: Built exactly as the layer describes: the full subcategory of finitely generated projectives of ModuleCat R, with the exact structure induced from the abelian one, proved to be the split structure (short exact sequences with projective quotient split) and essentially small. Sorry-free. The roadmap document does not record this.

targets.target: Scalar extension along a unital ring homomorphism preserves finitely generated projectives and their split exact sequences, without a flatness hypothesis
targets.note: Mathlib proves base change preserves projectivity (Module.Projective.tensorProduct, for an algebra over a commutative ring) and finiteness (Module.Finite.base_change), and has extension of scalars ModuleCat.extendScalars only between commutative rings. Tau Ceti shows every additive functor is conflation-exact for split exact structures (ExactStructure.isConflationExact_split), which would make such a functor exact on Proj_fg. No functor Proj_fg(A) ⥤ Proj_fg(B) along an arbitrary unital ring map is constructed, and K(A) is not constructed functorially.

targets.target: Functorial K(A)
targets.note: No higher K-theory functor exists; only K₀ functoriality (TauCeti.ExactK0.map for conflation-exact functors).

targets.target: Comparison of ΩQ(Proj_fg(A)) with the direct-sum group completion of the maximal subgroupoid; π₀ = K₀(A); zero component ≅ BGL(A)⁺; the product description K₀(A) × BGL(A)⁺
targets.note: The purely algebraic shadow — split K₀ is the group completion of the additive monoid of isomorphism classes — is proved in Tau Ceti, Mathlib has the group completion of a commutative monoid, and Mathlib has the maximal subgroupoid of a category (CategoryTheory.Core). Nothing topological exists: there is no plus construction, no BGL(A), no group completion of a symmetric monoidal groupoid, no infinite-loop space and no stable general linear group.

targets.target: Cofinality: every finitely generated projective has a complement making the sum free
targets.note: Mathlib proves that a finitely generated projective module over any semiring is a retract of some Rⁿ: there are f : Rⁿ → M surjective and g : M → Rⁿ with f ∘ g = id (Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective), so M ⊕ ker f ≅ Rⁿ, and over a ring ker f = range(id − g ∘ f) is finitely generated and projective (LinearMap.ker_eq_range_of_comp_eq_id). The K-theoretic cofinality consequence belongs to the absent plus comparison.

targets.note: Only the degree-zero statement (an invariant additive on conflations descends to K₀) exists; there is no K-theory space for the additivity theorem to be about.

targets.target: Dévissage for a full abelian subcategory closed under subobjects and quotients with finite filtrations
targets.note: Only a degree-zero special case: for an Artinian ring R, Tau Ceti proves G₀(mod R) is free on the classes of the simple modules, with coordinates the Jordan–Hölder multiplicities (TauCeti.simpleClassBasis, jordanHolderCoordinate) — dévissage from finitely generated modules to semisimple ones in degree zero. Dévissage for a general abelian subcategory closed under subobjects and quotients, and in any positive degree, is absent.

targets.target: The resolution theorem for a full exact resolving subcategory, with the alternating-resolution inverse in degree zero and the comparison with the existing K₀ resolution theorem
targets.note: Only degree zero, and only the projective case. Within that case the alternating-resolution inverse (eulerClassOf, eulerHom) and the module instance K₀(proj R) ≅ K₀ of modules with finite projective resolutions (moduleResolutionEquiv) are proved. The resolution theorem for a general full exact resolving subcategory, in degree zero or on K_n, is absent.

targets.target: Quillen localisation for a Serre subcategory of a small abelian category and its quotient
targets.note: Mathlib has Serre classes in an abelian category and the localisation of the category at the corresponding morphisms, with the expected characterisations — the input to Quillen's localisation theorem. The localisation long exact sequence in K-theory does not exist, in any degree.

targets.target: Cofinality with the degree-zero correction (idempotent completion may change K₀)
targets.note: Mathlib has the Karoubi envelope and the decomposition P ⊞ P.complement ≅ X of an idempotent in a preadditive category (Karoubi.decomposition), the summand input to cofinality. Tau Ceti compares exact K₀ of two exact structures on the same category (ExactK0.ofLE_surjective), which is not cofinality. No K₀ of the idempotent completion and no cofinality theorem for a cofinal subcategory exist.

targets.note: Relative groups, localisation boundaries and transfers are all absent, so no compatibility can be stated.

targets.note: K₁ does not exist in either library.

targets.target: The cyclic quantum dilogarithm in a Kummer extension, and its change under a choice of n-th root

The only q-product is Mathlib's Euler function ∏(1 − x^{n+1}) = (x;x)_∞ (eulerFunction) with the pentagonal number theorem, which is not the cyclic dilogarithm.

targets.target: The resulting class in units modulo n-th powers, and the distinction between units, S-units, Kummer classes and their quotients
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the Kummer map Kˣ → H¹(G_K, μₙ), computes it on cocycles and proves its kernel is (Kˣ)ⁿ, so Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ injects into H¹; surjectivity (profinite Hilbert 90) is explicitly noted as missing in that file, so the Kummer isomorphism is not available. The S-unit bookkeeping is present: Mathlib defines the Selmer group K(S, n) of classes unramified outside S, and Tau Ceti proves the exact sequence 1 → O_S×/n → K(S, n) → Cl_S[n] → 1 (fromSUnitLift_injective, ker_toClassGroup, range_toClassGroup). targets.note: No five-term relation of any dilogarithm exists and there is no Bloch quotient to descend to.

targets.note: Both sides are absent.

targets.target: Ring K₀ defined through the existing split/exact K₀ universal property

targets.target: Object-class induction and equality of classes by stable isomorphism

Missing: the statement that [P] = [Q] exactly when P ⊕ Rⁿ ≅ Q ⊕ Rⁿ for some n, which would follow from the group-completion comparison and cofinality of free modules. Mathlib does name the one-sided case: `Module.IsStablyFree R M` says M ⊕ N is free for some finite free N, over any ring, with `IsStablyFree.of_free_prod` as its constructor and `IsStablyFree.equiv` for transport; this is the P ⊕ Rⁿ ≅ Rᵐ case (Q free), not the general [P] = [Q] ↔ P ⊕ Rⁿ ≅ Q ⊕ Rⁿ criterion the layer asks for.

targets.target: Geometric realisation of nerves and of the maps induced by functors

targets.target: Homotopy between realised maps induced by a natural transformation, and homotopy equivalence induced by an equivalence of categories
targets.note: Mathlib defines simplicial homotopies X (x) Delta[1] -> Y and turns them into combinatorial homotopies, but never builds one from a natural transformation (via N(C x [1]) = N C x Delta[1]) or deduces invariance of |N C| under equivalences of categories.

targets.target: Compatibility of classifying spaces with products and filtered diagrams of categories
targets.note: Only the simplicial part for limits is there: it follows from the adjunction hoFunctor -| nerveFunctor, and Mathlib proves the representable case explicitly (Delta[p] (x) Delta[q] = nerve of the product order). Missing are |N(C x D)| ~ |N C| x |N D| after realisation and the commutation of nerve and realisation with filtered colimits of categories. Mathlib has started the convenient category of X-generated spaces where the product statement would live, but its cartesian closed structure is still a TODO and nothing connects it to realisation.

targets.target: Contractibility of the classifying space of a category with an initial or terminal object
targets.note: No contractibility statement for nerves or their realisations exists in either library.

targets.target: Classifying space of a discrete group: the nerve of its one-object groupoid identified with the bar construction
targets.note: Mathlib builds EG = (G^(n+1))_n as a simplicial G-set (the Cech nerve of G -> pt) and the bar resolution/bar complex of group homology, but never forms BG, never takes the nerve of SingleObj G, and states no identification between them.

targets.target: The realisation of BG is a K(G,1), with the map on fundamental groups induced by a group homomorphism

Applying this to BG needs the realisation of the nerve of G and its universal cover, which is missing.
